articles.title: ‘We're not building something that puts the music in the background, we want to put it in the foreground’: Former Head of Innovation at Spotify on wanting to make music platforms interactive again, and whether they can survive without the reliance on AI
articles.text:
‘The next major music platform should give people something to do with the music’: Spotify’s former Head of Innovation on his plans to launch an interactive music service, and whether AI features will help or hinder streaming
Three years after leaving Spotify, Mauhan M. Zonoozy is ready to take his software label to the next level
The current state of music streaming is interesting, yet unpredictable. The shift from the CD era into the streaming era has made access to music more ubiquitous, but it’s also thrown up problems: some users aren’t interacting with music like they did before, and the explosive spread of AI is threatening the entire streaming model. Enter Mauhan M. Zonoozy, former Head of Innovation at Spotify, who has plans to tackle both these problems.
Zonoozy left Spotify in 2023, and since then has set up his own music software label, A Vinyl Bar in Shibuya, a record label-meets-production studio that releases playful music apps the way labels drop records, including jetset.fm and Stacks. Essentially, it’s creating digital music playgrounds.
While Shibuya’s products don’t have extensive libraries of music like typical streaming platforms, they offer users different ways to create new sounds, even if you only use them for a couple of minutes. But despite the label still being in its infancy, Zonoozy knows exactly where he wants to take it.
I chatted with Zonoozy about where his post-Spotify career is heading, and his ambitious plans to insert his music services into a streaming world in which AI is becoming a growing presence.
Music is participatory
In a short period of time, Mauhan and his “small team of creative technologists” have released a slew of casual, interactive music platforms across web and mobile — but this is only the beginning.
“I spent years at Spotify and I loved it,” Mauhan tells me. “Incredible company, incredible team. But I think I spent most of my time effectively thinking about what comes next. I started A Vinyl Bar in Shibuya around a simple belief that music is a verb, that the next major music platform should give people something to do with the music. It should be more participatory, more engaging”.
Streaming has certainly made music a lot more accessible, but there was always one thing missing for Mauhan: interaction. “With streaming, you can hear almost anything, anywhere instantly, but the dominant interaction is still effectively sorting through folders and pressing play,” he continues. “There's an entire generation that was growing up playing with music through different mediums and different devices. I think their relationship with everything felt a lot more interactive.”
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
This sparked a lightbulb moment for Mauhan, and his mission statement is simple: “to empower more people to express themselves with music, or feel self-expressive with music”. This is where his latest project, Bop, comes into play.
Bop is a pocket DJ app, currently in beta, that lets you mix, mash, and mess with music. Its interface is like an MPC workstation, allowing you to create remixes of popular songs by dragging and dropping effects and sounds onto its grid. “We're not all about replacing the creative process,” Mauhan adds. “We're more about building instruments and new ways to express yourself.”
When it comes to the best music streaming services, tools like this aren’t a new concept — Spotify has its own DJ-style mixing feature — but Mauhan believes there’s still more room for music services whose focus is user expression.
“I think there's a yearning for creative expression (in music platforms),” he says. “I think listening to music the way artists created and intended is absolutely a big part of it, but I also think having Legos that you play and interact with, engage with is also very important.
“The next step in our journey is packaging that up into something that is platform scale, and we can actually deploy it and build a larger community of users and fans around it.”
Next stop: a larger music platform
It’s clear that Zonoozy has had a blast developing Shibuya’s array of sonic playground tools, but what I want to know is if there’s a larger music platform on the horizon — and turns out, there is.
“I think there's a bigger platform at the end of the tunnel for sure,” he tells me. “A Vinyl Bar in Shibuya is working actively on building it. I don't think it's gonna look or feel like any streaming platform you've seen before.” Now I’m intrigued — how will this platform compete with the likes of the music streaming big dogs? Turns out Zonoozy has thought about that too.
“We believe it's going to be more participatory,” he shares. “We're not building something that puts the music in the background, we want to put it in the foreground”. And it's as simple as that. “The hints are in the products, and we want things that feel more playful and approachable. I don't think anyone's going to accuse us of building a DSP,” he adds.
Despite it still being in early stages of development, Zonoozy has a lot of faith in Shibuya’s bigger project; but music streaming tools are evolving rapidly as is tech in general, so he’s had to do a lot of thinking ahead.
“My personal belief was that a lot of the cues around where media is going were in the gaming space,” he continues. “And I think interactive media was always a little bit ahead of the rest of the world in terms of film and music. I think because it was closer to technology, it was exploring the more creative technological boundaries of what you could do with media.
“I think now with what's going on and how powerful these computers in our pockets are becoming, there's so much new, cool stuff you can do. It's a responsibility for all of us working in music and tech to figure out ways to do it that supports the industry, the community, and more than anything, the art form.” It occurs to me that Zonoozy is as interested in conserving as he is in innovating.
Will music streaming survive without AI?
It wouldn’t be a discussion about where the music-streaming industry is going without me bringing up AI, and Zonoozy sounds dismissive about AI at first, telling me: “You know what I like about AI? It's easy to spell”.
AI is having a big influence on music platforms in many ways, with algorithmic recommendations and tools such as AI playlist generators now pretty much part of the package. Because these features are right at users’ fingertips, I ask, will there come a time where listeners won’t be able to use services without the help of AI?
Zonoozy has hope, saying, “It's hard for me to imagine a world where people are building things completely void of touching some semblance of AI, but I do believe that there will be products that are not purely driven by generative media.” While he doesn’t necessarily favor the reliance on AI tools to enhance the UX, Zonoozy isn’t against AI altogether. If anything, he acknowledges its benefits, and how it’s helped provide the foundations to his services.
“It's enabling technology for us, it's just not the consumer proposition,” he adds. “Shibuya doesn't build LLMs or ask anyone to prompt music and wait for a finished song, but we do use it as a co-pilot for coding and development. I'd be naïve to say that there's no AI somewhere in the stack there. But on the music side, all the stems are all hand produced”.
He continues, “I'm not anti-AI. I think AI is an incredible, powerful future-facing infrastructure. I think it can build so many cool things and empower so many cool things. I’m a traditionally strong techno optimist in that sense, I think it will lead to incredible discoveries and advancements — it makes coding infinitely easier. But AI is not our product thesis on our side.”
When it comes to streaming services, there’s a huge focus on churning out tools designed to make the listening experience more personalized, more convenient, and more interactive. Given the pace of this evolution, I find it difficult to envisage where streaming culture is headed — Zonoozy shared my uncertainty.
“In terms of streaming specifically, I don't know what's going to happen,” he admits. “The extreme levels of personalization to custom content made for you — I don't know where that line ends. Is it being personalised, or is it being generated for you?”

articles.title: I spent hours relaxing in my Xreal xbx smart glasses on my honeymoon — they’re stylish, boast incredible image quality, and are my new favorite affordable wearable
articles.text:
Xreal has made the most stylish budget smart glasses I’ve seen — and they give my RayNeo Air 4 Pros a real run for their money
My new favorite affordable smart eyewear
Meta may dominate the smart glasses zeitgeist, but it's far from the only player — my favorite brand in the space is actually Xreal, with its range of impressive but pricey wearable-display specs. And with the launch of its new xbx brand, Xreal's lineup now includes more budget-friendly options too.
If money were no object, Xreal’s One Pro glasses are easily the crème de la crème of smart specs. Their Bose-tuned audio is impressive for such a small package, their electrochromic dimming tech is perfect for swapping between clear vision and shaded for optimal viewing conditions, and their unique optic engine displays their image more vividly than the competition, with fewer visible distortions.
The only issue is their price — $649 / £579 (they aren't available directly in Australia), absent any discounts, although they can be found on sale occasionally.
If you’re on a budget, my preferred pick has instead been RayNeo. Its Air 4 Pro specs debuted earlier this year, and not only are they affordable at just $299 / £289, they still come with solid specs, including HDR10 support.
With its new xbx a01+, however, Xreal might have just claimed the budget crown for itself.
Budget brilliance
Now the elephant in the room is that Xreal's specs cost a bit more. At their current $299 / £269 discounted price at Xreal.com they're on par with or cheaper than RayNeo's glasses; however their official price is $359 / £349, and while they aren’t discounted at the moment, we’ve regularly seen the RayNeo Air 4 Pros selling for $249 / £249 (RayNeo also doesn't seem to sell directly to Australia) or cheaper.
At the same time, the Xreal xbx a01+ glasses boast a handful of improvements which warrant a slightly higher price.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
For a start, their brightness tops out at 1,600 nits, while the RayNeo Air 4 Pro can only hit 1,200 nits. This extra brightness should allow you to get more out of the HDR10 support, offering more room for the light vs dark contrast and vivid colors to breathe across the video format’s visual range. Highs can look more high, helping lows look lower by comparison.
Aiding the image quality are the swappable lens covers.
While advertised as giving you the ability to choose which color of sunglasses cover you most want to complement your style, the xbx's box also includes a completely opaque black cover you can use with your specs. Because the specs are essentially virtual projectors, a darker environment ensures the highest-quality viewing conditions, though I found the regular sunglasses were fine even in bright sunlight.
The xbx glasses are lighter too, weighing just 62g compared to the RayNeo Air 4 Pro's 76g. Admittedly I haven't found them majorly more comfortable, but as I kicked back with them in a sun lounger while on vacation for hours on end I was relaxed enough to doze off on several occasions.
The only tradeoff is, I'd say, the audio, which doesn't seem to involve Bose tuning this time, and isn't quite as impactful as the Air 4 Pro's. That said, I'll almost always use earbuds or headphones with my display glasses, because they’re better in terms of quality and minimize sound leakage, so this downgrade didn't bother me.
Who wins? You decide
You'll also have to contend with Xreal's standard optic engine too. This is the prism that reflects the micro-OLED display into your eyes, and the standard design is susceptible to external reflections — most commonly light bouncing off the top of the specs and into your view. Pictures will also be a little smaller thanks to a reduced field of view, and can be a little blurrier at the frame edges.
Only Xreal's One Pros boast the improved design, but having experienced it, it's tough to go back to the standard optic engine.
To be fair, though, that’s mostly a me problem, and if you’re new to the display glasses world the Xreal xbx a01+ and RayNeo Air 4 Pros should be perfectly adequate performance-wise.
As for which of the budget specs you should go for — whichever is cheaper would be my suggestion.
The technical improvements of the xbx specs are solid, but if you can save $40/£40 or more on the RayNeos, their few deficiencies can be overlooked.
That said, if stylish, colorful designs are a must, alongside a marginally better image quality, then you'll be very pleased with the new Xreal xbx a01+ glasses.

articles.title: The ViWoods AiPaper Reader is a phone-sized ereader that transformed my relationship with books, but it couldn’t quite beat my doomscrolling habit
articles.text:
I spent 6 months with this pocket Android ereader — and it got me into books again, but didn’t break my smartphone addiction
An ever-present reading companion
I love reading — or at least that’s what I tell myself. In reality, I’ve always had a very on-and-off relationship with it, going from devouring books in days to barely opening one for weeks or months on end.
But one constant I’ve realized is that I don’t tend to prioritize reading — if there’s a show I’m binging, a new game I can’t stop thinking about, or simply lots of social engagements to attend, books will generally get put aside until I have more time on my hands.
But then something occurred to me — while I don’t always have long stretches of time that I’m happy to devote to reading, my days are full of short periods that aren’t being filled, like while I’m waiting in line or at a train station, or simply waiting for the kettle to boil. And then there are times when I’m on a train or in a cafe and might want to read, but don’t have a book with me as I travel light.
With all that in mind, back in late January, I bought the ViWoods AiPaper Reader — a pocket-sized Android ereader that’s small enough to carry with me everywhere alongside my phone — in the hopes that it would get me reading during periods that might otherwise be dedicated to podcasts or simply spent sitting or standing in slightly bored silence.
At the same time, I also had some hope that, since this ereader has full access to the Google Play Store, it might help cure my smartphone addiction — as doomscrolling was likely to be less desirable on an E Ink screen.
A tiny device that was a big reading success
Before buying the ViWoods AiPaper Reader, I hadn’t read much in a while — I had dozens of unread books on my Kindle Colorsoft and big stacks of physical books silently judging me. I might start one, but it wouldn’t stick — life would get in the way, or it wouldn’t immediately grab me enough to reach for it again.
But the ViWoods AiPaper Reader changed that. I loaded up the Kindle app on it and got in the habit of keeping it in my pocket, alongside my phone. Then, almost any time I would previously have switched on a podcast — such as when on a train or in small empty moments of my day — I’d reach for this instead.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
It didn’t matter whether I had two minutes or two hours; I’d aim to read something, and because the AiPaper Reader was always in my pocket, there was no excuse not to. I didn’t even have to go to my shelves to grab a book.
It allowed me to build a consistent reading habit and make progress with books even on days when I didn’t have much time, or wasn’t massively in the mood to read. After all, reading a couple of pages while boiling the kettle is still better than nothing, and it all adds up. And best of all, because this device got me back into reading, I’m now more inclined to read my paperbacks than I have been for some time.
Was it all smooth sailing? No, there have been some days and even a few weeks where I would stop carrying the ViWoods AiPaper Reader with me. But so far, I’ve always found it easier to go back to than a larger ereader or a physical book.
An imperfect light and unnecessary AI
This isn’t the perfect pocket-sized ereader. It has a front light but not a warm light, which can make reading at night a bit less comfortable than on some of the best ereaders — especially as the brightness is adjustable, the minimum level is still quite bright.
There’s also the AI-shaped elephant in the room, which even if you know nothing about this device, you’ve probably been wondering about from its name.
Like so much recent tech, the ViWoods AiPaper Reader is trying to cash in on the AI craze; there's a dedicated AI button that you can press to speak to an AI chatbot, with models from OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, and Qwen all built in.
These platforms can be used either as general-purpose AI chatbots or in combination with ViWoods' own apps to, for example, look up definitions of words in the books you’re reading. But personally, I’m tending to just use the Kindle app for reading, which can’t directly communicate with the AI.
Plus, using the ViWoods' AI functionality requires a Wi-Fi connection, which drains the battery faster than I want from an ereader, and it’s slower to interact with than just pulling up Gemini on my phone.
Beyond AI, some of the other software available on the ViWoods isn’t perfect, either, as while it runs a fairly recent version of Android in Android 16, there’s no promise of any version updates, and ViWoods’ own interface leaves a little to be desired. For example, there's little explanation of how some features work, and many important settings are hidden away in an ‘advanced settings’ submenu. There’s also an 11-step process to actually authorize and activate the Google Play Store on this device, despite it running Android.
Those gripes aside, I’ve generally been impressed by the ViWoods AiPaper Reader. Its 6.13-inch Carta 1300 screen is big and crisp enough to comfortably read on, its battery lasts me anywhere from a few days to a few weeks depending on how much I’m using it, and it looks like a genuinely premium device, with a slim, sleek design that’s almost up to the standards you’d expect from a premium brand like Apple.
This didn’t cure my addiction
While the ViWoods AiPaper Reader got me reading again, it was less successful at breaking my doomscrolling habit — though not a complete failure.
I figured that, since it runs Android apps, I could keep my phone in another room when I’m at home, and use the ereader for most things, with its monochrome E Ink screen sure to leave me reaching for it less.
And it somewhat worked for that — when I was disciplined about actually keeping my phone out of reach. But after a while, I got out of the habit, and even when I did keep my phone elsewhere, I’d sometimes encounter things I genuinely wanted it for, like penning a long message. So this wasn’t the perfect solution for me.
I’d perhaps have more luck if I fully replaced my phone with a device like this — and the ViWoods AiPaper Reader does have a SIM card slot, so it can fulfil most smartphone functions. But it lacks speakers and cameras, so you’d be making some unfortunate sacrifices.
Were I serious about that idea, I might invest in something like the Mudita Kompakt instead, as that’s designed specifically as a minimalist E Ink phone. So, if you’re looking primarily for something to break your smartphone habit, I’d suggest a device like that instead (or, perhaps, the similarly distraction-free Balance Phone).
Still, as a secondary function on a device I’m mostly using for books, the ViWoods AiPaper Reader has not been a total failure.
Now, if you’ll excuse me, I’ve got some reading to do.

articles.title: Hackers are going after our water now — over 30 Minnesota utilities hit in coordinated cyberattack by apparent Iranian attackers
articles.text:
Hackers are going after our water now — over 30 Minnesota utilities hit in coordinated cyberattack by apparent Iranian attackers
More than 30 Minnesota water utilities were hit in a coordinated attack
- Cyberattack hits operational technology at more than 30 Minnesota community water systems, briefly taking treatment plant offline and forcing several towns onto manual operations
- A leaked WaterISAC memo obtained by WIRED relays a state fusion center assessment tying the intrusions to Iranian-affiliated hackers, but no US agency has formally attributed the attack yet
- The CISA had warned four days earlier that Iranian-affiliated actors were compromising internet-facing PLCs, repeating guidance that has mostly fallen on deaf ears
More than 30 community water systems across Minnesota were hit by a coordinated cyberattack, targeting the operational technology running pumps, wells, water towers, and wastewater lift stations rather than the office networks behind them.
Minnesota IT Services disclosed the attack on July 28 2026 and activated a statewide incident response, stating that it wasn't aware of any Minnesota city asking residents to change their drinking water use just yet.
A memo obtained by Wired, circulated by the water sector information-sharing group WaterISAC and carrying a restricted TLP: AMBER handling marking, relays a Minnesota state fusion center assessment that ties the intrusions to Iranian-affiliated hackers.
A warning that was more or less ignored
Four days before the attacks, CISA updated an advisory, AA26-097A, warning that Iranian-affiliated actors were compromising internet-facing programmable logic controllers made by Rockwell Automation, Schneider Electric, Siemens, and possibly others across the US water, energy, and government sectors. It documented confirmed disruptions and financial losses.
This drew no immediate response from state functionaries, and it is easy to see why: the US has tens of thousands of community water systems that serve small populations and lack budgets for dedicated cybersecurity staff.
This is despite there being a precedent: Iranian-linked actors hit the Municipal Water Authority of Aliquippa in Pennsylvania in November 2023, defacing a Unitronics controller with an anti-Israel message. CISA said at the time those devices were exposed to the internet with default passwords still in place. The advice issued then is the same advice being issued this week, which is telling about how little has changed since.
The WaterISAC memo, dated the day the attacks concluded, passes on a state fusion center report linking the activity to Iranian-affiliated actors. That memo was not meant to be public, but it has been corroborated by The New York Times and The Washington Post, which reported that they spoke to federal officials and US intelligence agencies, respectively, lending credence to the claims.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
CISA later warned that attackers are changing PLC passwords to lock operators out of their own equipment, and repeated the advice that has been unchanged for years: get PLCs off the public internet and put remote access behind a VPN or gateway.
Who was affected?
The worst of the cyberattack hit Braham, a town of roughly 1,700 people, where the city said attackers shut down the operating controls, taking the water treatment plant and the well offline. Crews restored it manually within a couple of hours, and residents were told to minimize water use in the meantime.
Plymouth, a Minneapolis suburb of about 80,000, found the problem confined to equipment connected over cellular links at two water towers and several wastewater lift stations. Its IT division disconnected the affected kit from the network entirely to stop the attack and prevent retargeting during reconfiguration.
Maple Plain declared a local state of emergency to manage its response, and South St. Paul reported that some automated controls were compromised. In most cases, contingency procedures held and water and wastewater operations continued.
None of this is happening in a vacuum, however. The June memorandum that paused fighting between the US and Iran has broken down, and both are trading strikes, including recent US attacks near the Strait of Hormuz that destroyed a water facility and cut supply to more than 20,000 people. Whoever carried out the Minnesota attacks, the symbolism of targeting municipal water is unlikely to be accidental.
The damage that these intrusions caused was limited; they produced brief outages that trained staff fixed by hand. That is an outcome with a silver lining, and it depended on utilities having people who knew how to run a treatment plant without its automation, even if its digital defenses collapsed outright.

articles.title: Take this Bob's Burgers quiz that's so hard, even the Belcher family themselves would be doubting their own lives
articles.text:
The hardest Bob's Burgers quiz of all time is here — but can you handle the grill heat and score more than 80%?
Your as* is grass, and I'm gonna mow it
Fun fact: whenever I have days that I work remotely, I'll always have an episode of Bob's Burgers on in the background. In fact, I watch all 16 seasons of the hit Hulu and Disney+ animated comedy so often, that I could tell you exactly what episode was on without directly looking at it.
I felt incredibly prepared for the handful of Bob's Burgers quizzes already on the internet claiming to be the hardest, but nobody has yet been able to truly test the reams of random knowledge I've acquired from watching the series so often.
Should I be able to tell recite the lyrics to the song that plays over Tina and Tammy's first time collectively ditching class in season 2? Probably not.
So, behold — the genuinely most difficult Bob's Burgers quiz that I have played to date (because I made it). If you get more than 80%, I'll assume that you're actually a Wharf resident who's somehow found their way into the real world.
I have left out anything that happens in The Bob's Burgers Movie, but you'll need to have seen seasons 1-16 in order to answer all of the questions.
Check back when Bob's Burgers season 17 (hopefully) airs in early 2027... you know that the above will be updated accordingly.

articles.title: Juega gratis a ‘WWE 2K26’ y tres títulos más en Steam antes de que acabe la promoción
articles.text:
Steam ha iniciado una nueva campaña de fin de semana gratis, permitiendo que los usuarios prueben cuatro juegos completos sin costo alguno, pero solo hasta el 3 de agosto a las 13:00 ET.
PUBLICIDAD
Esta promoción, conocida como Free Weekend, representa una oportunidad perfecta para quienes buscan experimentar géneros muy distintos antes de decidir si invierten en algún título. Sin embargo, conviene no confundirse: el acceso es temporal y los juegos no se quedarán en tu biblioteca una vez finalizado el evento.
La dinámica de este tipo de promociones se ha consolidado como un gancho recurrente en la plataforma. Steam baja la barrera de entrada, multiplica la base de jugadores simultáneos, y aprovecha para ofrecer descuentos en los mismos títulos, incentivando la compra tras la prueba gratuita.
PUBLICIDAD
¿Qué juegos puedes probar este fin de semana?
En esta edición, el catálogo incluye propuestas para todos los gustos:
- WWE 2K26: El gran atractivo para los fans de la lucha libre y la simulación deportiva. Permite experimentar combates, modos de torneo y una amplia plantilla de luchadores licenciados.
- Reaper Actual: Shooter de mundo abierto que apuesta por la acción táctica y la exploración, aún en acceso anticipado y con una comunidad activa que aporta feedback al desarrollo.
- Necesse: Mezcla de supervivencia, sandbox y exploración. Ha recibido comentarios positivos por su jugabilidad y equilibrio entre desafío y creatividad.
- Tower Dominion: Alternativa ideal para los amantes de la estrategia y la defensa de torres, con mecánicas clásicas y opciones multijugador.
¿Cómo funciona la prueba gratuita?
El acceso temporal te permite descargar y jugar la versión completa de cualquiera de estos títulos sin pagar. Una vez que termine la promoción, el 3 de agosto a las 13:00 ET, el acceso se bloqueará y solo podrás seguir jugando si decides comprar el juego.
PUBLICIDAD
A diferencia de otras campañas (como las de Epic Games Store o algunos regalos puntuales de Steam), estos títulos no se quedan en tu cuenta para siempre tras la prueba.
Descuentos y precios durante el Free Weekend
Además del acceso gratuito, Steam ha rebajado el precio de los cuatro juegos. Por ejemplo, WWE 2K26 suele costar 59,99 dólares, Reaper Actual 19,99 dólares, Necesse 9,99 dólares y Tower Dominion 17,49 dólares. Durante la promoción, todos están disponibles con descuento, aunque el porcentaje varía según la región y puede estar sujeto a restricciones locales.
PUBLICIDAD
Lo más recomendable es consultar la tienda desde tu cuenta para ver el precio final. Esta estrategia busca que los jugadores, tras disfrutar de la experiencia completa, aprovechen la rebaja para adquirir el título que más les haya convencido.
¿Qué dicen los usuarios y la comunidad?
El caso de Reaper Actual es llamativo: aunque sigue en acceso anticipado y acumula reseñas mixtas, la interacción constante entre desarrolladores y comunidad está ayudando a pulir el juego. Necesse, en cambio, ha destacado por su estabilidad y ha recibido valoraciones muy favorables; muchos jugadores aseguran que la prueba gratuita les bastó para decidirse a comprarlo.
PUBLICIDAD
Este tipo de eventos permite a los estudios recibir feedback directo y a los usuarios tomar una decisión informada, sin riesgo económico inicial.
Consejos para aprovechar la promoción

articles.title: I swapped my regular coffee maker for the fun-size Ninja Luxe Café Mini, which brews tasty espresso and drip coffee in even the most bijou of kitchens
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Ninja Luxe Café Mini Espresso Machine gives you lots of flexibility to craft the coffee or espresso beverage of your choice. While it's pretty quick to get from whole bean to cup, there is definitely a learning curve and some inconsistency.
Pros
- +Brews both espresso and drip coffee
- +Fewer steps than traditional machines
- +Burr grinder, coffee scale, and milk frother are built in
- +Adaptive brewing automatically adjusts temperature and pressure
- +Fairly compact for a semi-automatic machine
Cons
- -Learning curve
- -Takes some manual dexterity and strength
- -Inconsistent results
- -No obvious way to clean inside grinder
Why you can trust TechRadar
Ninja Luxe Café Mini Espresso Machine: two-minute review
The Ninja Luxe Café Mini Espresso Machine is a compact version of the Ninja Luxe Café. It doesn't require an enormous amount of counter space, especially considering that this single machine grinds your whole beans directly into your filter, weighs your grinds, brews your espresso or drip coffee, and froths your milk. You won't need any other coffee accoutrements on your counter.
While I did brew some absolutely delicious coffee with the Ninja Luxe Café Mini, there is definitely a learning curve. In fact, I wouldn't say I have mastered the espresso settings yet, even after brewing many cups. Even with the identical espresso settings, sometimes I get just an ounce or so and sometimes I get a lot more. Drip coffee comes out consistently well; no issues there. I also had some trouble frothing the milk; with just a minimum amount of milk in the jug it overflowed onto the counter.
Note that even though this is a semi-auto machine, you do need to have some manual strength and dexterity to get the portafilter properly into place. Be ready for some trial and error. If you're prepared to take on a project, I think you'll be well-rewarded for your efforts.
Ninja Luxe Café Mini Espresso Machine: price and availability
- Widely available both in store and online
- Retails for $449.99 USD (£338.50 GBP, $643.73 AUD)
- Only sold in the black and chrome colorway
You can find the Ninja Luxe Café Mini Espresso Machine at many brick and mortar stores and websites, including Amazon, Best Buy, Kohl's, Target, and Ninja's own site. It retails for $449.99 USD (£338.50 GBP, $643.73 AUD) and comes in just the one color, black and chrome.
Ninja Luxe Café Mini Espresso Machine: specs
| Name | Ninja Luxe Café Mini Espresso Machine | 
| Type | Semi-automatic | 
| Dimensions (L x W x H) | 10.24 in L x 12.17 in W x 13.43 in H / 26.01 cm L x 30.91 cm W x 34.11 cm H | 
| Weight | 18.96 lbs / 8.6 kg | 
| Brew styles | Espresso (double), Triple (espresso), Classic (coffee), Rich (coffee), and Over Ice (coffee) | 
| Milk frother | Yes | 
| Connected device | No | 
Ninja Luxe Café Mini Espresso Machine: design
- Efficient design gives it a smaller footprint
- Aesthetically pleasing, goes with any decor
- Five brew styles
The Ninja Luxe Café Mini is efficiently designed to house everything you need to make just about any sort of coffee drink in a relatively small package. When you first unpack it, you will need to determine your water hardness with the enclosed test strip and set your machine accordingly. Run a flush cycle and then you're ready to start brewing.
The machine has a conical burr grinder, a brewing system that makes both espresso and coffee, and a steam wand. It comes with two filter baskets:, a smaller 'double' and a larger 'luxe' basket (unlike most espresso machines, there's no basket for pouring a single shot).
Place the basket into the portafilter, the funnel on top of that, and then slide it into the grinding cradle. Choose your brew style. The machine evaluates your beans and determines a recommended grind size. Turn the grind dial to meet the recommended number and hit the grind button.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Once your ground coffee is the basket, remove the portafilter and tamp down the grinds with the assisted tamper. It has a spring inside so you'll apply just the right amount of pressure.
Then you can remove the funnel, place the portafilter under the Ninja Luxe Café Mini's group head and turn it until it locks into place. This takes some manual strength and dexterity, and the machine's relatively light weight means you have to brace it in place so it doesn't slide around, though it does get easier with repeated use.
You can manually select your level of strength (represented by one, two, or three beans) and temperature or just use the default. When you're done brewing, dispose of the puck of used coffee grounds, and clean the dirty components.
There is also a milk jug and steam wand. To use it, turn the manual valve on the side from brewing mode to frothing mode. The owner's manual includes detailed instructions of how to get the most froth from your milk of choice.
You'll need to clean the tamper, funnel, basket, portafilter, steam wand and jug after each use. You'll also need to empty and clean out the drip tray every few brews, and every time you froth milk. Additionally, you'll need to descale the machine periodically. However, there is no obvious way to get in and clean the grinder. That part never gets wet, but coffee oils will build up there over time.
- Design score: 4.5/5
Ninja Luxe Café Mini Espresso Machine: performance
- There is definitely a learning curve
- You need manual strength and dexterity
- Brew amounts are not consistent
Become a TechRadar Insider by simply clicking 'Join Now' at the top of this page. Have a question? Please email membership@techradar.com
Overall, I think you'll find that the Ninja Luxe Café Mini will make you some great coffee and espresso drinks. There's definitely a learning curve, but if you have the patience you'll figure it out. Of bigger concern was that sometimes the brewing seemed to just stop short of a full yield, and I'm not sure why. The same beans brewed at the same setting just didn't always yield the same size espresso. This only happened to me while brewing espresso; all three of the drip coffee settings yielded perfect results every time.
There are five different brew settings: Espresso (which is actually a double espresso), Triple (espresso), Classic (drip coffee), Rich (a richer drip coffee), and Over Ice (drip coffee brewed at a lower temperature). I tested all five of them multiple times.
Espresso
The smallest drink you can make is a double espresso, there is no single espresso setting on this machine. The owner's manual says to throw away the first espresso you brew each time you put new beans into the hopper because it takes a couple of brews for the machine to dial in correctly. I tasted it anyway and yes, you should toss it. After that first one, the espresso tasted good though sometimes it would randomly give me a shorter brew. I did notice that I consistently got a beautiful crema.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Triple espresso
The experience of brewing the triple espresso is just like brewing the regular (double) one, only you use the Luxe basket instead of the smaller one. Again, the machine would sometimes give me a tiny brew. Pictured below is one of the smaller triples; other times it was much larger. Otherwise, the espresso was good and always had a lovely crema.
Classic
The Classic drip coffee setting yielded consistently good results. In addition to adjusting the grind size, brew temperature, and strength if you like, you can also choose to brew 6, 8, 10, or 12 ounces of coffee. The user experience of brewing the drip coffee is the same as brewing espresso, except that you skip the tamping step. The machine does something totally different on the inside. You get no crema. And when you go to throw the puck away, it's very wet, as opposed to the drier, crumbly puck you get with espresso.
Rich
The rich drip coffee setting works just like the classic, only it yields a richer brew. I find I prefer the classic, as I found it a bit smoother and less bitter, but your tastes may differ.
Over ice
The drip coffee over ice setting might have been my favorite. I found it very smooth and it didn't taste too diluted from the ice.
Steam wand
I found that it took some practice to get the milk frothing just right. I tried just leaving the jug in place and frothing it from there, and it works ok but doesn't produce much foam. I tried following the instructions about angle and movement in the owner's manual, and got too much foam.
The wand will purge itself right after frothing, and you'll want to wipe off the milk from the outside of the wand right away. Otherwise it sticks on there pretty good, requiring a bit of scrubbing to get it off.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
- Performance score: 3.5/5
Should you buy the Ninja Luxe Café Mini Espresso Machine?
| Ninja Luxe Café Mini Espresso Machine score card |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attribute | Notes | Score | 
|---|---|---|
| Value | While not cheap, it does replace five machines: conical burr grinder, coffee scale, espresso machine, coffee machine, and milk frother. | 4/5 | 
| Design | It looks great on the counter and has a relatively small footprint for all it does. | 4.5/5 | 
| Performance | There's definitely a learning curve and my results were not consistent, but the coffee drinks especially were quite tasty and the espresso crema was perfect every time. | 3.5/5 | 
Buy it if
You want to be the barista
You'll need to put the effort in, but you can be the barista at home with this machine. You control the settings and the results, with help from the machine's sensors.
You want all the coffee accoutrements in one smallish machine
Forget having a separate grinder, scale, brewer, and frother spread out over your countertop. Just one little machine does it all.
You can't decide between espresso and drip coffee
Now you don't even need two different machines for espresso and drip coffee. The Ninja Luxe Café Mini Espresso Machine does both, plus iced coffee and milk drinks too.
Don't buy it if
It's not in your budget
While you'll likely make fewer trips to the coffee shop, and you don't have to buy five separate machines, it's still not cheap.
You don't have great manual dexterity and/or strength
It takes some coordination and muscle to get the portafilter correctly installed in the group head for brewing.
You expect perfectly consistent results with the touch of a button
This machine isn't a fully automatic touch-of-a-button machine. It's not always consistent and there is a learning curve.
Ninja Luxe Café Mini Espresso Machine: also consider
De'Longhi La Specialista Touch
This one is a little bit more automated and beginner-friendly than the Ninja Luxe Café Mini Espresso Machine while still being pretty small and lightweight. It's also a bit more expensive.
Ninja AutoBarista Pro Fully Automatic Espresso Machine
While almost double the price of the Ninja Luxe Café Mini, it's worthwhile if you want a one-touch, super easy-to-use machine. It makes about a dozen different beverages including coffee, espresso, iced drinks, and milk drinks.
Read my Ninja AutoBarista Pro Fully Automatic Espresso Machine review
Terra Kaffe TK-02
This fully automatic coffee and espresso machine does it all with a touch of a button or even a voice command to Alexa. Custom design your own beverages. It's the priciest of the bunch, but an amazing machine.
Check out my Terra Kaffe TK-02 review.
How I tested the Ninja Luxe Café Mini Espresso Machine
I brewed and drank every drink on the menu: (double) Espresso, Triple (espresso), Classic (coffee), Rich (coffee), and (coffee) Over Ice more than once. I used two different kinds of beans for each beverage, first going all the way through the menu with a dark french roast and then again with a medium-dark roast. I frothed two different kinds of milk (almond and skim dairy) several times and added the milk to espresso shots. I cleaned all of the parts that touch the coffee after each use.
First reviewed July 2026

articles.title: Caída del bitcoin: Strategy evalúa vender miles de millones y la criptomoneda toca su nivel más bajo en semanas
articles.text:
El mercado de las criptomonedas experimentó una nueva sacudida después de que Strategy, el mayor inversor institucional en bitcoin a nivel mundial, anunció que evalúa vender hasta 5.000 millones de dólares en la principal criptomoneda para fortalecer su liquidez. Esta decisión llegó poco después de que la compañía reportara ingresos trimestrales por debajo de las expectativas, lo que desencadenó una reacción inmediata en los mercados digitales y tradicionales.
El viernes 31 de julio de 2026, el precio del bitcoin cayó 3,1% en 24 horas, situándose cerca de los 62.700 dólares, su valor más bajo en tres semanas. De acuerdo con Forbes, la noticia de la posible venta masiva por parte de Strategy, sumada a un informe de ganancias ligeramente inferior a las estimaciones de analistas, encendió la alarma entre los inversores y provocó una caída adicional del 7,3% en las acciones de la compañía, que ya acumula una pérdida del 42% en lo que va de año.
PUBLICIDAD
Por qué importa la decisión de Strategy
La empresa, antes conocida como MicroStrategy y liderada por Michael Saylor, se ha posicionado como el actor institucional más influyente en el ecosistema bitcoin. Con más de 843.000 bitcoins (valorados en más de 63.800 millones de dólares según datos recientes), Strategy ha apostado gran parte de su liquidez y reservas corporativas en el activo digital, superando ampliamente su posición de efectivo, que el mes pasado apenas llegaba a 1.400 millones de dólares.
Tras anunciar ingresos trimestrales de 122,4 millones de dólares, apenas por debajo de las previsiones (122,9 millones), el CEO Phong Le afirmó que la venta parcial del portafolio de bitcoin permitiría a la empresa fortalecer reservas de efectivo y, eventualmente, financiar recompras de acciones.
PUBLICIDAD
Aunque el monto de la venta podría ser menor o incluso mayor, el fundador Saylor defendió la decisión como parte de una estrategia de asignación disciplinada de capital y creación de valor a largo plazo, a pesar de la volatilidad inherente al mercado cripto.
La relación de Strategy con el bitcoin ha sido objeto de debate desde que la empresa, originalmente dedicada a la inteligencia empresarial, comenzó a transformar sus balances corporativos en criptomonedas. Saylor, cuyo patrimonio neto ronda los 3.200 millones de dólares, logró recuperar su fortuna tras los años de la burbuja puntocom gracias a la revalorización de bitcoin.
PUBLICIDAD
Sin embargo, la reciente caída del precio y la presión de analistas como JPMorgan, que piden aumentar las reservas de efectivo para restaurar la confianza de los accionistas, han puesto en jaque la sostenibilidad del modelo.
La empresa ya había realizado una venta parcial de bitcoin en junio, provocando en ese momento una breve pero significativa caída de la criptomoneda por debajo de los 60.000 dólares.
PUBLICIDAD
Bitcoin: volatilidad histórica y contexto global
El bitcoin, creado en 2008 bajo el pseudónimo Satoshi Nakamoto, nació con la promesa de desafiar a las instituciones financieras tradicionales y ofrecer una alternativa descentralizada. Su volatilidad, sin embargo, ha sido una constante a lo largo de su historia. Pese al escepticismo de organismos como el FMI y el Banco Mundial, la criptomoneda ha registrado máximos históricos en los últimos años, especialmente tras eventos políticos y avances en adopción institucional.
La victoria de Donald Trump en las elecciones estadounidenses de 2024, junto al anuncio de una posible reserva estratégica nacional de bitcoin, impulsó el activo a superar los 107.000 dólares por unidad. No obstante, factores como la competencia de nuevas tecnologías de inteligencia artificial y movimientos de grandes inversores han generado oscilaciones constantes.
PUBLICIDAD
Este viernes, bitcoin cotizaba en torno a los 62.900 dólares, con una caída de más de un 3% en el día. A pesar de la volatilidad, sigue ocupando el primer puesto en capitalización de mercado entre todas las monedas digitales.
El flujo de inversiones institucionales, la aparición de nuevas aplicaciones blockchain y la búsqueda de alternativas de inversión frente a la incertidumbre económica mundial han sostenido el interés por bitcoin. Sin embargo, la decisión de Strategy de considerar una venta multimillonaria añade incertidumbre a corto plazo y pone a prueba la confianza de los mercados en la resiliencia del ecosistema cripto.

articles.title: Sunscreen, beach towel... security camera? Smart home expert Chris Price builds the ultimate tech setup to protect your property while you're on vacation
articles.text:
Is your home safe this summer? Security tech expert Chris Price shows how to expand a single camera into a budget-friendly home defence setup for when you're away on vacation
Peace of mind on the beach
Planning a summer getaway but worried about leaving your house for a few weeks? While statistically you are more likely to suffer a break-in during the winter months when it’s much darker, summer also presents an ideal opportunity for burglars. Even if you're at home there are increased risks, especially if you leave your windows open to get some fresh air into the house during a heatwave.
Of course, there are basic steps you can take to reduce your risk such as asking a neighbor to take in your mail and packages, and making sure windows are closed when you go out. But technology can help big time too. What’s more, you don’t have to spend a fortune on all the gear. Whereas once you had to spend thousands on security cameras and PVRs (personal video recorders) that had to be professionally installed, now you can buy cameras and video doorbells for a fraction of the price that can be controlled easily via your smartphone.
Starting simple
The trick is to start simple. A good idea if you are going away for a long time is to have an indoor camera focused on the most vulnerable part of the house where a burglar is most likely to break in — such as a back door. I’ve got a Nest Cam IQ Indoor focused on my patio doors leading out to the garden. I like it because it can record when it hears sound (such as glass breaking) as well as motion.
However, there are other cheaper models available from companies such as Amazon-owned Blink and Ring as well as lesser-known, but popular, Chinese brands such as EZVIZ, Reolink and Aqara.
Focused on the front door I have a tiny Blink Mini 2K+ which also provides a chime for the Blink video doorbell so we can hear it ringing in the house. Usually, I switch the motion sensor off on the Blink Mini during the day because it’s triggered every time a family member opens the front door which can be a bit of a pain. However, when I go on holiday I switch the motion sensor on just in case.
One important consideration is how footage is stored — either locally on a MicroSD card or in the cloud. Personally, I prefer storing footage locally on an SD card, although the downside is that you will usually have to buy a card separately. The advantage of local storage is that not only is it generally more secure (there have been cases of servers being hacked and private security footage being leaked), it also often works out cheaper in the long term.
That’s because many home security companies will charge you a monthly subscription fee to store all your recorded footage and access advanced AI-driven features such as facial recognition and text descriptions of videos.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
While these features may be vaguely useful, especially if you have lots of people coming to the door, for the vast majority it’s probably not worth the monthly fee.
Let’s go outside
Obviously, no discussion of home security is complete without talking about outdoor cameras and video doorbells. Whether it’s summer or winter, these devices are invaluable when it comes to optimizing your home security set-up and helping to prevent burglary.
Choosing the type of outdoor camera you want is largely down to personal choice and the type of property you live in. Generally speaking, outdoor cameras should be mounted reasonably high on your property to give you a better view and to prevent theft.
Many offer a wide viewing angle of between 130 and 180 degrees, while some of the latest models, such as the latest IMOU AOV PT, are pan-and-tilt models that detect and track movement automatically.
Want a security camera to act as a deterrent to an opportunist burglar? Then it’s worth considering a device with a powerful built-in spotlight and loud siren. If there are two things that burglars hate more than anything else, they're excessive noise and light that draws attention to what they are up to. Reolink’s Solar Floodlight Cam covers both bases with twin spotlights either side of the camera and an integrated 110dB siren.
Going solar
Unlike indoor cameras, which usually plug into the mains, powering an outdoor camera is a little more challenging. Although some are designed to plug into the mains via a waterproof housing, most now rely on either disposable/rechargeable batteries and/or solar power. Indeed, solar-powered cameras, such as the Reolink Solar Floodlight Cam mentioned above, have become increasingly popular in the UK particularly as summers have got hotter and panels have become more efficient.
While many of the latest outdoor cameras comprise separate solar panels that need to be mounted separately and plugged into a USB-C socket on the camera, others such as the IMOU Cell 3C come with a solar panel built in. Chinese company Baseus even has an innovative solar-powered camera, the Baseus Security S2, that boasts an innovative rotating solar panel that moves as the sun moves in order to maximize power to the camera.
Deciding how to power your outdoor camera isn’t the only factor you need to consider either. You also need to think about the technology you are going to use to transmit video clips to your phone’s security camera app. While for indoor cameras this is usually WiFi, for outdoor devices getting a connection between the indoor router and outdoor camera can be more challenging — especially over distances of around 30m.
One option therefore, may be to buy a device that offers dual-connectivity, including Wi-Fi and cellular (usually 4G), such as the IMOU AOV PT or Eufy 4G LTE Cam S330.
Optimizing your setup
So you’ve got your outdoor camera. What next? Well, now begins the process of optimizing it for your security needs. Generally, most outdoor cameras are far too sensitive and record far more footage than you actually need to look at. As a result, you could find your entire time on holiday viewing footage of someone walking past your house, or a car whizzing by, instead of enjoying quality time away.
Not only is this highly annoying, it could really waste battery power — something that's both costly and time-consuming, especially if you have to climb up on a ladder to take the device down to recharge or change the batteries every couple of weeks.
Within the app, it’s therefore a good idea to set the motion detection zones so that the camera only records footage captured on your property and also reduce the sensitivity settings too so the camera isn’t recording too much footage. If you know you are going to be away for a set period of time then it’s probably a good idea to ensure the camera can detect motion 24/7, but when you are home you may want to use the menus so it only records at time of the day when you know family members or flat mates aren’t going to be entering or leaving the property (such as night time).
When it comes to video quality, most outdoor cameras now offer at least 1080p video quality. However, some such as the Baseus Security S2 and the Reolink Altas PT Ultra, offer stunning 4K picture quality. While this is great, especially if you want to zoom in on close ups of a potential suspect, most of the time it’s probably unnecessary. By reducing video quality you will be able to store more footage on the SD card/in the cloud and not consume as much power either.
For night-time monitoring, standard infra-red (IR) night vision provides clear monochrome visibility in total darkness while a colour night-vision option uses advanced low-light sensors or built-in LED spotlights to capture colour details after dark.
Video doorbells — it’s good to talk
Think someone may be intruding on your property while you’re not around? All security cameras that I’ve ever tested (probably over 50 now) feature two-way audio so you can, if you so wish, talk directly to the intruder to tell him or her to get off your land. And they can also talk back to you, of course, using the built-in microphone.
Some of the latest models even generate automated messages or use different voices so the person doesn’t actually know who they are talking to (for example the Aqara G100 indoor/outdoor security camera lets you turn your voice into that of a robot or clown.) It’s a feature that some women and teens in particular might find reassuring, especially if they don’t want a man to think they are at home by themselves — though I can’t help thinking of Kevin McCallister in the film Home Alone.
Essentially video doorbells take the technology one step further by enabling you to speak directly to people who press the button, even if you are sitting on beach sipping a strawberry daiquiri on your summer vacation (as with the G100, Aqara’s G410 Doorbell Camera Hub also allows you to disguise your voice). Invented by Ring’s founder Jamie Siminoff back in 2013, video doorbells have really taken off in the last few years with most home security manufacturers now producing models.
Usefully, not only do video doorbells enable you to talk to whoever comes to the door as if you were at home, they can also be set up to detect and record nearby movement just like standard outdoor security cameras. The only real difference is that, whereas outdoor security cameras often have a wide viewing angle and wide aspect ratio, video doorbells tend to offer a much squarer field of view — often 1:1 — so you can see whoever is at the door more clearly.
Advanced functionality
For those looking to replace their traditional doorbell, video doorbells are a great solution. With many models, it’s even possible to use existing doorbell wiring to power them, rather than having to rely on disposable or rechargeable batteries. Many come with separate plug-in chimes so you can hear the doorbell clearly inside the house with a choice of customizable ‘ringtones’, ranging from classical music to Christmas carols.
Become a TechRadar Insider by simply clicking 'Join Now' at the top of this page. Have a question? Please email membership@techradar.com
That’s not to say that video doorbells are the perfect security solution for everyone. They’re not. Often, I’ve found there is quite a lag when you are talking to someone and if you live on a busy street it can be difficult to hear what they are saying. To counter this, some models, including those from Ring, enable you to play automated responses to the visitor, a bit like an old-fashioned answerphone — for example, ‘please leave the parcel outside’ or ‘call back in an hour’s time’.
Another issue is that with subscription services such as Ring Pro you can spend up to $19.99 / £15.99 a month on premium features such as person, package and vehicle alerts, video descriptions and 180 day video playback. At least with a Blink video doorbell it’s possible to store clips on the Blink Sync Module 2 hub using a separate USB drive while the TP Link Tapo D235 is one of the few doorbells with integrated MicroSD storage (it also offers free AI smart detection to distinguish between vehicles, pets and people).
Complete security solutions
Looking for a more advanced security solution for when you go away over the summer? Most manufacturers will allow you to view several cameras via their app. However, if you want to put different types of security devices together — such as locks, lights and a burglar alarm — then you will need a more advanced setup.
For example, one advantage of the Aqara G410 video doorbell is that it’s actually a fully-fledged smart home hub with a built-in Matter bridge and Thread border router that can be used as part of a smart home ecosystem such as Apple HomeKit, Google Home, Amazon Alexa and Smart Things.
Owned by Amazon, Ring products including cameras, video doorbells and burglar alarms can easily be controlled using Alexa routines with footage viewable via Echo Show devices. Furthermore, Ring Alarm also supports certified third-party products via the encrypted Z-Wave network, including smart locks from Yale, Schlage and Kwikset. This means you can lock/unlock doors, manage guest PIN codes and trigger automated security routines (such as arming the alarm when the door is locked) all inside the Ring app.
Securing your home for summer
With the summer holiday season well and truly upon us, and houses left empty as we down tools for a well needed break, now is the time to think about securing your home. While traditional precautions — such as securing windows, clearing letterboxes and locking away garden tools (including ladders) — remain essential precautions, modern technology can help too.
Protecting your home against burglary needn’t cost the earth either. You can now buy indoor cameras focused on vulnerable parts of the house for less than $70 / £50 while most outdoor cameras and video doorbells cost between $120 / £100 and $250 / £200. And while subscription charges do push up prices, often these aren’t necessary — especially if you can store footage locally on an SD card or USB drive.
Ultimately, combining the latest tech solutions with solid physical security will give you the peace of mind needed for you to truly unwind, ensuring your home remains a well-guarded fortress while you enjoy your break.

articles.title: El youtuber Hank Green admite que usar IA le genera dopamina y eso “no es sano para el mundo”
articles.text:
Hank Green, referente de la divulgación científica en YouTube, reconoció haber dependido “en exceso” de la inteligencia artificial para la elaboración de su contenido en YouTube.
Las declaraciones de Green, quien lidera canales como SciShow, Crash Course y Vlogbrothers, generaron una oleada de reacciones en sus seguidores y abrieron un debate sobre la transparencia y la ética en la creación de videos educativos en línea.
PUBLICIDAD
El episodio se desató tras la confesión de Green en una publicación de Reddit, donde admitió que el uso intensivo de ChatGPT como herramienta de investigación lo llevó a perder contacto con su propio proceso creativo y con la comunidad que lo acompaña desde hace años.
El youtuber, cuya trayectoria abarca más de dos décadas junto a su hermano John Green, anticipó una reducción en la frecuencia de publicaciones y pausas en proyectos como los juegos en línea SMUSH y 4x3.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo era el uso de IA en el canal de cienca en YouTube
Todo comenzó con una publicación en X, en la que Green reveló haber recurrido a ChatGPT para documentar un guion de video. El reconocimiento, lejos de pasar inadvertido, generó desconcierto entre los usuarios, muchos de los cuales lo acusaron de “socavar su credibilidad” al no informar previamente sobre el uso de IA en sus contenidos.
La controversia escaló cuando, en uno de sus videos, Green utilizó la frase “Agradezco la crítica”, una construcción frecuente en las respuestas generadas por modelos de lenguaje. Este detalle avivó las sospechas sobre la intervención de la IA en el guion y llevó a que el propio Green borrara el tuit original, trasladando la discusión a Reddit. Allí, el creador se declaró “mortificado” por haber “defraudado a tanta gente”.
PUBLICIDAD
El debate no tardó en dividir a los seguidores. Mientras algunos expresaron comprensión y apoyo, otros calificaron el episodio como “repugnante” y advirtieron que podría “hacer retroceder la comunicación científica años”.
Al interior de la comunidad, voces destacadas señalaron que la audiencia cultivada durante dos décadas por los hermanos Green difícilmente aceptaría la mediación de la IA en sus contenidos.
PUBLICIDAD
Las explicaciones de Hank Green y los riesgos de lo que hizo
Hank Green reconoció que la presión por mantener un ritmo elevado de producción lo llevó a apoyarse cada vez más en los chatbots. Admitió que el uso de la IA, si bien facilita el acceso rápido a artículos académicos y recursos, le restó libertad para explorar los temas y desarrollar enfoques propios.
“He dependido demasiado de la IA como ayuda de investigación. Puede ser muy útil para esta tarea, pero creo que ha sido en detrimento de mi trabajo porque no me ha dado la libertad de encontrar mis propios caminos hacia y alrededor de un tema”, explicó.
PUBLICIDAD
Green fue enfático al señalar que el problema no es solo técnico, sino también personal y ético. Confesó que las interacciones constantes con modelos de lenguaje le generaban dosis frecuentes de dopamina, una dinámica que sus allegados consideraron insana.
“Necesito aceptar que el nivel de dopamina que obtengo al interactuar con los LLM… haciendo más y más… no es sano para mí ni para el mundo. Es descuidado y me ha desconectado de donde está la gente en este tema”, escribió.
PUBLICIDAD
La preocupación de Green fue compartida por su entorno más cercano. Tanto su esposa Katherine como su hermano John le expresaron, sin rodeos, que su uso de IA no era saludable. Este señalamiento, sumado al rechazo de parte de la audiencia, lo llevó a replantear su relación con la tecnología y a priorizar la autenticidad en su trabajo futuro.
Como respuesta inmediata, Green anunció la reducción de la frecuencia de videos en su canal personal y la pausa temporal de los juegos SMUSH y 4x3. En su mensaje de disculpa, dejó entrever que Hankschannel podría regresar en el futuro, aunque con menos videos o con mayor apoyo en la escritura e investigación, pero siempre con mayor transparencia sobre el origen de los contenidos.
PUBLICIDAD
El youtuber manifestó su intención de ajustar el enfoque de sus videos, privilegiando producciones más meditadas y “sentidas” por encima de la cantidad. Incluso anticipó que podría realizar más videos espontáneos, sin guion, en los que prime la reflexión personal.
En este contexto, Green se comprometió públicamente a garantizar que sus palabras sean propias y que el proceso de creación sea claro para la audiencia. “He ido tan rápido que mi propio proceso no está claro para mí y quiero que eso sea una garantía de ahora en adelante”, aseguró.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: A crewless British boat just proved it can send drones into dangerous waters
articles.text:
UK tests robot boat that can fly its own wired drone even in 14ft waves and stay at sea for weeks
Royal Navy tests futuristic unmanned vessel
- Robot boat launches drone without crew during challenging ocean demonstrations
- Pioneer vessel survives rough seas while supporting airborne surveillance operations
- Tethered SkyRanger drone provides continuous monitoring from unmanned ships
A robotic boat has launched and recovered its own drone off the deck, without a single crew member aboard either vehicle.
British firm ACUA Ocean and American sensor maker Teledyne FLIR Defense completed the demonstration for the UK Ministry of Defence.
The trial paired an uncrewed surface vessel named Pioneer with a small tethered drone known as the SkyRanger R70 aircraft.
Rough-water stability makes flight operations possible
The entire demonstration depended heavily on the Pioneer's ability to hold steady in genuinely rough conditions each time at sea.
In January 2026, ACUA Ocean said the vessel held steady in waves reaching 4.25 meters, or roughly 13.9 feet high.
The company reported a 60% cut in roll motion compared with traditional single-hull monohull vessels used across the industry.
That stability functions as the mechanical foundation allowing a tethered drone to fly safely off a small robotic vessel at all.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
A violently rocking platform would make sustained flight operations for the SkyRanger R70 nearly impossible under open ocean conditions overall.
ACUA Ocean said Pioneer has already completed prior Royal Navy contracts covering surveillance, reconnaissance and anti-submarine warfare tasks before this trial.
Tethered drone extends persistent ocean surveillance
The system pairs a tethered uncrewed aerial system, or T-UAS, with an uncrewed surface vessel known as a robotic boat.
Teledyne FLIR's SkyCarrier is a ruggedized launch platform housed in a container that unfolds into an articulating landing pad system.
During the trial, SkyCarrier successfully launched a SkyRanger R70 drone autonomously from the deck of the moving Pioneer vessel itself.
Once airborne, the SkyRanger R70 stayed connected to Pioneer through a power and data tether, avoiding any need to land and recharge.
"Integrating the SkyRanger R70 with the Pioneer creates something genuinely new: a persistent, deployable capability," said Neil Tinmouth, chief executive of ACUA Ocean.
Richard Cunha of Teledyne FLIR Defense also said pairing the drone with Pioneer opens up an entirely new class of missions.
The SkyRanger R70 runs multiple embedded NVIDIA processors that perform real-time object detection and classification without ground input.
The combined sensor package delivers Group 2 level ISR performance while flying on a much smaller Group 1 airframe type.
UKDI, the Ministry of Defence's early-stage funding arm, backed the demonstration well before it reached any full-scale procurement decision process.
"Securing UKDI funding for this demonstrator is a significant milestone for ACUA Ocean and UK maritime autonomy broadly," Tinmouth said.
This technology will support the Royal Navy priorities including anti-submarine warfare, mine countermeasures and undersea infrastructure protection efforts overall.
That said, a successful demonstration under UKDI funding does not guarantee the system will reach large-scale deployment across naval operations soon either.
Cost, reliability at sea over long periods, and integration with existing fleets remain open questions that testing alone cannot resolve.

articles.title: 5 trucos para cuidar tu Air fryer: evita accidentes y malos olores en casa
articles.text:
Mantener la freidora de aire o Air fryer en óptimas condiciones prolonga su vida útil y reduce el riesgo de accidentes domésticos y la aparición de olores desagradables en la cocina.
Cada vez más hogares incorporan este electrodoméstico por su practicidad y la posibilidad de cocinar con menos aceite, pero el desconocimiento sobre su mantenimiento puede afectar tanto sus resultados como la seguridad.
PUBLICIDAD
De acuerdo con Mouvair, muchos usuarios piensan que al estrenar una Air fryer pueden prescindir de cuidados especiales. Esta percepción es errónea, porque la falta de limpieza y el uso inadecuado de utensilios pueden provocar desperfectos y hasta obligar a reemplazar el electrodoméstico antes de tiempo.
Por qué es clave lavar la Air fryer después de cada uso
Uno de los consejos más claves entregados por los fabricantes delectrodomésticos es la limpieza inmediata tras cada sesión de cocción. Aunque lavar platos no resulte atractivo para la mayoría, limpiar la freidora de aire tras cada uso evita la acumulación de residuos que generan olores y sabores no deseados.
PUBLICIDAD
Los fabricantes explican que, si se omite este paso, se corre el riesgo de que la suciedad se incruste en el cesto y en otras partes del electrodoméstico.
Además, los restos de comida pueden mezclarse con los alimentos en futuras preparaciones, lo que afecta la experiencia culinaria y favorece la proliferación de bacterias.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué utensilios conviene utilizar para no dañar la freidora de aire
El uso de utensilios apropiados es otro aspecto crucial para el cuidado de la Air fryer. Según Mouvair, se debe evitar el uso de objetos metálicos o esponjas abrasivas, porque pueden rayar el recubrimiento de la cesta y facilitar que los alimentos se peguen.
Se sugiere optar por herramientas fabricadas en madera, silicona o materiales similares. Este tipo de utensilios permiten manipular los alimentos sin poner en riesgo la integridad del revestimiento antiadherente.
PUBLICIDAD
Al preservar la superficie interna de la freidora, se facilita la limpieza y se evitan contaminaciones cruzadas, sumado a extender la vida útil del electrodoméstico.
Por qué llenar la cesta al máximo perjudica la cocción
Otra práctica común que puede comprometer el funcionamiento de la freidora de aire es sobrecargar la cesta. Los fabricantes advierten que muchas personas buscan optimizar el tiempo preparando grandes cantidades en una sola tanda, pero esto impide que el aire circule adecuadamente.
PUBLICIDAD
La consecuencia directa es una cocción desigual: algunos alimentos quedarán crudos y otros muy secos, y el exceso de ingredientes puede forzar el ventilador, lo que acelera el desgaste del aparato.
Por esta razón, preparar porciones moderadas garantiza que el aire caliente llegue a todos los alimentos, obteniendo resultados homogéneos y evitando reparaciones prematuras.
Cómo almacenar la Air fryer cuando no se usará durante un tiempo
Guardar la Air fryer correctamente incide en su conservación. Se sugiere que, si el electrodoméstico no se va a utilizar durante un periodo prolongado, se debe colocar en su embalaje original y almacenarla en un espacio fresco y seco.
PUBLICIDAD
Esta medida protege el aparato de la humedad, el polvo y los posibles daños en el enchufe o las conexiones eléctricas, sumado a que previene la acumulación de suciedad cuando no está en uso y facilita que, al volver a utilizarla, el aparato se encuentre en condiciones óptimas de funcionamiento.
Qué moldes y accesorios convienen usar para evitar daños y malos olores
El tipo de moldes y accesorios utilizados influye en el mantenimiento de la freidora de aire. Se sugiere usar recipientes aptos para altas temperaturas, como los de pyrex o materiales similares, sobre todo para preparaciones como galletas, queques o lasañas.
PUBLICIDAD
En caso de no disponer de un molde adecuado, se puede cubrir el cesto con papel aluminio. Esta prevención impide que los alimentos se adhieran al recubrimiento y evita que se produzcan daños durante el desmolde.
Asimismo, contribuye a mantener el interior libre de restos y olores persistentes, favoreciendo una experiencia culinaria más agradable y segura.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Cómo activar de nuevo 3G en el celular y por qué sirve en ciertas zonas y eventos de entretenimiento
articles.text:
Cuando la conectividad móvil falla en conciertos, estadios, festivales o zonas rurales, la capacidad de activar manualmente la red 3G en el celular puede marcar la diferencia entre estar completamente incomunicado o poder enviar mensajes y realizar llamadas esenciales.
Las redes 4G y 5G, aunque rápidas y modernas, tienden a colapsar en lugares con alta concentración de usuarios, provocando que incluso tareas básicas como enviar un texto o abrir una app tarden minutos o nunca lleguen a completarse. En este contexto, regresar a la tecnología 3G (frecuentemente identificada en la pantalla del móvil con las letras H o H+) se convierte en una estrategia de contingencia muy efectiva.
PUBLICIDAD
¿Por qué importa hoy activar 3G?
La saturación de las redes móviles es un fenómeno habitual en grandes eventos y zonas alejadas de los centros urbanos. La demanda masiva puede sobrecargar las antenas 4G y 5G, mientras que la infraestructura 3G, menos utilizada, permanece funcional y disponible. Cambiar manualmente a 3G permite al usuario acceder a canales menos congestionados, aumentando la probabilidad de mantener la comunicación en momentos críticos.
En situaciones donde la cobertura moderna desaparece o se vuelve inestable, la opción de alternar a 3G garantiza un nivel básico de conectividad para llamadas, mensajes y uso de aplicaciones esenciales —algo especialmente valioso para quienes dependen del móvil en desplazamientos o emergencias.
PUBLICIDAD
¿Qué significa la letra H en la cobertura móvil?
Cuando el indicador de la señal muestra una H o H+, el dispositivo está usando tecnologías HSPA o HSPA+, evoluciones de la red 3G convencional. HSPA (High-Speed Packet Access) permite velocidades de descarga de hasta 7,2 Mbps, superando ampliamente a la 3G tradicional, que rara vez excede los 2 Mbps. H+ (HSPA+ o 3,5G) puede alcanzar hasta 21 Mbps, acercándose al rendimiento de una red 4G básica.
Estos indicadores no solo señalan que el usuario está en una red más antigua, también informan sobre la calidad y la velocidad de la conexión disponible. En la práctica, navegar, utilizar redes sociales o enviar mensajes resulta posible con H o H+, aunque los contenidos que requieren mucho ancho de banda (como videos en alta definición o videollamadas) pueden experimentar cortes o baja calidad.
PUBLICIDAD
Dónde y cuándo sirve activar el 3G
El cambio a 3G es especialmente útil en:
- Recintos masivos (estadios, conciertos, festivales) donde la red 4G/5G colapsa.
- Zonas rurales o alejadas donde las nuevas tecnologías aún no han llegado.
- Viajes internacionales, sobre todo en países que mantienen infraestructura 3G activa y donde el roaming 4G resulta costoso o inestable.
- Situaciones de emergencia en las que cualquier conexión es mejor que ninguna.
Cómo activar 3G en el celular
El procedimiento puede variar según el sistema operativo, pero en la mayoría de los dispositivos consiste en:
En Android:
- Abre el menú de Ajustes.
- Ve a Conexiones > Redes móviles > Tipo de red preferida.
- Selecciona “Solo 3G” o “3G/2G automático”.
En iPhone:
- Ingresa en Configuración > Datos móviles > Opciones.
- Elige “Voz y datos” y selecciona 3G.
Al forzar el uso de 3G, el teléfono dejará de intentar conectarse a redes 4G/5G, liberando así canales de comunicación menos saturados.
Diferencias entre H y H+
Mientras la H indica velocidad de descarga superior a la 3G básica, la H+ representa un avance que facilita el uso de apps de mensajería, llamadas de voz y hasta videollamadas en calidad media. La transición entre ambas depende de la saturación, la distancia a la antena y las especificaciones técnicas del dispositivo.
PUBLICIDAD
Consejos prácticos cuando solo hay señal H o H+
- Cambia de ubicación y acércate a ventanas o espacios abiertos para mejorar la señal.
- Reinicia el dispositivo si la conexión no mejora.
- Consulta con el operador para verificar el estado de la red en la zona.
- Aprovecha la conectividad para tareas básicas y evita consumir ancho de banda con videos en HD.
Aunque 3G y HSPA sean tecnologías consideradas antiguas, su presencia permite que millones de usuarios sigan conectados en circunstancias adversas. Saber cómo activarlas y cuándo usarlas añade un recurso práctico para quienes dependen del móvil en todo momento, recordando que, en conectividad, lo simple y probado puede salvar el día cuando lo más moderno falla.
PUBLICIDAD
