articles.title: 'Nozzlegate' erupts as Prusa CORE One 3D printer kits arrive with soft steel nozzles — Bondtech admits machining flaws with no quick fix (Updated)
articles.text:
'Nozzlegate' erupts as Prusa CORE One 3D printer kits arrive with soft steel nozzles — Bondtech admits machining flaws with no quick fix (Updated)
Founders Edition buyer launches “Nozzle Gate” website in response
Update 8/2/2026: This article has been updated with the official statement made by Prusa on r/prusa3D.
Bondtech, the inventor of the INDX toolchanger system used to create the highly anticipated Prusa CORE One+ INDX, admitted to a significant mistake. The nozzles, which are nitrocarburized steel, do not meet industry standards for “hardened steel” as advertised.
Prusa Research has pumped the brakes on the INDX project, and has delayed shipping INDX conversion kits until mid-August. They issued a statement on Reddit:
“Bondtech has recently confirmed that the nozzles currently supplied with the INDX system are surface-hardened rather than fully hardened as originally planned, and has not yet finalized the compensation plan for affected customers. We believe it is better to wait until both we and you have clearer information, rather than ship the kits while this important question remains unresolved.”
The statement was also emailed directly to everyone with an active INDX order in the system. The company said this delay will also give customers a chance to cancel their orders if they wish. As an olive branch, Prusa Research INDX conversion kits will included extra hardware free of charge. The statement didn’t say what the gift would be, but that specifics would be shared before shipping.
Prusa engineers immediately began testing the INDX nozzles and determined that little wear could be seen after running five kilograms of carbon fiber PETG through the nozzles. However, after just 100g of super-abrasive Ultraglow filament, the protective coating began to fail.
Nitrocarburized steel is tougher than the standard brass nozzles that come with a stock Prusa CORE One+, but not as durable as hardened steel. The real problem is not that they went with a lesser nozzle, but that they kept the “hardened steel” wording in promotional materials. If Bondtech said from the beginning (or before customers locked in their pre-orders) that the INDX shipped with ordinary steel nozzles, no one would have blinked.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Information on the nozzle quality began to surface after a Reddit user posted a support email from Bondtech founder, Martin Bondeus. The email stated that “during production, we encountered manufacturing challenges that prevented us from machining that material reliably – the cutting tools simply did not withstand the process. Rather than releasing a product with inconsistent quality, we decided to supply the nitrocarburized version for the time being.”
These nozzles are not of poor quality, but they fall short of the standards set for hardened steel. According to a statement by Bondtech, the Founders Edition shipped with nitrocarburized steel, which is steel treated to obtain a hard shell. They’ve batch tested the nozzles and found them to be around 30-32 on the Hardness Rockwell C scale (HRC). For comparison, true hardened steel lands at 55-60 while an everyday brass nozzle comes in under 10 HRC.
For most users, and most materials, these mid-tier steel nozzles work exceptionally well and will last for an extremely long time. But once you start to feed your INDX abrasive filaments like glass-fiber, carbon-fiber, glow in the dark and metal filled filaments, things get dicey. The treated steel nozzles will last longer than brass, but Bondtech said they will experience “accelerated wear” when printing abrasives.
Bondtech has stated on its website that a “concrete solution” to the problem is not ready and that manufacturing truly hardened INDX nozzles could take months. They are also not offering any form of compensation before knowing the cost of the replacements. They are requesting that customers hold off on returning the kits and simply enjoy using non-abrasive materials until a solution is found.
The INDX takes a bespoke induction heated nozzle that has no off the shelf replacement at this time.
The news has hit the Founders Edition buyers quite hard, as many have already found difficulty with the kits they so eagerly purchased months ago. Some assembly problems can be expected with such a product, as they are being mounted on CORE One printers already in service. The INDX is a separate upgrade kit, and it requires stripping down a CORE One, removing the Nextruder and replacing it with the INDX carriage, then mounting a rack to hold the eight tool heads.
One “founder” was so upset he vibe coded an entire website in protest: Nozzlegate.com. The website outlines what the perceived problems are with Bondtech, and what consumers can do about it. We contacted the website owner, who asked to go by his handle “Daddie0.”
He told me that, like others who purchased Founder Edition kits, he’s disappointed in the quality of the product. He said his INDX was suffering from multiple mid-print crashes and layer shifts, and after two weeks of troubleshooting, it was finally fixed with a firmware update from Prusa. “Then nozzlegate hits. My EU right-given two-week return window ends a day after the news breaks.”
Realizing that his window for a standard, hassle-free return had closed on a machine he felt was a lemon, he shifted strategies. He began digging into Bondtech’s official documentation to see what recourse he had for a defective product.
What he found sparked a new battle. Disagreeing with Bondtech’s listed 90-day warranty policy, which he claims misleads consumers by failing to mention Sweden's mandatory multi-year consumer protections, he channeled his frustration into the NozzleGate website.
The INDX kit is a collaboration between Prusa Research and Bondtech, with the first wave of Founders Edition kits a limited edition run going to early adopters.
Tom’s Hardware received a Founders Edition INDX kit, which we installed on a Prusa CORE One we previously reviewed. Though the build took over the kitchen table for an entire weekend, our resulting INDX is printing non-abrasive filaments with excellent quality.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Denise Bertacchi is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware US, covering 3D printing. Denise has been crafting with PCs since she discovered Print Shop had clip art on her Apple IIe. She loves reviewing 3D printers because she can mix all her passions: printing, photography, and writing.

articles.title: Is bulldozing homes, seizing land, harming the climate, and replacing workers really worth everyone having an AI agent?
articles.text:
Is bulldozing homes, seizing land, harming the climate, and replacing workers really worth everyone having an AI agent?
AI agents will soon handle your work, and your personal life
There are a lot of sacrifices being made to usher in the latest technological age. Jobs, businesses, even whole industries are at risk of disappearing.
Now we can add homes to the list - as new electricity infrastructure for data centers in the state of Georgia means 30 homes are to be bulldozed and 330 parcels of land seized.
The good news is that the additional power will allow for extra data center capacity. And those same people who lost their houses can look forward to having their own personal AI agent to help to find a new place to live.
Losing homes for AI
In case you missed it, Mark Zuckerberg has announced yet another five year plan for AI, saying that billions of people will soon have their own personal AI agents - something that will require a data center buildout far beyond anything we’ve currently seen.
These agents will be “working on your behalf 24/7 to achieve your goals in whatever the domain is that you care about,” Zuckerberg said. They’ll basically do everything you already do, manage your relationships, sort your finances, even manage your household tasks.
So when AI frees everyone from the burdens of being human, what are we left to contend with? We get to channel the world's resources, climate, homes, and personal information and in return, AI can live your life for you. You’ll have so much free time to do… something else? Maybe listen to the tuneful hum of the local data center?
The promises of AI seem to add up to human replacement. The main reason businesses are chewing at the bit to adopt AI technology is because it promises to cut one of their main expenses: labor. The levels of productivity will stay the same, or maybe even improve, but profits will skyrocket thanks to significantly reduced operating costs.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
There will be new jobs in new never-before-thought-of sectors, or so we are told. But is this just a way to placate those losing their jobs to AI technology?
At present, AI is cutting through the entry level positions and administrative work that used to be a good way into a new industry. AI is therefore replacing existing workers, while simultaneously shutting them out from moving to other industries. Lets not forget that many workplaces are implementing AI interviewers that suck what was left of human interaction (much of which is a facade) out of the job seeking process.
As an added kick in the teeth, once you’ve lost your source of income your energy bills will likely rise as data centers attach to an already strained electricity grid. Many US electricity providers have upped bills as a way to pay for infrastructural upgrades to provide new connections for data centers. And don’t forget the air quality will get worse as more and more gas-burning turbines power up to meet the demand for power.
I still believe there is some good AI can do for the world, particularly in science and medicine. But the main benefit I expect AI to provide to the workplace is a revitalization of labor unions. Despite decades of union busting and a general decline in membership as the old guard retires, this new threat to workers will hopefully act as a catalyst to return labor unions to their former glory.
The more members they have, the stronger they are. No amount of AI agents can change that.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
Benedict is a Senior Security Writer at TechRadar Pro, where he has specialized in covering the intersection of geopolitics, cyber-warfare, and business security.
Benedict provides detailed analysis on state-sponsored threat actors, APT groups, and the protection of critical national infrastructure, with his reporting bridging the gap between technical threat intelligence and B2B security strategy.
Benedict holds an MA (Distinction) in Security, Intelligence, and Diplomacy from the University of Buckingham Centre for Security and Intelligence Studies (BUCSIS), with his specialization providing him with a robust academic framework for deconstructing complex international conflicts and intelligence operations, and the ability to translate intricate security data into actionable insights.

articles.title: 3 razones para ver la última temporada de ‘Cien años de soledad’ de Netflix
articles.text:
En 2024, la adaptación de Cien años de soledad de Netflix sorprendió. No solo porque la serie logró captar lo mejor del universo de realismo mágico imaginado por Gabriel García Márquez. Además, porque la producción exploró a través de sus capítulos el mundo de la obra clásica a detalle. Lo que incluyó profundizar en el legendario pueblo de Macondo como un escenario salvaje, radiante y atemporal en el que todo podía suceder. Al mismo tiempo, traer a la vida a docenas de personajes que forman parte de la cultura latinoamericana y del Caribe sudamericano.
La segunda temporada, concebida oficialmente como última parte de esta ambiciosa adaptación, representa la culminación de ese esfuerzo. También, una recreación fidedigna del último tramo de la novela, en la que el realismo mágico se impregna de un duro comentario político. En especial, porque el legendario universo literario creado por el Premio Nobel colombiano es más que un escenario literario. También, recorre los diversos cambios sociales y culturales que atravesó Sudamérica durante el siglo XX. Todos sin perder el sentido de lo asombroso, humorístico y trágico que define a la querida y universal novela.
Pero además, para su última temporada, que se estrena en dos tandas de capítulos a estrenarse el 5 y el 26 de agosto, Cien años de soledad tiene un reto. El de recorrer la transformación de Macondo en una aldea mágica, en una pequeña ciudad pujante y después, un territorio arrasado por el abandono y la pobreza. Todo, mientras diferentes generaciones de la familia Buendía, nacen y dejan a su paso una historia de leyenda. No obstante, además, una de las series más queridas de Netflix explora en un terreno de narrativa extraordinaria. Una aventura que se resume en tres razones para ver la producción que te dejamos a continuación.
Una adaptación fidedigna de la novela original
Aunque la primera temporada fue catalogada como un éxito, lo cierto es que los showrunner Alex García López y Laura Mora enfrentaron críticas. La mayoría, por tomar la historia original y tomar algunas salvedades específicas para explorar en el ancestral Macondo y sus relatos más conocidos. De hecho, buena parte de la resistencia de Gabriel García Márquez a una adaptación de su obra se debió a que creía que ningún formato podría reflejar el mundo. Algo que pareció comprobar una temporada sobria, interesante, pero por momentos carente del brillo y el asombro que definen la novela.
No obstante, para segunda y final temporada, los episodios se sumergen de lleno en los últimos cincuenta años de la estirpe Buendía. A la vez, en la decadencia del mítico pueblo de Macondo, todo a través de una cuidada puesta en escena. Y esta vez, una prometida fidelidad al texto original. De hecho, los nuevos capítulos prometen abordar el inevitable tránsito desde la utopía inicial hacia una decadencia profunda y mística. Todo a través de una idea casi religiosa sobre la historia de un pueblo que contiene a cada pueblo del continente e incluso del mundo.
Pero en lugar de hacerlo realista o tratar que tenga un aire más mundano, Cien años de soledad vuelve a sus raíces puras de realismo mágico. Por lo que la producción opta por una historia en que lo asombroso se vuelve parte del tiempo y de las vicisitudes. También, un recorrido misterioso a través del bien y del mal, de la búsqueda del propósito y hasta de la redención. Todo a través del pueblo de Macondo, construido a escala real por Netflix como un gigantesco set físico de más de 40,000 metros cuadrados en la finca Arizona. Esta, ubicada en el departamento del Tolima (entre Alvarado e Ibagué), recrea la evolución del pueblo a lo largo de un siglo.
La misma evolución del libro ‘Cien años de soledad’ llega a la adaptación de Netflix
De la misma forma que el libro, la segunda temporada de Cien años de soledad cuenta una etapa cruenta en Macondo. Y se enfoca en el coronel Aureliano Buendía (Claudio Cataño) y el tramo final de su vida. Por lo que el relato se expande hacia una madurez sombría, donde el realismo mágico adquiere un tono más cinematográfico y emocional. El enorme reto de traducir una de las obras más complejas de la literatura hispanoamericana encuentra en estos capítulos una resolución visualmente imponente.
Pero además, la serie hará un recorrido por un universo que se vuelve muchísimo más complejo. Eso debido a que Macondo ya no solo es un pueblo perdido en la serranía colombiana. Ahora, es una pequeña ciudad que muestra y profundiza en los prodigios, males y progreso del siglo XX desde una óptica asombrosa. Para la ocasión, Cien años de soledad usará la idea del pueblo como un ente vivo, capaz de crecer y convertirse en un personaje más.
Eso mientras sus personajes se vuelven cada vez más simbólicos y extraordinarios. También, uno de los puntos altos de Cien años de soledad será traer a la televisión, momentos hitos dentro de la novela. Entre ellos, dos de los más recordados: la desaparición de Remedios, la bella (Yiseth Garcerant) y la llegada de Fernanda del Carpio (Carla Baratta). Así como la muerte de Melquíades (Moreno Borja) y su regreso de entre los muertos. Y, claro está, apoteósico final de la novela.
Dos tandas de capítulos para profundizar mejor en ‘Cien años de soledad’
Para su última temporada, Cien años de soledad divide esta conclusión en dos bloques clave. Todo pensado para maximizar el impacto dramático y permitir que la audiencia asimile el peso de la historia. El primer bloque se estrena el 5 de agosto, compuesto por siete episodios de larga duración que desarrollan el grueso de la trama generacional. A la vez, los conflictos sociopolíticos que transformarán el entorno de Macondo.
Posteriormente, el 26 de agosto se estrena un gran capítulo final concebido prácticamente como un largometraje independiente de casi dos horas de duración. Este, diseñado exclusivamente para cerrar de manera épica el ciclo existencial de los personajes principales. Esta inusual estrategia de distribución busca emular el ritmo pausado pero contundente del libro. Lo que asegura que el desenlace de la maldición familiar reciba la atención y la solemnidad técnica que merece.
Cada entrega de esta etapa ha sido tratada de forma individual por los directores Laura Mora y Carlos Moreno. De hecho, el dúo ha trabajado arduamente para elevar los estándares estéticos, el diseño sonoro y la composición musical, logrando una atmósfera envolvente.
Lo que debes saber sobre la segunda temporada de ‘Cien años de soledad’
La trama de la segunda temporada comienza inmediatamente después de la firma del armisticio y el histórico Tratado de Neerlandia. Un periodo donde la anhelada paz sigue siendo un espejismo lejano para los habitantes de la región. Los sectores conservadores, atemorizados por la latente influencia y las amenazas remanentes del desencantado coronel Aureliano Buendía, comienzan a urdir conspiraciones. Lo que altera irreversiblemente el equilibrio de la comunidad.
En medio de estas tensiones políticas y por un capricho del destino, llega al pueblo desde la lejana y fría Bogotá el personaje de Fernanda del Carpio. Su matrimonio con Aureliano Segundo (Thiago Suaza) introduce costumbres rígidas y valores externos que chocan de manera frontal con el espíritu libre de la casa. Pero también otorga a la matriarca Úrsula Iguarán (Marleyda Soto) sus primeros herederos legítimos. De este modo, la producción aborda con gran precisión el choque cultural y el relevo generacional dentro de la enorme casona familiar.

articles.title: HP’s HyperX Omen 15 isn’t quite the budget-friendly gaming laptop its predecessor was
articles.text:
The HP HyperX Omen 15, which I first saw at CES, replaces the HP Victus 15, a longtime bestselling budget gaming laptop. The Victus cost just $800, or less when on sale, and was a good entry point to decent laptop gaming.
HP’s HyperX Omen 15 isn’t quite the budget-friendly gaming laptop its predecessor was
But it’s decent enough for 1080p gaming in our RAMageddon world.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
The Omen 15 has nice little upgrades over the Victus. Its RTX 5050 Laptop GPU can play 2026’s latest games, albeit on low-ish settings. But it’s also got a brighter 16:10 aspect ratio display with higher refresh rate, and a 1080p webcam to make it a little better for non-gaming stuff.
I’d call it a working-class gaming laptop, but thanks to RAMageddon, the Omen 15 starts at $1,200 — a far cry from the $800 that made its predecessor so appealing. But laptop prices are way up across the board, and if you want current-gen gaming hardware, this is about as cheap as you’re going to find it.
The Good
- Affordable-ish gaming performance in a decent to solid package
- Fine for 1080p / 1200p gaming and light content creation
- 165Hz refresh rate on a fairly bright screen
- Upgradeable DDR5 RAM and NVMe SSD (with two slots for each)
The Bad
- Not as affordable the HP Victus 15 it replaces
- Only one of the USB ports is USB-C — and not even Thunderbolt
- No face or fingerprint unlocking
- Keyboard, trackpad, and speakers range from okay to bad
Component report card
- Screen: C
- Webcam: C
- Keyboard: C
- Trackpad: D
- Port selection: C
- Speakers: C
- Number of ugly stickers to remove: 3
Our HyperX Omen 15 review unit is a $1,199 configuration sold through Walmart with an eight-core Intel Core 5 210H “Raptor Lake” chip, RTX 5050 discreet GPU, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and 512GB SSD. There are pricier Omen 15 configs out there with RTX 5070 GPUs and OLED screens, but that’s like spending Acura money on a Honda Civic. On the lower end, HP still has a Victus 15 config with the RTX 5050 for $900, but it has 8GB of RAM — that’s not really tenable, especially for playing the latest games.
The good news is that the Omen 15 with an RTX 5050 is pretty serviceable for playing games at its 1920 x 1200 native resolution. Last-gen games like Control can get a smooth 70 to 80fps on High preset while using DLSS. Cyberpunk 2077 can run on the Ultra preset (no ray tracing) with DLSS set to Quality and get 60 to 70fps— sometimes dipping down to 40 while driving with lots of stuff onscreen. Standard frame generation boosts it to 95 to 105fps, and 70s to low 80s in a car. Multi Frame Gen, which you don’t get on last-gen GPUs, can push that ever further if you don’t mind more “fake frames.”
Newer games are a more Medium to Low affair. For example, Helldivers 2 runs comfortably at just above 60fps on its Medium preset with DLSS set to Quality — though it dips into the 40s when the bug guts hit the fan. But Battlefield 6 was lower, down in the 50fps range while running Medium preset with DLSS cranked to Performance. I also tested Halo: Campaign Evolved, which defaulted to its Very Low preset, where it looked like a potato. On Low settings, with DLSS set to Medium, it mustered between 50 to 60fps, but with frequent drops into the 40s with lots of enemies onscreen.
While playing all these games, the fans kicked up to a decent volume, but they weren’t obnoxiously loud, and the chassis stayed reasonably cool. The hottest point, a small spot under the chassis, rose to 113 degrees Fahrenheit / 45 Celsius. But the main areas that normally make contact with your hands or lap didn’t get too warm — pretty good thermals for a somewhat compact gaming laptop.
So the RTX 5050 GPU and its 8GB of VRAM can get by with the latest graphically intense games, so long as you’re not expecting a visual powerhouse. But what about living with the rest of the laptop?
Much of the Omen 15’s price has gone to its specs. That means there are some rough edges showing in the usual areas. The trackpad has a responsive mechanical click, but if you pick up the laptop by either of its front corners the chassis flexes and causes an accidental click. This is common in mostly plastic laptops, but still annoying.
The keyboard has decent enough tactility when typing. But even though I know gamers love a number pad, it makes this 15-inch laptop feel cramped. I don’t enjoy typing on it like I have other HP laptops. The speakers? A little muddy-sounding — especially for music. And the ports? It has HDMI 2.1 and gigabit ethernet, which is great, but only one USB-C to go with its two USB-A ports. And all of them are a modest 10Gbps — not particularly speedy compared to USB4 or Thunderbolt 4. Gaming laptops are supposed to have ports aplenty, but this is just ports apassable.
Aside from its gaming performance, the Omen 15’s other strength is its screen. The 1920 x 1200 IPS panel isn’t particularly special, but at 400 nits it’s decently bright and it has nice contrast and colors. It’s good for games, and fine for productivity work and light content creation. I did a bit of Lightroom Classic editing on the Omen 15, and my 50-megapixel RAW files were workable at a modest clip. (It helped that I was editing a batch of under 50 images, and not, like, 2,000.) The bigger problem with trying to do creative things was the Omen’s paltry 512GB of storage. It fills up quickly when games like Battlefield 6 take up 142GB. There’s a second M.2 slot for another drive, just as there’s a second RAM slot, which is great for future upgrades — but boy will that cost you right now. You can hold out for RAM and SSD prices to come back down to Earth, but if that takes as long as it’s expected to, the Omen 15 might feel pretty outdated by then.
The Omen was also fine for my everyday work: Chrome tabs, four virtual desktops, Signal, Slack, music streaming, etc. While the 1080p webcam is a little grainy and slightly low in saturation, it looks fine on video calls. The main barrier to getting work done on the Omen 15 is that its battery never lasted me more than five and a half hours. That’s far from the worst for gaming laptops, but keep that chunky power adapter with its barrel plug nearby.
The HyperX Omen 15 is a decent gaming laptop. It’s just not the value the Victus 15 used to be. But neither is anything else. Absent a really good sale, you’re going to pay over $1,000 for anything with the RTX 5050, and usually a lot more. But buying into even the bottom rung of the 50-series gets you all of Nvidia’s latest features, like Multi Frame Gen and whatever DLSS 5 eventually shapes up to be. Last-gen 40-series or AMD GPUs aren’t bad options, but Multi Frame Gen can help keep frame rates playable for longer.
It’s still worth looking for those sales, though. HP, Best Buy, and Walmart often have deals on most of HP’s product line. Even now, there’s an Omen 16 with an RTX 5060 GPU and slightly larger (but dimmer) screen for just $100 more than the Omen 15.
RAMageddon makes buying a new gaming laptop daunting. If you need to buy now and you don’t want to go open-box or secondhand, you just have to come to terms with the fact that you’re going to be paying higher prices than equivalent models from a year or two ago — even in the “entry level.” Considering the circumstances, the Omen 15 is an okay value at $1,200 for getting into laptop gaming.
HyperX Omen 15 specs (as reviewed)
- Display: 15.3-inch 1920 x 1200 165Hz IPS, 400 nits, anti-glare
- CPU: Intel Core 5 210H (Raptor Lake, 8 cores)
- GPU: Nvidia GeForce RTX 5050
- RAM: 16GB DDR5 (two SODIMM slots, user-accessible)
- Storage: 512GB NVMe M.2 (two slots, user-accessible)
- Webcam: 1080p
- Connectivity: Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.3
- Ports: 2x USB-A 10Gbps, 1x USB-C 10Gbps, AC power (barrel plug), HDMI 2.1, RJ-45 gigabit ethernet, 3.5mm combo audio jack

- Dimensions: 13.5 x 9.96 x 0.89 - 0.93 inches / 342.9 x 252.98 x 22.61 - 23.62mm

articles.title: Youth Photographic Society showcases winners of 2026 international competition
articles.text:
Youth Photographic Society showcases winners of 2026 international competition
In this photo essay, we showcase the YPS photography exhibition at Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath, along with curator insights.
Launched in 2014, PhotoSparks is a weekly feature from YourStory, with photographs that celebrate the spirit of creativity and innovation. In the earlier 1,010 posts, we featured an art festival, cartoon gallery. world music festival, telecom expo, millets fair, climate change expo, wildlife conference, startup festival, Diwali rangoli, and jazz festival.
Youth Photographic Society (YPS) Bengaluru recently presented winners of its International Salon 2026 photographic awards in an exhibition at Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath (KCP). Started in 1971, YPS is a not-for-profit organisation with over 700 members, and is among the largest photography clubs in India.
See our coverage of earlier exhibitions at this Bengaluru cultural hub here, including the 2023 edition of YPS Salon. KCP’s most popular event is the annual Chitra Santhe, regarded as India’s largest street fair for art.
YPS was founded under the patronage of the earlier Department of Youth Services & Sports, Government of Mysore. Vanaja Rao was its first president, and a range of expert and emerging photographers have been showcased over the decades.
Over the last few years, YPS has gone through a digital transformation for modernising its services. The annual awards report is also available for download on its website, describing the award categories, jury and winners.
YPS has organised over 40 national and 15 international Salon competitions. They are sought after by Indian and foreign participants on account of professionalism, open judging, carefully choreographed print exhibition, and high-quality catalogues.
“YPS International Salon 2026 reaffirms our commitment to artistic excellence and our growing global presence. This edition witnessed 311 participants, with 3,489 images submitted from 38 countries,” Salon 2026 chairperson Anitha Mysore explains.
The Salon showcased wide diversity in themes, creativity and visual expression across sections. “To further encourage artistic exploration, we introduced Colour Abstracts as a new section. The response was both enthusiastic and inspiring,” she adds.
The photographers’ lineup, some of whose works are featured here, includes Aadit Arcot, Aage Madsen, Aarav Prasanth, Ajita Nayar, Alain Morata, Anand Nirgude, Alex Mclean, Ananth Kamat, Alexander Hochhaus, Animesh Saxena, and Andreas Kuen.
Other photographers are Oleg Malovitskyi, Partha Roy, Pauline Naudi, Peter Haeusler, Phani Bhushan Ramasastry, Phillip Kwan, Minaketan Sabar, Muhammed Rafeek, and Pietro Rocchiccioli.
Each of the four exhibited categories of photographs presents a unique perspective on the art of photography. Viewed together, they create a balanced experience that inspires creativity and deepens appreciation, and encourages viewers to see the world through different lenses.
Monochrome photography highlights the beauty of light, shadow, texture, and composition. By removing the distraction of colour, it allows viewers to focus on emotions, patterns and storytelling. Black-and-white images often evoke nostalgia or drama, demonstrating how simplicity itself can create powerful visual impact.
In contrast, colour photography celebrates the vibrancy and diversity of our experienced world. Colour has the ability to influence mood, communicate emotion, and draw attention to details that might otherwise go unnoticed.
Nature photography connects audiences with the beauty and wonder of the broader world. They inspire appreciation for the environment while showcasing the patience, observation and technical skill required to capture nature at its finest. They also provoke conversation about biodiversity and humanity's relationship with our planet.
Colour abstracts take creativity a step further by challenging conventional ways of seeing. Instead of representing subjects literally, abstract photography creates imaginative compositions that encourage viewers to engage with the artwork emotionally and intellectually rather than seeking a single meaning.
At YPS Salon, these four categories created a compelling balance between realism and imagination, simplicity and complexity, and observation and interpretation. A wide spectrum of photographic techniques and artistic styles were showcased.
Such a combination highlights the versatility of photography as an art form and also inspires photographers and viewers alike to experiment with different perspectives, formats and techniques. It demonstrates that photography is more than capturing images—it is a powerful medium for storytelling and discovering beauty in both the ordinary and the extraordinary.
“As we move forward, we remain committed to fostering creativity, strengthening our global community, and elevating the standards of photographic excellence that define YPS,” Mysore signs off.
Now what have you done today to pause in your busy schedule and harness your creative side for a better world?
(All photographs taken by Madanmohan Rao on location at Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath.)

articles.title: Gaya : les vélos cargos électriques peuvent être loués en longue durée
articles.text:
Gaya est une marque française de vélo électrique, elle commercialise essentiellement des vélos cargo à destination des familles, nous avons d’ailleurs pu tester leur dernier modèle le Incroyable Le Long qui nous a conquis. La marque lance aujourd’hui une offre de location longue durée. Disponible dès maintenant en boutique et sur le site de la marque, elle permet de louer un vélo à partir de 89 € par mois, assurance comprise, pour une durée allant de 12 à 36 mois.
Une formule de location longue durée tout compris
Jusqu’à présent, Gaya proposait plusieurs modes de paiement : achat classique ou paiement en 4× sans frais. La marque offre désormais la possibilité de souscrire à une offre de location longue durée. Les clients peuvent configurer le modèle de leur choix, les modèles proposés à la location sont neufs. Les durées de location sont de 12, 18, 24, 30 ou 36 mois. Cette offre de location longue durée a été conçu avec la plateforme de leasing GreanLeaze.
Le prix de loyer de votre futur vélo va dépendre du prix d’achat du modèle choisi. Si l’on prend par exemple, le modèle Incroyable, que nous avons avons eu la chance de tester l’an dernier et commercialisé à 2900 € vous devrez alors débourser 112 € pour 36 mois, 140 € pour 24 mois, 169 € pour 18 mois et 226 € pour un an de location. Le prix d’appel de 89 € par mois correspond à la location d’un vélo L’Original, Le Court pour une durée de 36 mois.
L’assurance contre la casse et le vol est incluse dans l’offre de location, celle-ci couvre jusqu’à 2 casses et 1 vol par an (batterie incluse), avec une franchise de 10 % en cas de sinistre. Au moment de la souscription, un premier versement correspondant à deux mensualités est demandé, avant le paiement d’un loyer fixe pendant toute la durée du contrat.
À la fin de la location, deux choix s’offrent à vous : garder votre vélo grâce à une option d’achat ou bien le rendre. L’offre de location Gaya est éligible au Forfait Mobilité Durable.

articles.title: Gastan más de 5 millones de euros para liberar 30 aves y en seis meses solo sobrevive una
articles.text:
Mantener a raya la población de una especie invasora lleva consigo enormes esfuerzos, investigación e inversión. Evitar que las especies autóctonas desaparezcan, también. Desgraciadamente, no es tan "fácil" como conseguir crías de la especie en cuestión y liberarlas en su hábitat natural y para muestra, el urogallo cantábrico, una subespecie exclusiva de la cordillera Cantábrica y también la más amenazada de toda Europa occidental.
En 2005 el urogallo cantábrico pasó a la categoría de "en peligro de extinción" y a día de hoy quedan menos de 300 ejemplares en libertad y bajando (la Junta de Castilla y León da una cifra aún más baja). En 2018 empezó un plan para tratar de recuperarlo que incluye la cría en cautividad, mejora de su hábitat y liberaciones a modo de prueba. La primera liberación experimental ha sido un auténtico desastre.
Los juegos del hambre del urogallo. Entre el 23 de octubre y el 4 de noviembre de 2025 llevaron a cabo la primera suelta de 30 urogallos criados en cautividad en el Centro de Valsemana en la Zona de Especial Protección para las Aves del Alto Sil, en León. Acabó como los juegos del hambre: como recogía el Diario de León, seis meses después solo quedaba viva una hembra. Los datos de seguimiento con dispositivos GPS/GSM y emisores VHF recogen que 26 de las 29 bajas son obra de depredadores como el zorro, aves rapaces o la marta.
Por qué es importante. Porque constata con cifras aplastantes que la reintroducción de aves criadas en cautividad rara vez funciona con gallináceos de bosque principalmente por un motivo: son demasiado ingenuas frente a potenciales depredadores, como ya se había demostrado. Con una población silvestre en estado crítico, estos intentos fallidos supone malgastar recursos y tiempo, que biológicamente hablando escasea para la especie.
Contexto. Desgraciadamente, no es la primera vez que pasa. Un experimento similar en Harz (Alemania) tuvo un desenlace parecido: solo el 23% de las aves liberadas sobrevivió, la mayoría de las muertes ocurrió en el primer mes (la vida media fue de 13 días) y el 62% de muertes tuvieron como culpable el zorro. Además de los depredadores, también encontraron problemas fisiológicos: su aparato digestivo no está tan preparado como el de un ave salvaje para la dieta silvestre.
En detalle. Antes de la liberación, estuvieron entre 12 y 19 días en los voladeros de presuelta, donde se adaptaron bien. Después, la liberación se llevó a cabo de forma gradual y sin incidencias en cinco grupos (tres solo de machos y dos mixtos). Su seguimiento inicial mostró que la mayoría se quedó alrededor del punto de suelta, con solo tres ejemplares alejándose más de un kilómetro. La cría en cautividad funciona muy bien, lo que confirma que el problema no es reproducir la especie, sino que sobreviva después.
Si bien es cierto que el programa ha traído avances y aprendizajes, el balance de resultados en cifras es más pesimista. No hay datos públicos de coste de esta suelta concreta, pero sí del programa: el Centro de Cría de Valsemana con su ampliación y la mejora del hábitat del urogallo cantábrico superó los 5 millones de euros en total.
Sí, pero. Aunque en términos de supervivencia el resultado ha sido un fracaso, el enfoque no es inviable. Un estudio en Polonia con 22 urogallos jóvenes liberados encontró que su actividad, movimientos y dieta eran similares a los de aves silvestres, concluyendo que la reintroducción de urogallos criados en cautividad puede tener éxito siempre y cuando se reduzca la mortalidad inicial.
De hecho, un programa alemán de los 80 - 90 sí que logró establecer una población de 30-40 individuos tras liberar 393 aves. En pocas palabras: la mortalidad inicial es altísima, pero perfeccionando el entrenamiento antipredatorio y el control de depredadores en la zona de suelta, la tasa puede mejorar. De hecho, es algo que la propia Junta ya se plantea para futuras acciones.
Portada | Patrice schoefolt

articles.title: Llega al Perú Clapper: cómo monetizar desde el primer día haciendo videos
articles.text:
Clapper anunció el inicio formal de sus operaciones en Perú durante el tercer trimestre de 2026, consolidando su presencia en Latinoamérica. La plataforma de videos, que ya cuenta con miles de usuarios locales, supera ahora los 700 mil registros en el país.
El objetivo es ofrecer un entorno donde los creadores de contenido puedan acceder a herramientas de monetización desde el primer día, una diferencia clave respecto a otros servicios que imponen requisitos previos para acceder a ingresos.
PUBLICIDAD
La compañía busca fortalecer su posición como espacio de referencia para quienes desean generar ingresos y construir comunidades digitales propias.
“Perú cuenta con una comunidad de creadores con enorme potencial y un ecosistema digital en constante evolución. Queremos ofrecer un espacio donde cualquier persona pueda crear contenido sin la presión de perseguir algoritmos y acceder a oportunidades de monetización desde el primer día, sin importar el tamaño de su audiencia”, dijo Edison Chen, CEO y fundador de la empresa.
PUBLICIDAD
Expansión en Latinoamérica y apuesta por la economía de creadores
Clapper se encuentra disponible en más de 50 países y ha identificado a Latinoamérica como un mercado estratégico en su crecimiento global. La llegada oficial a Perú responde a una tendencia en aumento: la búsqueda de nuevas alternativas para la creación y monetización de contenido digital, impulsada por el desarrollo de la llamada economía de creadores.
Según el informe Global Entertainment & Media Outlook 2025–2029 de PwC, los ingresos globales del sector alcanzaron cerca de 3 billones de dólares en 2024 y la proyección para 2029 es de 3.5 billones.
PUBLICIDAD
El reporte señala que el crecimiento estará vinculado principalmente a la publicidad digital y la aparición de nuevos modelos de creación y distribución basados en comunidades y nichos. Estos datos ilustran el potencial de plataformas como Clapper para responder a las necesidades del mercado actual.
Enfoque en contenidos locales y participación de la comunidad
La estrategia de Clapper para el mercado peruano prioriza la difusión de contenidos relacionados con estilo de vida, gastronomía, emprendimiento y cultura local. La empresa ha detectado que el contenido en español muestra uno de los mejores desempeños en su avance regional, acompañado de altos niveles de retención y una participación activa de creadores que privilegian formatos conversacionales y cercanos a sus audiencias.
PUBLICIDAD
“Hoy existe una gran oportunidad para replantear cómo las plataformas digitales construyen comunidad. Las personas buscan espacios donde puedan expresarse con mayor libertad, conectar desde intereses comunes y desarrollar relaciones genuinas con sus audiencias, siempre dentro de un entorno basado en el respeto”, aseguró Chen al presentar la estrategia para Perú.
Monetización sin requisitos
Una de las características distintivas de Clapper es la eliminación de barreras para acceder a la monetización. A diferencia de otros servicios, como TikTok, Facebook, Twitch o Instagram, la plataforma ofrece herramientas para generar ingresos a todos los usuarios desde que crean su cuenta, sin importar el tamaño de su audiencia ni la cantidad de seguidores.
PUBLICIDAD
Estos son los requisitos para monetizar que solicitan las aplicaciones de videos más populares hasta el momento:
TikTok (Programa de recompensas para creadores)
El programa principal de monetización por visualizaciones (que reemplazó al antiguo Fondo de Creadores) exige un estándar más alto en números y duración del video:
PUBLICIDAD
- 10,000 seguidores genuinos.
- Al menos 100,000 visualizaciones válidas en los últimos 30 días.
- Tener cuenta personal (las cuentas de empresa/negocio están excluidas) y ser mayor de 18 años.
- Requisito de formato: Solo monetizan videos originales de más de 1 minuto de duración.
Facebook (Anuncios In-Stream en videos y Reels)
Para generar ingresos insertando anuncios en el contenido subido a Páginas o perfiles en Modo Profesional:
- 5,000 seguidores.
- Al menos 60,000 minutos reproducidos en los últimos 60 días (incluyendo videos bajo demanda, en vivo o Reels).
- Tener 5 o más videos activos en la página.
Twitch (Programa de Afiliados)
Para monetizar transmisiones en vivo mediante suscripciones, bits y anuncios básicos:
- Al menos 50 seguidores.
- 500 minutos en directo repartidos en un mínimo de 7 días distintos durante los últimos 30 días.
- Una media de al menos 3 espectadores simultáneos.
Instagram (Regalos y Suscripciones en Reels)
- Para recibir Regalos (Gifts) en Reels o activar Suscripciones de pago, la plataforma exige una cuenta profesional y suele requerir un mínimo de 5,000 a 10,000 seguidores (según la función y el país), además de cumplir estrictamente con las políticas de monetización para socios.
- Los bonos directos de Instagram por rendimiento operan habitualmente por invitación.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Le film d'animation Memories de Katsuhiro Otomo s'offre une édition collector en Blu-ray 4K
articles.text:
« Avec Memories, Katsuhiro Otomo achève sa transition du manga vers l’animation, déjà largement entamée quelques années auparavant avec Akira », nous dit le site de Dybex, l’éditeur de ce coffret Memories en édition collector. Réalisé par Katsuhiro Otomo (Akira), conjointement avec Koji Morimoto et Tensai Okamura, deux animateurs ayant notamment travaillé sur Akira, Ghost in the Shell ou encore Cowboy Bebop, ce triptyque se compose de trois courts métrages de science-fiction, tirés du manga du même nom écrit et dessiné par Katsuhiro Otomo.
Précommandez Memories en Blu-ray 4K
Ce coffret collector de Memories s’annonce particulièrement généreux, avec une édition limitée à seulement 999 exemplaires. Cette édition est vendue au prix de 69,99 € sur le site de La Fnac, et sortira le 16 septembre 2026. Elle contient :
- un Blu-ray UHD 4K, destiné aux téléviseurs et lecteurs compatibles 4K, avec le film en VOSTFR 5.1 et VF 5.1,
- un second Blu-ray classique proposant lui aussi les deux pistes audio, pour les lecteurs Blu-ray standards,
- un Steelbook contenant les deux disques,
- un jeu de cartes postales,
- le storyboard intégral de La Rose magnétique,
- un livret spécial,
- deux CD audio avec la B.O. du film.
C’est quoi, ce film d’animation Memories ?
Sorti en 1995, Memories est un film d’animation japonais composé de trois courts métrages de science-fiction, réunis autour de l’univers de Katsuhiro Otomo, le créateur d’Akira. Chaque segment propose une histoire et une ambiance très différentes, mais tous explorent à leur manière des thèmes chers à la science-fiction, comme la technologie, la mémoire, la folie ou encore les dérives de l’humanité.
Le film se distingue par sa grande richesse visuelle et son ton souvent sombre et étrange. Le premier court métrage, Magnetic Rose, le plus beau de cette anthologie, suit des astronautes confrontés à une mystérieuse station spatiale et à un passé qui semble prendre vie. La somptueuse musique de Yoko Kanno (Cowboy Bebop) accompagne le court métrage, l’un des plus beaux de l’animation japonaise.
Stink Bomb adopte un ton plus satirique autour d’une catastrophe aussi absurde que dévastatrice. Enfin, Cannon Fodder propose une vision dystopique d’une société entièrement organisée autour de la guerre. Trois histoires très différentes, donc, qui font de Memories une œuvre incontournable pour les amateurs d’animation japonaise et de science-fiction.

articles.title: Suno unterliegt der Gema vor Gericht
articles.text:
Nach Erfolg gegen OpenAI: Gema setzt sich vor Gericht gegen KI-Musikgenerator Suno durch
Im November 2025 hatte die Musikverwertungsgesellschaft Gema bei ihrer Klage gegen KI-Anbieter OpenAI und dessen Chatbot ChatGPT vor dem Landgericht München Recht bekommen. Wie die Gema dem Gericht darlegte, hatte OpenAI ohne entsprechende Erlaubnis Liedtexte innerhalb seines KI-Modells memorisiert, verarbeitet und damit vervielfältigt. Das Gericht war der Argumentation gefolgt.
Gema bringt Suno vor Gericht
Mit Suno hat die Gema jetzt ein weiteres KI-Unternehmen aus den USA vor Gericht geholt. Diesmal ging es nicht um Liedtexte, sondern um sechs Musikstücke, darunter „Atemlos“, „Big in Japan“ und „Daddy Cool“. Wie das Landgericht München I am 31. Juli 2026 urteilte, soll Suno für seinen auf KI beruhenden Musikgenerator bestimmte geschützte Musikwerke ohne Genehmigung vervielfältigt haben.
Dies müsse Suno unterlassen. Das Verbot betrifft laut einem Bericht der Tagesschau auch die Verwendung der Werke beim KI-Training. Suno bestritt derweil, dass die Musikwerke als solche in seinem KI-Modell gespeichert seien. Vielmehr enthielten solche Modelle mathematische Parameter, die beim Training aus großen Datenmengen abgeleitet würden.
Berufung auf Fair Use schlägt fehl
Zudem berief sich das US-Unternehmen auf die sogenannte Fair-Use-Regelung. Im US-amerikanischen Recht dürfen damit geschützte Werke für bestimmte Zwecke auch ohne Zustimmung des Rechteinhabers genutzt werden. Suno bestritt zudem die Zuständigkeit des deutschen Gerichts.
Die Gema hatte übrigens einen einfachen Test unternommen, um den eigenen Verdacht zu untermauern, dass Suno die entsprechenden Musikstücke vervielfältigt habe. So gaben sie dem Musikgenerator Text, Titel und Stil der sechs Songs – aber keine weiteren Vorgaben wie Melodie oder Arrangement. Laut Gema hätten die KI-generierten Ergebnisse den Originalen „stark geähnelt“.
Gema kann mit Schadensersatz rechnen
Sollte das bisher noch nicht rechtskräftige Urteil umgesetzt werden, müsste Suno der Gema auch einen Schadensersatz zahlen. Über dessen Höhe ist aber noch nicht entschieden worden. Suno zeigte sich nicht mit dem Urteil einverstanden und will jetzt seine Optionen prüfen. Auch über eine Berufung denkt das Unternehmen nach.
Beobachter:innen sehen in der Entscheidung aber eine Signalwirkung. Das Urteil können vor allem andere Rechteinhaber in ihren Prozessen gegen KI-Anbieter wie Suno als Argument verwenden. Unter anderem Universal und Sony klagen derzeit vor Gericht gegen Suno. Warner Music hatte sich hingegen Ende 2025 mit der KI-Firma auf einen Lizenzvertrag geeinigt.
Und so wird durch die Geldgier der Musikindustrie der Fortschritt der KI ausgebremst.

articles.title: Les Anneaux de pouvoir saison 3 : date de sortie, intrigue, trailer… Tout savoir sur la série Prime Video
articles.text:
Les Anneaux de pouvoir saison 3 : date de sortie, intrigue, trailer… Tout savoir sur la série Prime Video
Le futur de la Terre du Milieu s'assombrit de plus en plus dans la saison 3 de la série dérivée du Seigneur des Anneaux. Voici tout ce qu'il faut savoir sur la suite des Anneaux de Pouvoir.
Le service de streaming Prime Video diffusera prochainement la saison 3 de sa série dérivée de l'oeuvre de J.R.R Tolkien et dans cette dernière, Sauron se prépare à forger son arme ultime destinée à contrôler la Terre du Milieu.
Après avoir fabriqué plusieurs anneaux dans la deuxième saison de la série Le Seigneur des Anneaux : Les Anneaux de Pouvoir, il est temps pour le Seigneur des Ténèbres de faire règner la terreur et de forger un Anneau Unique "pour les gouverner tous." Histoire, casting, images... On fait le point sur la saison 3 des Anneaux de Pouvoir.
Quelle date de sortie pour la saison 3 des Anneaux de Pouvoir ?
C'est à partir du 11 novembre prochain que les fans de la série pourront retrouver la saison 3 sur Prime Video. Le calendrier de diffusion de ces huit nouveaux épisodes est le suivant :
- Épisodes 1 à 4 : 11 novembre 2026
- Épisodes 5 et 6 : 18 novembre 2026
- Épisodes 7 et 8 : 25 novembre 2026
Quelle intrigue pour la saison 3 des Anneaux de Pouvoir ?
Ces nouveaux épisodes se déroulent cinq ans après les événements de la saison 2, alors que la guerre entre les Elfes et Sauron bat son plein.
Le Seigneur des Ténèbres cherche à forger l'Anneau Unique, l'arme qui lui donnera l'avantage décisif pour remporter la guerre, asservir tous les peuples à sa volonté — et régner enfin sur la Terre du Milieu tout entière.
Qui est aux commandes de cette saison 3 ?
Les showrunners de la série Le Seigneur des Anneaux : Les Anneaux de Pouvoir sont toujours J.D. Payne et Patrick McKay, qui sont également producteurs exécutifs aux côtés de Lindsey Weber, Justin Doble, Kate Hazell et Charlotte Brändström.
À la réalisation, on retrouve Brändström (Outlander), Sanaa Hamri (La Roue du Temps) et Stefan Schwartz (The Boys). La musique demeure composée par Bear McCreary (God of War).
Qui est au casting de la saison 3 ?
On retrouve dans la distribution de cette nouvelle saison des visages déjà vus dans les épisodes précédents des Anneaux de Pouvoir, comme Charlie Vickers sous les traits de Sauron, Morfydd Clark dans le rôle de Galadriel, Robert Aramayo dans celui d'Elrond et Ismael Cruz Córdova en Arondir.
Cependant, de nombreux nouveaux venus vont aussi apparaître dans cette saison 3, dont Jamie Campbell Bower (Stranger Things) dans le rôle du mari de Galadriel, Celeborn, et Andrew Richardson (Guys & Dolls) sous les traits d'Anárion, le frère d'Isildur.

articles.title: A Meta developer's Linux patch could boost Steam Deck frame rates by up to 32%
articles.text:
Linux is Game: The Steam Deck was built around AMD APUs and the Linux-based SteamOS platform. APUs have to work within tight power constraints, which is why some developers are pushing the software side as far as it'll go to make games run faster.
David Vernet, a Linux kernel hacker at Meta, recently unveiled a series of new patches for the open source kernel. He explained that the code is designed to cut down on stuttering and frame-time spikes on AMD APU-based gaming handhelds, thanks to a new operating mode added to the amd-pstate driver.
Amd-pstate is a driver designed to improve control over processor frequency in AMD CPUs running a Linux-based operating system. The driver includes the Energy Performance Preference (EPP) attribute, which tells the hardware whether the currently running software wants maximum speed or wants to save battery power instead.
Vernet's patches build on active EPP mode, which normally lets the AMD APU decide the best strategy for whatever's running. He explained that gaming workloads, mostly built around one "busy" thread taking frequent short sleeps, tend to perform poorly under that kind of scheme.
The new code adds a per-core EPP boost. When the epp_boost module is enabled in Linux, each core on the processor is sampled every 10 ms. If a core is at least 50% busy, its EPP field is set to "performance," and it stays there until 300 ms pass without another busy sample, at which point the driver restores the core's previous EPP setting.
According to benchmark data Vernet provided, the new EPP boost mechanism can have a significant impact on frame rate, especially at the 1%-low level. He tested Civilization VI on a Steam Deck and found its 1%-low frame rate improved by 31.8%. The p99 frame time improved by 4.1%, though average frame rate was unaffected.
Vernet used Civ VI for his tests because of the game's heavy reliance on single-thread CPU performance, and because it offers a repeatable, built-in benchmark pass. Most likely he also just likes the game. Still, the proposed patches should theoretically benefit other games running on any SteamOS (or Linux) handheld with an AMD APU.

articles.title: 'It's a new era': I spoke to the passionate, ambitious, and visionary founders of Story Kitchen, who fought the videogame adaptation curse and Hollywood scepticism — and won
articles.text:
'That's our next mission — proving that games are art': meet Story Kitchen, the bold, trail-blazing studio behind the popular Sonic movies that wants to turn your favorite game into the next movie or TV hit
"It is easier, but it's not easy," Story Kitchen co-founder Dmitri Johnson interjects.
I'm midway through an in-depth conversation with Johnson and business partner Mike Goldberg about their pioneering entertainment company when the former clarifies something he alluded to earlier.
The topic in question? Pitching movies and TV shows based on video game properties to other studio figureheads is still challenging. That's in spite of myriad recent examples of popular game franchises being turned into other screen-based art forms that have achieved critical and commercial success.
"We're working every day to continue changing the stigma that games are only for kids and lazy people who still live in their mom's basement," Johnson adds with a wry smile. "These are artists and storytellers in their own right — and their work deserves to be seen by more people."
Press start
You probably haven't heard of Story Kitchen, but you definitely know the video game adaptations they've helped to shape.
From Paramount Pictures' money-spinning Sonic the Hedgehog film franchise and Netflix's animated Tomb Raider show, to Prime Video's forthcoming TV re-imaginings of the aforementioned Lara Croft-fronted game series and Dontnod's beloved first Life is Strange title, Story Kitchen is at the forefront of what's unsurprisingly being labeled the 'golden age' of video game adaptations.
It's a cinematic epoch some believed would never happen — and with good reason. The 1990s and early 2000s are littered with examples of maligned video game movies, including — but by no means limited to — 1993's The Super Mario Bros. Movie, 2005's Doom, and 2003's House of the Dead, the latter of which is one the worst-rated films on popular review aggregation website Rotten Tomatoes.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
With so many entertainment giants failing to understand the source material, the 'videogame adaptation curse' — a phrase Goldberg says "sounds really good when stories are written about it" — became a catch-all term for these and similarly crucified productions. Combine that with the notion that, as Goldberg notes, "Hollywood didn't respect the gaming community, developers, or publishers", and it seemed that video games would forever be viewed as the runt of the visual media landscape.
That was until dj2 Entertainment, the precursor to Story Kitchen co-founded by Johnson and Dan Jevons in 2011, took a leap into the unknown.
The company's primary goal was simple: make Hollywood believe that video game stories were worth telling and investing in. Predictably, Hollywood just didn't see the appeal of turning games into movies or TV shows, and countless rejections followed.
Then came the first Sonic the Hedgehog film. After slowly and methodically earning the trust and respect of SEGA, Johnson convinced the Japanese videogame titan and, later, Paramount Pictures that people wanted to see the Blue Blur star in his own movie.
A few notable setbacks, including the titular character's speedy redesign after fans attacked his initial look following the release of Sonic's first trailer, followed. Fast-forward to early 2020, though, and, despite the pandemic bringing Sonic the Hedgehog's theatrical run to a premature end, the action-adventure comedy grossed $320 million worldwide. On a reported budget of $90 million, it more than recouped its production and marketing costs.
"Dmitri always believed that, with education and respect, a different result [video game adaptations being successful] would occur," Goldberg says. "And, he was right."
'It's a new era — but not every game should be adapted'
A lot has happened in the short time since Sonic's big-screen debut, one that Goldberg describes as "an absolute game changer in the Hollywood ecosystem".
He's not wrong. Film adaptations of other iconic and/or hugely popular game series, including Mario and Minecraft, have earned billions at the global box office. Meanwhile, TV retellings of hit franchises like The Last of Us on HBO Max, and small-screen projects that expand on existing game universes, including Fallout on Prime Video and Netflix's League of Legends animated program Arcane, have drawn universal acclaim, won multiple awards, and introduced millions more people to stories, characters, and worlds they would never have connected with otherwise.
Suffice it to say, the explosion of video game adaptations is indicative of an industry-wide paradigm shift that also allowed dj2 Entertainment to level up its own game. Indeed, by investing the metaphorical skill points into the company's evolution from dj2 Entertainment to Story Kitchen, onboarding industry talents like Elena Sandoval and Timothy I. Stevenson, and signing first-look deals with Amazon in February 2022 and DreamWorks Animation in May 2024, Johnson, Goldberg, and company are well-placed to help create the next wave of gaming transmedia hits.
At the time of publication, around 30 projects, some of which have already found homes and others that'll be shopped around Hollywood, are in the works at Story Kitchen HQ. That might sound a lot, but it's a mere raindrop in the ever-expanding gaming ocean. So, why doesn't Story Kitchen just take a long list of game titles to film studios, TV networks, and the world's best streaming services, and reel them off until one piques their interest?
"It's a new era, but not every game should be adapted," Golberg replies, "And not every game should be adapted right now. We want to be a friend and advocate for the space, though, because we don't see this as a fleeting moment [for video game adaptations]. We think it's got long-term potential, so we're working to ensure that we see that through."
That's not to say Story Kitchen is only focused on adapting the biggest game franchises. AA and indie titles are as much a part of the pitching process, if not more so, than their flashier, big-budget counterparts.
"We don't go into things like 'how many copies did this game sell?'," Johnson says. "We actually despise that question and refuse to answer it at this point. We respond with 'here's why these characters and stories are incredible' and 'here's why it's something we've never seen before'.
"What it really boils down to is passion," he continues. "What are the things that we can't stop thinking about and have to pursue? Once that process starts, we're convinced something has to be made, and that translates into our meetings with other companies. Initially, it might not necessarily make sense to them, but they all want to hear the pitch because it's coming from a place of passion, so most networks and studios are excited when we take something out to them. This isn't a cash-grab — these conversations are happening because we actually care."
Prime-d for more success?
And care, Johnson and Goldberg certainly do. The multi-billion-dollar-spinning Sonic franchise, which currently comprises three movies and a Knuckles TV spin-off on Paramount+, has improved with each new entry.
As of July 2026, a fourth flick is deep in post-production ahead of its March 19, 2027 release date. An untitled Shadow-fronted off-shoot project is also reportedly in the works, though Johnson and Goldberg declined to speak about it because, as Goldberg rightfully points out, "there are levels of NDAs (non-disclosure agreements) we must respect."
Sonic the Hedgehog 4 isn't the only thing that'll roll off the Story Kitchen production line next year. Indeed, two TV projects are expected to make their Prime Video debuts in 2027, the first of which should be a Tomb Raider TV adaptation that Johnson admits has been "years in the making".
Overseen by Fleabag's Phoebe Waller-Bridge, it'll star Sophie Turner as gaming icon Lara Croft. Amazon revealed a perfect first-look shot at Turner in Croft's classic tank top and shorts combo as principal photography got underway in January and, while filming was halted in March due to a "minor injury" sustained by Turner, there's nothing to suggest it'll delay the live-action series' launch.
Thanks to a partnership Story Kitchen established with Tomb Raider custodians and videogame developer Crystal Dynamics during development on Netflix's Tomb Raider animated show, Johnson says "we had a very clear blueprint of how to move together as partners". So, when Amazon, which already had an agreement with Crystal Dynamics to publish future Tomb Raider games, proposed making a live-action TV show, it seemed like a lightning-in-a-bottle moment for all involved.
"Every decision [on the show] is made with Crystal Dynamics' sign-off," Johnson reveals. "So, season one has their blessing and they're very hands-on, but they also respect Phoebe, who's a super-fan, and her perspective of what a live-action Tomb Raider project should be.
"We've actually just started seeing rough cuts, and we were grinning like 10 year olds the entire time. It's going to be good. By the way, we're not the type of people who hype up their own s**t. It's going to be something that your mom can come across and not know that it's based on a 30-year-old videogame franchise. We don't want it to be a niche adaptation just for core fans, who we absolutely honor and will make feel seen. But, if we do our job right, which we're tirelessly trying to do, newcomers will fall love this show just as much as we have."
Life is Strange is a whole other beast. The 2015 episodic adventure game, which tells the story of a high schooler named Max who discovers she can rewind time, is famous for its branching dialog option-based narrative. Ultimately, though, the choices players make during any given playthrough lead to just one of two endings.
In collaboration with its production partners Amazon, Life is Strange franchise publisher Square Enix, and Margot Robbie's LuckyChap Entertainment, then, how is Story Kitchen tackling an evolving tale built on player choice? Furthermore, how did they decide which ending to not only use, but one that, regardless of what happens in Life is Strange: Reunion, aka Deck Nine's 2024 sequel to the first Max-led game, some viewers might interpret as being its true canonical ending?
"We went into Life is Strange knowing that almost all of the major decisions were almost a 50-50 split," Johnson muses. "So, at the start of development, you have to accept that you're not going to make everyone happy. That said, the way we're approaching some of those critical decisions from the games, I think everyone is are going to feel seen, and they're going to be happy and probably emotional [with how things play out]."
It's full steam ahead for Amazon MGM Studios film adaptations of two award-winning and popular Hazelight games in It Takes Two and Split Fiction, too.
Where the latter is concerned, things are still in the early stages of development. However, prolific actor Sydney Sweeney, Wicked duology director Jon M. Chi, and Deadpool writers Rhett Reese and Paul Wernick are, as confirmed by Goldberg, all involved.
"You play these games with your significant other, friend, or a family member, and everyone has their own experience," Goldberg says. It's been such a fun challenge of interpreting that and turning it into a singular shared experience [for viewers].
"Reese and Wernick even insisted on playing the game, and that's how we want our village to be built. You're not required to be a game, but we loved that they wanted to play and experience it together before they committed to this adaptation, and that's going to influence their own script."
As for It Takes Two's film reimagining, it's been over four years since Dwayne Johnson's Seven Bucks production team boarded the Amazon-led project. Speaking to Eurogamer last March, Hazelight creative director Josef Fares, who's known for not mincing his words, took aim at how long it was taking for the film to move forward.
"Hollywood, there's so much b******t," Fares responded when asked for an update. "I think 90 percent of the meetings are actually b******t, and 10 percent are what actually happens. There's a lot of talk, but not a lot of walk. I don't know what's going on. Hopefully something. It would be cool to get something out of it, but my hopes are not so high."
"They are," Johnson says when I ask him if Fares, Hazelight, and Johnson's company are still involved, before he adds: "We're so close to the Hazelight boys at this point that there's a shorthand with them, and the relationship with them and partners on our side... it's all very fluid."
Days of future past
That's just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the 30+ film and TV projects that Story Kitchen plans on delivering.
Johnson and Goldberg want to cover as many genre bases and demographics as possible, too. Film adaptations of three Roblox games — Grow a Garden, Steal a Brainrot, and Jailbreak — are in the works, as are Just Cause, Shinobi, and Ruiner productions with Universal.
Elsewhere, Netflix has signed on to bring Sifu and Kingmakers adaptations to its user base, Lionsgate is hard at work on a Streets of Rage movie, and film reimaginings of hit indie games Disco Elysium and Dredge have also been announced. Additionally, a House of the Dead movie led by The Last of Us and Superman star Isabela Merced — "she's our homie," Johnson beams —is just another of Story Kitchen's other planned projects.
It isn't just video games that are being turned into movies, either. Toys 'R Us, a popular toy retailer in the '80s and '90s that's recently enjoyed a resurgence in the US, is getting the live-action film treatment. Meanwhile, Teddy Ruxpin, an animatronic storytelling bear that was a US bestseller in the '80s, will star in a feature that's been described as 'Sonic the Hedgehog meets Elf'.
"I think it's going to go the same way as Barbie," self-confessed Teddy Ruxpin fan Johnson says in reference to the 2023 megahit starring Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling. "I went into that thinking 'ugh, cash grab' and then had a little tear in the eye by the third act.
"It [the Teddy Ruxpin movie] is funnier than it has any right to be," Johnson continues. "We have ridiculous musical numbers when we shouldn't, and it's so brilliantly bananas that it works. I think it's going to catch people off-guard, and kids are gonna walk out of it wanting a Teddy Ruxpin."
But, back to the games — and, perhaps most importantly, Story Kitchen's mission to create films and TV shows not only based on beloved titles from the past and those that are currently popular, but also those yet to be released.
"We're about to pitch a show based on a game that hasn't even been announced," Goldberg teases as an example of the latter. "And, should nothing change, it'll finally be announced at the 2026 Game Awards. But we're already going to take a fully fleshed, packaged, and scripted drama TV pitch on it to studios next month, so we can move as swiftly as possible once the game is officially revealed."
Whatever that soon-to-be-announced game is, its developer will surely hope it performs as well as 2025 surprise hit Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 did.
The first-ever title from French studio Sandfall Interactive, Clair Obscur unexpectedly dominated the gaming sphere last year. With over eight million copies sold (as of April 2026) and numerous award wins under its belt, it's little wonder that this critically and commercially successful title is being turned into a live-action film. As Johnson is keen to point out, though, the Clair Obscur bandwagon isn't one that Story Kitchen jumped on post-launch.
"As a company, we pride ourselves on not chasing heat," he explains. "We're less likely to pursue a game once it's become an established hit, because we don't ever want to be seen as those people.
"We were actually working with Sandfall as early as 2023," he continues. "We read almost 600 pages of scripts, had raw music files [to listen to], [and] art to look at, so we fell in love with it before we saw any real gameplay. Obviously, you don't know how a game is going to perform, so we went into this knowing that it could be a tough sell. Without the massive success it had, it would've been an uphill battle [to pitch our movie adaptation to studios]. But, as I said earlier, once the passion kicks in, we don't take 'no' for an answer. We were convinced three years ago that this was something to be excited about, and... that's all we can say about it right now."
If there's one thing I took from my chat with Johnson and Goldberg, it's this: they genuinely care about what they're doing. Like, a lot. They don't phone in their work, nor did they lazily trot out stock responses to my questions. They are completely committed to telling the world that games are not only great, but that their stories are also worth translating and telling in other mediums.
There's so much more that Story Kitchen wants to accomplish, though. Even with the abundance of productions already on their plate, Johnson and Goldberg have ambitions on adapting even more franchises for the big and small screen. Their dream projects? Mega Man and — surprisingly — Bad Dudes for Johnson, and Nintendo's iconic sci-fi franchise Metroid for Goldberg.
But such wish fulfillment must wait for another day. As we approach the tail-end of what was supposed to be an hour-long interview, Goldberg reveals that he and Johnson are being summoned by Amazon for a meeting — the contents of which he can't disclose.
It's a sign of just how busy the pair have become, but they wouldn't have it any other way. After all, Story Kitchen is no ordinary passion project — it's reshaping the multimedia landscape as we know it.
"We were recently looking back on our list of games to consider for last year's BAFTA Game Awards," Johnson says, "And there's one from a tiny Australian team called The Drifter that, after I came across it in 2025, I couldn't stop gushing about. Anyway, we ended up tracking them down and, in the very first meeting we had with another studio, we were able to find a home for this indie game in the form of a big theatrical movie.
"That wouldn't have been possible five, six years ago, and that's why we're enjoying this moment now. Step one was getting rid of this silly notion that games are cursed. Now, step two, and we say this with a straight face, you'll see Oscars, Emmys, and BAFTAs being won by movies and TV shows that are based on games. That's our next mission: proving that videogames are art. The stories being told, the characters they contain... they're no different to a New York Times best-selling book — and we're ready to show the world why."

 Une barre Google intégrée, mais jamais imposée
Placée juste au-dessus des apps favorites, telles les messages, le navigateur ou encore l’appareil photo, cette nouvelle zone rappelle immédiatement l’organisation des smartphones Pixel. Elle permet de lancer rapidement une recherche Google sans ouvrir d’app ni ajouter manuellement un widget.
Pour autant, Samsung ne copie pas complètement la formule de Mountain View. Sur les appareils compatibles, l’utilisateur peut afficher uniquement Google, conserver le moteur Finder de Samsung ou réunir les deux outils. Il reste également possible de désactiver entièrement cette zone, qui laisse alors place à l’indicateur servant à naviguer entre les différentes pages de l’écran d’accueil.
Il suffit pour cela de maintenir le doigt sur une zone vide, d’ouvrir les paramètres de l’écran d’accueil puis de sélectionner le menu consacré à l’affichage de la recherche. Les boutons permettent ensuite de modifier la présentation en quelques secondes.
Cette nouveauté semble pour l’instant surtout active sur les Galaxy Z Fold 8 et Z Fold 8 Ultra et n’apparaît pas encore systématiquement sur le Z Flip 8, ni sur le Galaxy S26 Ultra équipé de la quatrième bêta de One UI 9. Samsung pourrait donc encore modifier sa disponibilité avant la sortie officielle de ses pliants, prévue le 12 août, puis l’étendre aux autres terminaux compatibles lors du déploiement de l’interface.
One UI 9 cache aussi plusieurs options pratiques
La recherche n’est pas la seule évolution observée. Android Authority rélève qu'il est désormais possible de couper l’accès au réseau pour certaines apps, une option utile pour mieux contrôler les données mobiles et la confidentialité. Les paramètres destinés aux développeurs accueillent également des réglages plus précis pour la protection du son joué en arrière-plan, une fonction rendue possible par Android 17.
Enfin, Bixby pourra être lancé grâce à un geste, sans prononcer la commande habituelle ni utiliser de raccourci. Il faudra approcher le smartphone à moins de cinq centimètres de la bouche. Le système restera désactivé lorsque l’assistant répond déjà à une demande ou lorsqu’un contenu multimédia est en cours de lecture.
Les nouveaux pliants tant attendus du géant sud-coréen sont d'ores et déjà disponibles en précommande et seront les premiers à profiter de la version finalisée de One UI 9. La gamme Galaxy S26 et Galaxy Z de la génération précédente devraient logiquement suivre.
