articles.title: Les arnaques téléphoniques du futur sont là : les faux livreurs se mettent aux notes vocales
articles.text:
Les arnaques téléphoniques du futur sont là : les faux livreurs se mettent aux notes vocales
L’arnaque au faux colis vit avec son temps : les escrocs intègrent désormais des photos et des messages vocaux pour tromper la vigilance des usagers. Une menace de plus en plus sophistiquée qui invite à une vigilance accrue.
Vous en avez forcément reçu un jour ou l’autre : les arnaques aux fausses livraisons de colis à votre domicile. La mécanique est bien rodée : le faux livreur, qui ne mentionne jamais votre nom ni celui du service d’expédition, vous indique ne pas avoir pu déposer votre colis en votre absence. Il vous propose donc de reprogrammer la livraison, et vous fournit un lien vous permettant - moyennant finance - de choisir une nouvelle date vous convenant davantage. C’est bien sûr entièrement faux : aucun service, de La Poste à Mondial Relay, en passant par DHL et consorts, ne vous facture la reprogrammation de la réception.
Les arnaques donnent de la voix
L’arnaque est connue, mais elle passe actuellement à la vitesse supérieure. Car désormais, le traditionnel SMS est assorti d’une photographie… et d’un vocal. Le principe est toujours le même, à ce détail près que le message est désormais bien plus détaillé, et pourrait berner un peu plus facilement qu’à l’accoutumée. Même si les smartphones disposent de filtres anti-phishing de plus en plus performants, ce type de messages passe le plus souvent au travers des mailles du filet : nous vous invitons donc à la vigilance. Dans notre cas, il suffit ainsi de regarder attentivement la photographie accompagnant le message reçu pour constater que l’étiquette collée sur le colis ne porte ni notre nom, ni notre adresse... et que cette même photo traîne partout sur le Net.
Rappelons qu’il existe de plus en plus d’outils, le plus souvent basés sur l’intelligence artificielle, pour filtrer au mieux les messages et les appels indésirables.Les systèmes iOS d'Apple ou l'application Google Messages (déployée par défaut sur la quasi-totalité des smartphones Android, y compris chez Samsung qui a remplacé son app maison) s'occupent ainsi de filtrer la majorité des SMS suspects. L’enjeu concerne en outre les appels : sur les Pixel de Google, par exemple, il suffit d’activer l’option de filtrage du spam dans l’application Téléphone ; il est même possible d’appuyer sur la commande “Filtrer l’appel” à la réception d’une communication suspecte, afin que l’IA se charge de vérifier à votre place l’identité de l’appelant. Opérateurs et interfaces constructeurs multiplient ainsi les initiatives pour bloquer les tentatives d’arnaque avant qu’elles n’atteignent l’utilisateur, mais la solution la plus efficace pour éviter ces pièges reste encore d’en connaître les rouages.

articles.title: Pixel 11 specs and price leak with no surprises
articles.text:
Android Headlines claims to have the specs and price for the entire Pixel 11 lineup. What the site shared basically lines up with everything else that we’ve heard in the lead-up to the August 12th event. The Pixel 11 is expected to get a $100 price hike, starting at $899, but will come with 256GB of storage instead of 128GB in the base model. While the entire lineup will sport the new Tensor G6 and Titan M3 chips, the base model Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL are both getting that rumored RAM cut to just 12GB, along with price increases to $1,099 and $1,299, respectively.
Pixel 11 specs and price leak with no surprises
More confirmation that price hikes and RAM cuts are coming our way.
The Pixel 11 will supposedly ditch the telephoto lens and settle for a dual rear camera setup instead. The pro models appear like they’ll keep the same camera setup from the Pixel 10 lineup. The displays also seem to be largely unchanged from the previous generation. The Pixel 11 Pro Fold wasn’t immune to RAMageddon, either, and will also start with 12GB of RAM and a new price of $1,899.

articles.title: Health, safety, AI: test your business creativity with Edition 243 of our weekly quiz!
articles.text:
Health, safety, AI: test your business creativity with Edition 243 of our weekly quiz!
This insightful feature from YourStory tests and strengthens your business acumen! Here are 5 questions to kick off this 243rd quiz. Ready?
Lateral Sparks, the weekly quiz from YourStory, tests your domain knowledge, business acumen, and lateral thinking skills (see the previous edition here). In this 243rd edition of the quiz, we present issues tackled by real-life entrepreneurs in their startup journeys.
What would you do if you were in their shoes? At the end of the quiz, you will find out what the entrepreneurs and innovators themselves actually did. Would you do things differently?
Check out YourStory’s Book Review section as well, with takeaways from over 355 titles on creativity and entrepreneurship, and our weekend PhotoSparks section on creativity in the arts.
Q1: Medical prescriptions
Patients who need medicines often need to visit multiple pharmacies to complete a prescription, since not each small store may have all the needed products. What’s a more efficient solution here?
Q2: Inspection of interiors
Inspecting the inside of a ship's hull, fuel tank, or nuclear reactor is a dangerous job. How can safety be improved here, along with asset productivity?
Q3: Holiday planning
Planning a holiday often involves static PDFs, endless follow-ups, and mark-ups that seem to appear only later. How can these pain points be resolved?
Q4: Waste management
Many countries generate million tonnes of waste every year, and much of it is dumped or burned. What’s a more sustainable and yet financially viable approach here?
Q5: Safe and sustainable livelihoods
Many women labourers in the tobacco sector such as bidi rolling report chronic respiratory conditions, eye damage, and even cancer. What better alternatives can be designed in this regard?
Answers!
Congratulations on having come this far! But there’s more to come – answers to these five questions (below), as well as links to articles with more details on the entrepreneurs’ solutions. Happy reading, happy learning – and happy creating!
A1: Medical prescriptions
Founded by Aman Priyadarshi, Plazza tries to ensure that medicines prescribed by doctors are actually available when patients need them. Its AI-based inventory planning predicts local demand and recommends which medicines each store should stock.
AI helps continuously analyse prescribing patterns at the neighbourhood level, allowing every store to maintain a tailored inventory. Read more here about its model, and its Series A funding round co-led by Accel, Elevation Capital, and Nexus Venture Partners.
A2: Inspection of interiors
Founded by Vishrant Dave, Prateesh Awasthi and Ayush Ranjan, Armatrix is a deeptech startup with robots that have snake-like arms. They are flexible enough to thread through tight, twisting spaces that a rigid industrial robot cannot reach.
AI helps with real-time path planning and digital-twin simulation, so the arm can adapt as it moves through unpredictable industrial layouts. Read more here about the robotic maintenance market for shipyards, refineries and defense areas, and the startup’s seed round of founding.
A3: Holiday planning
Founded by Kshitij Chaudhary, 30 Sundays aims to make travel services honest and effortless, via customised trips and transparent information. It has embedded AI across sales, lead qualification, itinerary creation, follow-ups, and reservations
It also keeps the human in the loop to customise and support the traveller’s journey. Read more here about this holiday planning and booking platform, and its Series A funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners.
A4: Waste management
Nearly 40% of waste in a city like Bengaluru originates from tech parks and bulk generators, according to Wilma Rodrigues, Chief Transformation Officer at Saahas Zero Waste. It operates a zero-waste program for such bulk generators.
It also has an extended producer responsibility vertical covering plastic and electronic waste, and a closed loop retail arm that sells recovered products back to communities. Read more here about how the company diverted 40,000 tonnes last year across recycling, composting, biogas, and reuse channels, claiming a 96% landfill diversion rate.
A5: Safe and sustainable livelihoods
Founded by Karunya Gunavathy, Kottravai helps women labourers transition from bidi rolling to sustainable livelihoods. It trains and employs women to make coconut-shell, banana-fibre, terracotta, and food products.
It has also partnered with Crazy Coconut, a sustainable, eco-friendly brand, to train the women for three months. Read more here about its four production clusters, emerging units for aromatic candles and wellness products, and plans for corporate gifting.
YourStory has also published the pocketbook ‘Proverbs and Quotes for Entrepreneurs: A World of Inspiration for Startups’ as a creative and motivational guide for innovators.

articles.title: Claude Mythos: Anthropic-KI knackt Verschlüsselungsstandard – was das bedeutet
articles.text:
Anthropics Claude Mythos knackt Verschlüsselungsstandard – was das für die Internetsicherheit bedeutet
Als der Verschlüsselungsstandard AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) im Jahr 2001 eingeführt wurde, galt er als nahezu unknackbar. Die Anthropic-KI Claude Mythos Preview soll diesen Algorithmus jetzt geknackt haben. Allerdings nicht in der Vollversion, die zum Schutz von Internetverbindungen, drahtlosen Netzwerken und der Speicherung von Daten eingesetzt wird.
Mythos knackt Verschlüsselungsstandard
Ähnliche kryptografische Algorithmen kommen bei der Verschlüsselung von Online-Banktransaktionen ebenso zum Einsatz wie in der privaten Kommunikation oder bei der Übermittlung von Staatsgeheimnissen. Wie die New York Times (NYT) berichtet, hat Claude Mythos Preview Schwachstellen in einer abgeschwächten AES-Version ausgemacht. Dabei soll die KI 200- bis 1.000-mal schneller gewesen sein als menschliche Kryptografie-Expert:innen zuvor.
Während für aktuell eingesetzte Verschlüsselungsalgorithmen keine akute Gefahr besteht, warnen Beobachter:innen vor den rasanten Fortschritten der KI-Modelle im Bereich Kryptografie. Die langfristigen Auswirkungen auf traditionell eingesetzte Schutzmaßnahmen im Internet könnten erheblich sein, wie es bei der NYT heißt.
Kryptografie: Rasante KI-Entwicklung
So erklärte Anthropic-Forscher Nicholas Carlini, dass KI-Modelle noch 2025 nicht annähernd so leistungsfähig gewesen seien wie heute. Sie hätten Probleme, die er schon im Alter von 16 Jahren lösen konnte, nicht lösen können. „Aber jetzt betreiben sie modernste Forschung, die auf diesem Gebiet zuvor nicht entdeckt werden konnte“, so der Forscher, der früher in Googles KI-Abteilung tätig war.
Mythos soll den Angriff auf den Verschlüsselungsstandard zudem fast vollständig autonom entwickelt haben. Im Anschluss daran sollen zwei menschliche Forscher:innen fast einen Monat daran gearbeitet haben, die vorgeschlagene Methode zu überprüfen.
Cybersecurity: KI versus Quantencomputer
Schon länger warnen Expert:innen davor, dass Quantencomputer künftig in der Lage sein könnten, moderne Verschlüsselungsstandards zu knacken. Das wiederum hätte tiefgreifende Folgen für die digitale Privatsphäre sowie für die nationale Sicherheit. Die aktuellen KI-Fortschritte lassen jetzt Bedenken aufkommen, dass der mathematische Kern von Internet-Sicherheitsstandards auch unabhängig von Quantencomputern verwundbar sein könnte.
Neben der AES-Attacke soll Mythos laut Anthropic zudem einen weiteren verbesserten Angriff auf ein anderes kryptografisches System namens Hawk orchestriert haben. Hawk soll eigentlich sowohl gegen traditionelle als auch gegen Quantencomputer-Angriffe sicher sein und gilt als Kandidat für einen neuen Verschlüsselungsstandard des National Institute of Standards and Technology.
Schwachstelle in Post-Quanten-Standard
Das Post-Quanten-Verfahren ist über Jahre getestet worden. Die Hawk-Entwickler:innen selbst haben derweil bestätigt, dass die von Mythos gewählte Angriffsmethode funktionieren könnte. Das wiederum könnte bedeuten, dass KI-Modelle wie Claude Mythos Preview künftig auch bei der Entwicklung solcher kryptografischer Verfahren hilfreich sein könnten, um entsprechende Schwachstellen zu identifizieren.

articles.title: This $10 bundle of 100+ DRM-free games means to support laid-off game developers
articles.text:
Why it matters: The video game industry has seen a historic wave of layoffs in recent years, with thousands of workers impacted in the last few weeks alone. To support some of the developers affected, indie game storefront itch.io is collaborating with an industry union to sell a collection of over 100 heavily discounted games.
The Game Industry Hardship Fund bundle is live on itch.io through August 13. The collection currently includes more than 100 indie titles, along with a few soundtracks, assets, and other materials, all for just $10.
All proceeds go toward the Game Industry Hardship Fund, which the United Videogame Workers union has promoted amid repeated massive rounds of layoffs throughout the industry. US and Canada-based developers can add more games to the bundle, so it will likely keep growing over the next couple of weeks. Customers can download any games added after their purchase at no additional cost.
The bundle mostly consists of small indie titles, but it also includes a few gems with positive Steam ratings. Examples include A Short Hike (MSRP: $8), Dungeon Bodega Simulator ($10), Eldritch ($15), Neon Struct ($18), Holedown ($10), and more.
Although games purchased through the bundle do not activate on Steam, downloads via the itch app or website are DRM-free. Many of the included titles also natively support macOS and Linux, and items from bundles appear in a separate tab on itch.io's library section.
The Game Industry Hardship Fund aims to support the thousands of employees laid off over the past several years amid the industry's pandemic-era overinvestment. The bundle page cites reports claiming that 33% of the industry's workers have experienced job losses in the past two years.
Publishers have announced layoffs impacting thousands this summer alone. France's video game union, the Syndicat des travailleurs et travailleuses du jeu vidéo, announced a strike after more than 1,000 workers lost their jobs. Bungie also recently eliminated roughly 400 positions after pivoting away from Destiny 2.
Ubisoft laid off 51 workers at its Barcelona studio shortly after the massively successful launch of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, a game the office helped develop, and MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy recently faced protests from laid-off workers in the UK while flying in fans for playtesting.
Most notably, Microsoft recently eliminated 1,600 positions, with another 1,600 employees set to be laid off over the course of this year. In a bid to "reset" Xbox, the company let go of five studios and began reorganizing its gaming business. That move has already prompted further layoffs at the now-independent Double Fine.

articles.title: Cómo extraer las ideas clave de un libro en formato ePub con Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM)
articles.text:
NotebookLM, ahora rebautizada como Gemini Notebook, es una de esas aplicaciones que te permiten aprovechar mejor el tiempo, sacarle más partido a tus notas y documentos y, en definitiva, darle utilidad a eso que llamamos inteligencia artificial. En vez de pedirle a Gemini que busque algo en internet, a través de Gemini Notebook puedes hacer búsquedas en tus anotaciones y archivos, ordenarlos, procesarlos y utilizarlos en tu día a día.
Precisamente, una de las muchas ventajas de Gemini Notebook es que es compatible con varios formatos. Es decir, que puedes procesar videos de YouTube y enlaces a artículos, imágenes en varios formatos, documentos de texto, presentaciones, hojas de cálculo y un largo etcétera. Esto facilita mucho las cosas si tienes varios contenidos desperdigados y necesitas darles forma para estudiar o aprender. Gracias a esta app puedes convertir textos, videos e imágenes en resúmenes, preguntas y respuestas, pódcasts, vídeos y otros formatos más cómodos de digerir.
En este artículo vamos a centrarnos en un formato de texto muy popular. No tanto como el PDF que abunda en todas partes, pero casi. Se trata del formato ePub, utilizado en libros electrónicos. Así que si tienes en tus manos, o en tu dispositivo de lectura, un libro de lectura, manual, libro de texto o un farragoso documento en ePub, puedes pedirle ayuda a Gemini Notebook para que extraiga aquello que necesites. Aunque, claro está, el libro o documento deberá estar libre de DRM o protecciones de lectura para que Gemini pueda leerlo.
Los límites de Gemini Notebook
Antes de empezar, conviene recordar que NotebookLM, ahora Gemini Notebook, tiene ciertos límites en su versión gratuita. Esto significa que si, como la mayoría, tienes una cuenta básica de Google para trastear con esta app, te interesará saber hasta dónde puedes llegar. En el caso que nos ocupa, es decir, trabajar con documentos ePub, te interesa saber esto. Gemini Notebook permite:
- Subir fuentes, como un ePub, de hasta 500.000 palabras.
- O, bien, de hasta 200 MB de tamaño.
- Puedes realizar 50 chats por día.
- Crear hasta 3 resúmenes de audio por día.
- Hasta 3 resúmenes de video por día.
- Puedes pedir hasta 10 informes por día.
- Puedes pedir hasta 10 tarjetas o flashcards por día.
- Permite generar hasta 10 cuestionarios por día.
- Permite generar hasta 10 mapas mentales por día.
- La función de Deep Research se puede usar 10 veces por mes.
Para hacerte una idea, Don Quijote de la Mancha supera las 400.000 palabras. Y Guerra y Paz de León Tolstói tiene más de 560.000 palabras. Pero no suele ser así. Moby Dick, de Herman Melville, tiene más de 200.000 palabras, pero está lejos del límite que admite NotebookLM. Por lo general, una novela media actual suele tener entre 70.000 y 100.000 palabras. Y si hablamos de libros de texto, un libro especializado o universitario suele superar las 80.000 palabras, pero sin llegar a la cifra límite de Gemini Notebook.
Cómo extraer el contenido de un ePub con Gemini Notebook
Si ya estás familiarizado con Gemini Notebook, antes NotebookLM, sabrás que esta aplicación se basa en cuadernos. Así que para no mezclar fuentes y centrarnos en un documento ePub, lo primero que haremos es crear un nuevo cuaderno. Recuerda que esta app está disponible vía web y en app para iOS y para Android. Así que ve a Mis cuadernos y haz clic o pulsa el botón Crear nuevo o Crear cuaderno.
Al abrirse el nuevo cuaderno, lo primero que aparecerá en pantalla es una ventana flotante invitándote a subir fuentes. O a buscarlas en internet. En esta ocasión, vamos a procesar un libro ePub muy popular y del que queremos extraer información, citas o pasajes concretos. Incluso enseñanzas filosóficas, tal vez. Así que arrastra y suelta el archivo ePub al campo correspondiente o haz clic en Subir archivos y elige el ePub que tienes a mano.
Al cabo de unos segundos, Gemini Notebook habrá procesado tu libro o documento ePub. Y rellenará por ti el campo Título del cuaderno que creaste. En el caso que nos ocupa, en el Chat verás un breve resumen sobre el documento ePub que subiste. Así como varias preguntas para que empieces a preguntarle a Gemini Notebook por el contenido del documento.
Qué puedes hacer con un ePub en NotebookLM
Una vez has subido un ePub a Gemini Notebook, ¿qué puedes hacer con su contenido? Lo primero de todo, puedes leerlo directamente de ahí. Si pulsas o haces clic en la fuente, verás que el contenido está disponible. No es que NotebookLM sea el mejor lector de libros ePub, pero te permite acceder a su contenido si no tienes ninguna aplicación compatible a mano. Además, tener acceso directo al contenido te permitirá comparar lo que genere Gemini con el contenido original.
Pero lo que seguramente querrás es exprimir el contenido del documento ePub. Tanto si se trata de un libro de ficción como si es un manual o un libro académico, a través del chat de Gemini, integrado en Gemini Notebook, podrás conversar con el documento. Por ejemplo, haciéndole preguntas concretas. Ejemplo. Queremos leer La Odisea de Homero aprovechando el éxito de la película homónima de Christopher Nolan. Pero antes, queremos prepararnos una guía de lectura. Y empezaremos preguntándole por los personajes que aparecen. Gemini Notebook hará una lista, organizando los personajes por afinidad y los describirá con citas directas del libro. Solo tienes que pulsar las citas para leerlas tú mismo.
En definitiva, a través del chat puedes preguntar cualquier cosa. NotebookLM lo buscará directamente en el documento ePub que le has facilitado. Si le pides algo que no está, te dirá que no lo encuentra. Así que deberás facilitarle las fuentes donde buscar. Por ejemplo, pongamos que quieres asociar los nombres de los personajes con los actores que los interpretan. Tendrás que añadir a Fuentes un enlace a la ficha de la película para que así Gemini haga su parte. O pedirle explícitamente que busque en internet.
Aprender, estudiar o disfrutar de un libro
Además del chat, que te permite obtener respuestas a partir del documento ePub, en el panel Studio de Gemini Notebook encontrarás varios formatos que puedes usar para extraer información útil de documentos ePub y convertirla en un resumen de audio o pódcast, un resumen en vídeo, un informe detallado, un cuestionario para saber si has entendido bien el libro o documento, un mapa mental para ayudarte con personajes, lugares o eventos, tarjetas didácticas y mucho más.
Es decir, que si necesitas estudiar el contenido de un libro de texto, con NotebookLM podrás hacerlo cómodamente y automatizando el proceso de resumir o extraer el contenido más importante. Y si se trata de un libro de ficción, con estas herramientas puedes crear tus propias guías de lectura que te ayudarán durante la lectura del libro. En especial si se trata de narraciones extensas con muchos personajes, fechas, eventos o lugares mencionados.
Y lo mejor de todo es que puedes exportar todos esos documentos generados con NotebookLM para consultarlos en tu lector de libros electrónicos, en tu tableta o en tu teléfono móvil. Así podrás comparar el documento ePub con el contenido generado con IA y extraer tus propias conclusiones.

articles.title: Hora de trocar o relógio: smartwatches em promoção na Amazon
articles.text:
Se você está pensando em colocar um smartwatch no pulso — ou presentear alguém —, a Amazon reúne agora uma boa seleção de modelos em oferta. São opções para diferentes perfis, desde quem quer algo simples e funcional até quem busca recursos mais avançados, como IA integrada e tela AMOLED. Confira três destaques que vale a pena conhecer.
Haiz My Watch I Fit – 44mm com proteção IP67
O Haiz HZ-ZL02D é uma escolha prática para quem quer entrar no mundo dos smartwatches sem complicação. Com caixa de 44mm e certificação IP67, ele resiste a respingos e situações do dia a dia sem drama. Monitora atividades físicas e notificações, tudo com visual discreto na cor preta.
Ver na Amazon →
PEJE Smartwatch – Chamadas Bluetooth, IP68 e mais de 123 modos esportivos
O smartwatch da PEJE se destaca pela versatilidade. Faz chamadas via Bluetooth diretamente pelo pulso, tem tela touch HD de 1,28 polegadas e proteção IP68, que garante resistência à água mais robusta. Acompanha pulseira extra e aguenta de 5 a 7 dias com uma única carga — além de suportar mais de 123 modos esportivos para quem leva a atividade física a sério. Funciona com iOS e Android.
Ver na Amazon →

A tela AMOLED de 1,43 polegadas entrega imagem nítida e vibrante, e o conjunto inclui monitoramento de frequência cardíaca, qualidade do sono e suporte a 100 modalidades esportivas. A certificação 3ATM garante resistência à água, e o kit vem com duas pulseiras — grafite e azul — para variar o visual. Compatível com iOS e Android.
Ver na Amazon →
Ofertas assim costumam mudar rápido na Amazon — tanto em disponibilidade quanto nas condições. Se algum desses modelos chamou a atenção, vale acessar agora para garantir o melhor momento de compra.

articles.title: Plug-in batteries will be the next ‘game changer’ for home energy, experts predict — here’s why they’ll be ‘bigger than solar’ and could save you up to £400 a year
articles.text:
‘Plug-in batteries are the real game-changer’: I talked to Octopus Energy and Anker about the home energy revolution than could soon be 'bigger than solar' for millions
The next 'air fryer' moment? Don't bet against it
It's typical, you wait for ages for a home energy revolution and then two come along at once — or at least that's what appears to be happening in the UK.
You've probably heard about the first landmark moment. 'Plug-in solar' hit the headlines last week when the UK government announced that small, solar panel kits that feed electricity directly into your standard home socket can legally go on sale from August 27.
That's a big deal. Plug-in solar means that millions of people who have traditionally been locked out of generating their own clean electricity — renters and flat owners, for example — will be able to join the residential solar party, albeit on a more modest scale.
But not everyone was celebrating wildly with biodegradable confetti. Across the country, energy nerds bemoaned one glaring omission in the government's new legislation — a legal pathway for 'plug-in batteries'.
For many, these small home batteries — think a mini Tesla Powerwall that plugs into a standard wall socket — are the "real game-changer", as Octopus Energy and Anker both described them to me. That's because they promise to be even more accessible than plug-in solar and act as a money-saving brain that makes your home an active part of a smarter UK electricity grid.
Bold claims indeed, so I spoke to four of the biggest players in this burgeoning space — Anker, Octopus Energy, EcoFlow and Windfall Energy — along with the UK government to find out when plug-in batteries might be coming, what the drawbacks are and, most importantly, how much you can really expect to save...
When are they coming?
The main premise of plug-in home batteries, like the Windfall Battery above, is simple — they charge automatically using cheap-rate electricity (usually at night), then discharge that electricity around your home during more expensive peak-rate periods. "Even without solar panels, a plug-in battery delivers meaningful savings through grid arbitrage alone," Anker Solix's EU CEO, Kelvin Cao, tells me. Savings estimates range from between £100-£400 per year, depending on your battery, tariff and usage.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Great, so when exactly will they become legal in the UK? When I asked the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), the official answer was predictably vague. "We are rolling out plug-in solar, which will be quickest to reach the market — helping to bring bills down for good," a DESNZ spokesperson said.
Plug-in batteries are smart energy storage devices that connect to your home's electrical network through a standard wall socket, without any professional installation. They automatically charge from the grid when electricity is cheap and release energy back into your home during peak-rate hours to cut your energy bills. They can work on their own or alongside solar. While they're not currently legal in the UK, that could potentially change soon.
The DESNZ told me its main focus right now is plug-in solar kits and that plug-in batteries have their own technical and regulatory hurdles, which it's currently investigating. Still, there are hopes that grid-connected batteries that plug into your wall socket could be legalised within the next year.
Several big players are quietly preparing plug-in batteries — which are already available in countries like Germany — for a UK launch. Anker, for example, has built a page for its Solix Solarbank 4 that clearly explains the benefits of plug-in batteries, should they become legalised in the UK. "We are eager to support the rise of the plug-in era in the UK and become part of its evolving energy landscape," Anker Solix's EU CEO, Kelvin Cao, told me.
Octopus Energy also recently announced that its new plug-in Nook Cube battery will go on sale sometime in 2027. More confident on the timescale is Windfall Energy, a London startup that's designed the best-looking piece of home energy kit I've seen for a while, the Windfall Battery.
"I was at a roundtable with a Minister of Parliament about a month ago, and everyone there was pretty much calling for batteries to come hot on the heels of plug-in solar," Windfall Energy's co-founder Rob Hallifax told me.
So when is Windfall expecting to start selling its 2.5 kWh home battery, which has an RRP of £1,200 and had previously been slated to ship in autumn? "Winter is more likely now. We want to time it with the plug-in regulations. It’s looking like the end of this year, early next," he added.
Why now?
You'll probably have noticed that the UK has been on an energy rollercoaster that can technically be described as 'not fun'.
Back in the late 1990s and early 2000s, inflation-adjusted gas and electricity prices were actually stable or even falling. But there was a huge spike for both in early 2022 and they've never returned to pre-energy crisis levels. Electricity prices are still 13% higher than in January 2020, according to the UK government, and they continue to move in the wrong direction.
Plug-in batteries promise to be, if not a cure, then at least a much-needed pain killer for our energy bills headache. They're emerging now because of three things — falling prices for lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) batteries, the easing of electrical regulations in some regions (Germany created the world's first dedicated plug-in solar product standard in late 2025), and soaring wholesale gas prices that are reflected in the graph above.
As Anker's Kelvin Cao tells me, this has "reshaped how European households think about electricity". Unfortunately, that double-digit increase in energy prices is also "unlikely to come down any time soon". That's why Germany started the trend, and the UK is (hopefully) about to follow.
So how exactly do plug-in batteries save you money? "There’s two parts to the price saving," Windfall Energy's co-founder Rob Hallifax tells me. "The simple one is just the price arbitrage. So if you're paying 10p at night and 30p in the day for electricity per kilowatt hour, then you buy it at 10p, use it when it's 30p, you're saving 20p per kilowatt hour," he says.
That part's pretty simple — with the Windfall Battery, this 'buy low, use when prices skyrocket' approach makes up about £168 of its promised £250 per year savings. But there are also extra savings from getting your plug-in battery really singing in tune with the electricity network.
The UK grid acts a bit like a giant smart thermostat, signaling when the system needs more or less electricity, and the idea is that energy suppliers could follow by telling plug-in home batteries when to charge and discharge. Smaller plug-in batteries would likely be capped at an 800W output (without professional installation), so wouldn't be exporting power to the grid. But they could still play a role in balancing demand.
This makes tariffs the second big factor in the money-saving potential of plug-in batteries — and that's something Octopus Energy has been a UK leader in.
"The energy sector overall has not really embraced the fact that you can just offer different types of products to different types of consumer customer groups," Alex Schoch, Group Director for Flexibility at Octopus Energy, tells me. "Of our eight million customers, 1.2 million are on some kind of smart tariff," he adds.
Octopus Energy told me there could potentially be dedicated plug-in battery tariffs or bolt-ons for existing ones. If you've ever been baffled by choosing the right energy tariff, this could also get simpler thanks to plug-in batteries.
"I equate it to the evolution of mobile phone plans," Octopus Energy's Alex Schoch tells me. "First, they were incredibly generic. Then they got so complicated that Carphone Warehouse came into being just to explain the complexity. And now we’re at a stage where we create hyper-personalised plans based on your needs as a consumer. We’re on that same journey when it comes to energy".
But doesn't this also demand a lot of trust in energy companies? Windfall Energy's Rob Hallifax agrees, but thinks falling bills will ultimately convince consumers. "It's their (consumers'] battery, they're in control of it, but the energy company is controlling it a bit to help them maximize the savings," he says. "The consumer has to trust that the energy company is doing this to save them money, and I think that will come when they see their bills go down," he adds.
What's the catch?
Clearly, plug-in batteries won't be a magic wand for everyone's bills, even if the batteries could be subsidised or even given away for free by the UK government to lower-income households, as the i Paper reported recently (the DESNZ declined to comment on this when I asked).
For most plug-in batteries, the payback period (the time it takes for savings to cover the cost of the battery) is expected to be around 3-4 for years, so not exactly a financial quick fix. The Windfall Battery promises annual savings of £250 (with an RRP of £1,200), while Anker tells me that the larger Solix Solarbank 4 on a dynamic tariff like Octopus Agile could save you just under £400 per year. That battery has no UK price yet, but retails for €1,999 in Europe (around £1,700).
The other concern raised by skeptics is safety. Is allowing potentially millions of households to connect batteries to their electricity networks without professional installation really a good idea? Windfall Energy's Rob Hallifax acknowledges that it's an understandable concern. "People see a battery, and they think of scooters and fires, and there some valid concerns. Obviously, safety is critically important, and just one battery fire would be one too many," he says.
"But modern batteries are generally extremely safe,' he adds. "There are some studies out of Germany now where they compare batteries to EVs and other home appliances. One headline is that they’re typically about as safe as a washing machine," he adds. The other common comparison is with fan heaters, which are legal in the UK but carry a higher risk of 'user error' incidents than plug-in batteries.
Still, the added complexities of grid-charging batteries mean some agree with the UK government's top-dipping approach. EcoFlow, one of the biggest global players in home batteries, is among them. "We're aware and completely understand that these things take time," Lorna Wallace-Smith (EcoFlow's Head of UK PR) told me. "The fact that they were able to move forward with at least one step is is great" she added.
But hasn't Germany's rapid adoption of both plug-in solar and home batteries shown it's safe? "I think that's something we should learn from, as well as not fast-track into something without knowing it's absolutely built for UK homes," she added.
Could they outshine solar?
Despite these concerns, it seems clear that plug-in batteries have the potential to eclipse the more complex plug-in solar kits in the UK — and most of the experts I spoke to agreed.
"They are the fundamental great equalizer," says Octopus' Alex Schoch on plug-in batteries. "It’s such an important thing for renters because you can then take it with you to your next place," he adds.
"I think in the next couple of years we will see plug-in batteries really be the transformational scale deployment. I think it has the potential of being a mass market thing even faster than solar," he predicts.
Windfall Energy's Rob Hallifax naturally agrees when comparing plug-in batteries to their solar equivalent. "There are 28 million homes in the UK and about half of them are either rented or flats and small homes. So more people could get them, millions, and there’s also the benefit to the grid and to the system," he says.
There is one other obvious comparison with an accessory that's cheap, easy to use and promises to save you money. "We use air fryers as quite a good example. Four or five years ago they just came from nowhere and suddenly half the country has one," he says.
But wouldn't an 'air fryer' level of popularity also cause a problem for plug-in batteries? After all, a lot of their money-saving potential comes from tapping into today's so-called 'delta' between cheap-rate and peak-rate electricity. If plug-in batteries help to solve the imbalance of today's grid demand — and tariffs are adjusted to reflect that — could that start to diminish their savings potential?
"I think yes and no," says Windfall Energy's Rob Hallifax. "So maybe in 50 years the whole grid will be sort of perfect. I think the fundamental thing is that if you have renewable generation, that's always going to be variable. That's just the nature of the world. And so somewhere in the system, storage has to be part of it," he adds.
Octopus Energy's Alex Schoch agrees that such a change would be a long way off. "In theory, yes." he says in response to my pessimistic scenario. "But I would actually say the length of time here is measured in decades, not in a sub-decade quantum," he adds.
However, he does note that a similar process is already happening. "We've had such an explosion of solar in the UK over the last few years that now during Spring and Summer, a lot of the cheapest wholesale price electricity times are actually late morning, early afternoon, mid afternoon, and no longer overnight," he notes.
Charging ahead
The legalisation of plug-in batteries in the UK appears to be a matter of 'when' not 'if'. As a flat owner in south west London with no roof and only a limited appetite for plug-in solar, I'm right in the target market — and will certainly be interested when that moment comes.
But it also won't be an impulse buy where I snap up the first thing I see Amazon. "The biggest pitfall to avoid is making decision on price alone," says Anker's Kelvin Cao. "Now that plug-in solar has regulatory approval, the UK market will attract a wave of low-cost imports, some of which will be excellent and some of which will not. This will be a similar problem once the plug-in batteries are legalised," he warns.
"A battery that cuts corners on cell quality, protective engineering and compliance with applicable safety standards might look more attractive on its price tag, but it will not deliver the same reliability over the 10 to 15 years that a household should reasonably expect," he adds. In other words, buying cheap could backfire when it comes to savings.
So what exactly should you look for when plug-in batteries are legalised? "As a baseline, consumers should look for durable LFP battery cells, a high cycle life, robust protection against weather and corrosion, and integrated safeguards against electrical and thermal risks," Kelvin Cao says.
"They'll probably also say that the product must be listed on the Energy Networks Association (ENA) Type Test Register to demonstrate that its protection settings meet G98 requirements," adds Windfall Energy's Rob Hallifax.
A real-world view
A large number of early adopters are already getting a taste of the benefits of a battery-only setup. One of those is TechRadar contributor Mark Pickavance, who wrote our EcoFlow Stream Ultra X review (which is well worth a read).
I caught up with him to see how it's going and he continues to be impressed. He told me that his monthly energy costs are down by about £40 a month with his setup (which was installed with the help of an electrician), and you could get most of that from a single Ultra X.
The only problem is that this stuff can get addictive. "I started with the premise of using just a battery, but once you have one the logical progression is solar. However, for people renting, it's the ideal solution, and if you use an Economy 7-like tariff (Octopus Go), you can take a chunk out of your costs," he said.
The arrival of plug-in solar from August could, then, be a good dry run of what to expect when plug-in batteries arrive. The big differences between residential buildings between Germany and the UK could mean plug-in solar doesn't quite take off in the same way in the UK, but Anker's Kelvin Cao remains bullish.
"This is no longer a niche movement. Germany passed one million officially registered plug-in solar systems in 2025, with around 430,000 new systems registered during that year alone," he notes. If plug-in batteries follow a similar pattern in the UK, that could have big consequences for energy bills — and the UK's grid as a whole.

Having worked in tech journalism for a ludicrous 17 years, Mark is now attempting to break the world record for the number of camera bags hoarded by one person. He was previously Cameras Editor at both TechRadar and Trusted Reviews, Acting editor on Stuff.tv, as well as Features editor and Reviews editor on Stuff magazine. articles.title: Bloctel tire sa révérence, Claude pirate trois entreprises par erreur et Google rebaptise ses hackers : on vous raconte la semaine Cyberguerre
articles.text:
Démarchage téléphonique : que va-t-il se passer avec l’arrêt de Bloctel le 11 août 2026 ?
- À partir du 11 août 2026, Bloctel, la liste française d’opposition au démarchage téléphonique, sera fermée, car la loi interdit désormais le démarchage par défaut.
- Le décret n° 2026-662 stipule que le consentement doit être clair, spécifique et révocable, et les entreprises doivent prouver qu’elles l’ont obtenu de manière légale.
- Des applications telles que Saracroche, Begone, WinCalls et Préfixe Bloqueur offrent des solutions efficaces pour bloquer les appels indésirables et les arnaques en utilisant des listes communautaires et des filtres de numéros.
Nous y voilà : après OpenAI, Anthropic annonce à son tour que Claude a piraté trois entreprises par erreur
- Anthropic a identifié trois incidents où ses modèles IA ont accédé à des systèmes réels lors de tests de cybersécurité, mettant en lumière des erreurs de configuration.
- Les modèles, dont Claude Opus 4.7 et Claude Mythos 5, ont utilisé des accès internet non sécurisés pour extraire des données et compromettre des systèmes.
- Contrairement au cas d’OpenAI, ces incidents ont été détectés proactivement par Anthropic, démontrant un besoin critique d’amélioration des pratiques en cybersécurité IA.
Google change le nom des hackers les plus traqués au monde, sans régler l’essentiel
- Google Threat Intelligence Group introduit un nouveau système de cryptonymes à deux mots pour nommer les groupes de hackers, remplaçant les anciennes identifications de Mandiant et du Threat Analysis Group.
- Cette nouvelle nomenclature interne vise à harmoniser les identifiants après la fusion de Google et Mandiant, en utilisant des catégories basées sur l’origine géographique ou la motivation des hackers.
- Bien que cette initiative améliore la cohérence interne de Google, elle ne résout pas la fragmentation nomenclaturale entre différents éditeurs de cybersécurité à l’échelle mondiale.

articles.title: Scientists built night vision that shows full color instead of just green
articles.text:
Forward-looking: Researchers have developed a prototype device that converts infrared light into full-color images, offering a different approach to night vision that goes beyond the usual monochrome displays. The system, built by a team at the Beijing Institute of Technology, uses mercury telluride quantum dots paired with a dual-layer OLED. Instead of translating infrared into a single color based on brightness, the device maps different wavelengths and intensities into distinct visible colors.
That distinction is key. Traditional infrared imaging systems rely on detectors that capture a broad range of wavelengths but don't preserve much detail about them, so the output is typically rendered as brightness differences in a single color, often green. Effective as that is, it doesn't take advantage of how well the human eye can distinguish subtle color changes.
The new design tackles that limitation at the material level. The quantum dots used in the device are only a few nanometers in size, which gives them discrete energy states.
As a result, they respond differently depending on the wavelength and intensity of incoming infrared light. Lower-energy, longer wavelengths generate fewer charge carriers, while shorter wavelengths and stronger signals can trigger more complex electronic transitions and produce more carriers.
Those signals are then passed into a two-layer OLED structure. One layer emits red light, while the other emits cyan. An energy barrier between them controls how charge flows through the device.
With weaker infrared input, the system produces dim red light. As the signal strengthens or shifts to shorter wavelengths, more charge crosses the barrier and activates the cyan layer, resulting in a mix of colors and increased brightness.
Because the color output is tied directly to the physics of the incoming signal, rather than a preset mapping, the system carries more information. The researchers estimate it could detect much smaller differences in infrared power than conventional brightness-based systems.
To test the concept, the team built a lightweight eyeglass prototype. The device weighs 23 grams and is semi-transparent, allowing users to see both visible and infrared-enhanced images at the same time. In controlled experiments, it produced clear, color-coded images of simple patterns and moving objects under shortwave infrared illumination.
The setup can also be configured in different modes, either overlaying infrared information onto normal vision or filtering out visible light entirely for a more immersive view.
The researchers also explored whether the converted signal could be picked up by biological systems. In lab tests, infrared light processed through the device triggered responses in engineered cells that react to visible light.
Additional experiments showed measurable brain activity in mice and retinal responses in human volunteers when viewing infrared signals through the system. Infrared light on its own produced no such effects.
In the paper, the team says the work "redefined infrared vision" by "transcending the monochrome paradigm," adding that it paves the way to "next generation visual prosthetics."
There are still limitations. The tests were done in controlled environments using simple, high-contrast targets, so it's not clear how well the system would perform in more complex real-world settings. The OLED component also requires external power, which makes the current version more like a wearable display than a passive optical device.
There are also open questions around materials. Mercury telluride is a heavy-metal compound, and the study does not address long-term safety or whether it could be used in devices that come into direct contact with the body.
For now, the work shows a different way to handle infrared imaging – one that builds color into the sensing process itself rather than adding it afterward.

articles.title: Un ver informatique peut se propager dans Microsoft Word, d'un document à l'autre, avec l'aide de Copilot
articles.text:
Le chercheur Håkon Måløy a découvert une vulnérabilité critique dans Microsoft Copilot pour Word. L’intelligence artificielle de Microsoft, directement intégrée au logiciel Word, peut être manipulée par un attaquant en vue de mener une offensive. La méthode d’exploitation décrite par le chercheur repose sur la création d’un ver informatique IA. Ce ver est capable de se répliquer et de se propager de document en document de manière autonome.
À lire aussi : Nouveau record pour Windows – Microsoft corrige 570 failles de sécurité avec un seul Patch Tuesday
Comment Copilot déploie un ver informatique sur Microsoft Word
Dans un premier temps, l’attaquant va mettre au point un document malveillant, truffé d’instructions cachées. Ces instructions, dissimulées au beau milieu du document, sont destinées à manipuler Copilot. Pour que la victime ne remarque rien d’anormal, ces commandes malveillantes sont tout simplement écrites en tout petit, avec une police blanche sur un fond blanc, à la toute fin du document. Elles passent ainsi inaperçues. Sans se rendre compte de la supercherie, l’internaute va demander à l’IA de résumer ou de modifier le document reçu. En utilisant des options comme la baguette magique ou la fonction Éditer avec Copilot, l’utilisateur demande à l’outil d’analyser le texte.
En cherchant à répondre à la demande de son interlocuteur, Copilot va tomber sur ces commandes piégées. L’IA lit absolument tout le contenu du document, y compris le texte blanc caché par le pirate. Sans surprise, IA ne fait pas la différence entre le texte qu’elle doit analyser et les ordres qu’elle doit exécuter. De facto, elle se retrouve à obéir aux instructions du cybercriminel.
Une fois les instructions secrètes lues, l’intelligence artificielle passe à l’action. C’est à ce moment-là que l’offensive se mue en véritable ver informatique IA. Microsoft Copilot copie consciencieusement les instructions malveillantes invisibles, à la demande du hacker, et les intègre dans un nouveau document qui vient d’être généré. Si ce nouveau fichier est partagé avec un autre collègue qui l’utilise à son tour avec Copilot, le cycle recommence, et l’attaque se propage de document en document. Une fois le code malveillant intégré dans un document jugé sûr, il peut être redistribué via SharePoint, Teams ou par e-mail… ce qui peut faire de gros dégâts sur un réseau d’entreprise.
« Si le fichier porteur est ensuite utilisé dans un autre flux de travail assisté par Copilot, les instructions peuvent se déclencher à nouveau et se propager dans d’autres documents, même sans que le document d’origine de l’attaquant ne soit présent », souligneHåkon Måløy.
À lire aussi : Danger sur Windows – une faille de Microsoft Copilot permet de voler toutes vos données
Une faille qui restera béante
Comme l’explique Håkon Måløy, il est facile de passer à côté des modifications apportées par Copilot à un document. Celles-ci sont souvent validées rapidement par des employés qui font confiance à l’outil un peu trop facilement. Le chercheur a démontré que cette vulnérabilité persistait malgré les mises à jour de l’assistant vers des modèles linguistiques très avancés, tels que GPT-5.5 et GPT-5.6. L’expert parle d’une faiblesse ancrée en profondeur dans l’architecture de l’intelligence artificielle. Il s’agit d’une « faiblesse architecturale plus large dans les systèmes actuels basés sur les grands modèles linguistiques ».
Alerté par le chercheur, Microsoft a déployé quelques correctifs partiels pour limiter les dégâts, mais n’a pas trouvé de solution pour colmater définitivement la vulnérabilité. Pour l’heure, la seule véritable défense repose sur la prudence et la méfiance systématique. C’est loin d’être la première fois qu’une faille de sécurité analogue est débusquée dans le fonctionnement de Copilot. L’an dernier, une faille intitulée EchoLeak a été découverte, et elle permettait d’exfiltrer des données d’entreprise via un simple mail piégé, sans action de l’utilisateur.

articles.title: Google Chrome may soon block New Tab hijacker extensions by default
articles.text:
Google is preparing a new Chrome security feature that would block policy-installed extensions from hijacking the New Tab page or changing the default search engine.
BleepingComputer spotted the protection in a chain of work-in-progress Chromium Gerrit changes. It has not shipped yet, but Google plans to enable it by default once the changes are approved.
"In low-trust environments (unmanaged consumer devices), enterprise policy force-installs and recommendations are abused to lock in search engine or new tab page hijackers," Anunoy Ghosh, who works at Google, wrote in a post.
"This CL enables the kBlockDseNtpOverrideExtensionsOnUnmanagedDevices feature flag by default, activating the end-to-end blocking defense on unmanaged Windows and macOS devices."
Right now, Chrome allows organizations to use enterprise policies to force-install extensions and control browser settings.
It's not exactly bad on properly managed work devices connected to a domain or mobile device management system, but malware has been abusing the same feature on regular consumer PCs.
A malicious program can add local Chrome policy keys without your permission and force-install an extension that replaces the New Tab page, changes your search engine, or redirects searches to suspicious websites.
Chrome may then believe that the extension was installed by an administrator, which prevents you from removing or disabling it.
In some cases, Chrome also displays the confusing “Managed by your organization” message, even though the PC is not actually owned or managed by an organization.
Google describes these consumer PCs as “low-trust” environments because Chrome is reading policies stored locally without confirmation from a trusted authority, such as a domain or MDM service.
Under the proposed protection, Chrome would block attempts to install policy-controlled extensions that override the New Tab page or default search engine.
The installation would be canceled, and Chrome would save the extension ID in a blocked-extension preference.
Chrome would also stop trying to download the same blocked extension during future policy checks, which should prevent repeated installation attempts and unnecessary network activity.
Google is also addressing another trick used by malware
An extension that you installed manually would no longer be converted into a locked, policy-controlled extension. It would remain under your control, so you could still disable or remove it.
If a previously managed device loses its trusted management status but still has local policy keys, Chrome would automatically uninstall affected New Tab and search-engine override extensions.
Google is adding metrics to measure how often these policy-based hijackers appear and how frequently Chrome blocks them.
Legitimate administrators would also have access to an escape-hatch policy that disables the protection when a required enterprise extension overrides the New Tab page or search engine.
The Gerrit changes are still under review, so the feature is not available in stable Chrome yet.

articles.title: Los móviles con cuatro cámaras están de moda, pero a veces son puro marketing: así puedes distinguir las que merecen la pena
articles.text:
Hubo un tiempo en el que tener dos cámaras en el móvil era una auténtica revolución. Hoy, bajar de tres o cuatro sensores en la parte trasera parece un auténtico sacrilegio, sobre todo para los departamentos de marketing. Sin embargo, la realidad técnica es que tener más "ojos" no significa ver mejor.
En los móviles de gama media y de entrada, nos hemos acostumbrado a ver módulos de cámaras enormes que, al analizarlos de cerca, esconden sensores que solo están ahí para rellenar la ficha técnica. A lo largo de este post te vamos a enseñar a distinguir cuándo un móvil merece la pena por su cámara y cuándo no.
Google Pixel 10 - 128GB
La trampa de los sensores de relleno
Seguro que, en más de una ocasión, has visto un móvil que presume de cuádruple cámara AI por un precio sospechosamente bajo. Lo más probable, en este caso, es que estés ante una configuración de 1 + 1 + 2: una cámara principal y tres sensores secundarios de escasa utilidad.
Este es un claro ejemplo de marketing en la fotografía móvil. Los sospechosos más habituales son:
- Sensor macro de 2 MP: es, sin lugar a dudas, el rey del relleno. Con una resolución tan baja, cualquier foto ampliada del sensor principal suele tener más detalle que la foto nativa de este macro.
- Sensor de profundidad de 2 MP: estamos en 2026 y el procesado por software y la IA son tan avanzados que no necesitan una lente física de baja calidad para calcular la profundidad. Ten en cuenta que muchos móviles de gama alta ya ni lo incluyen.
Así puedes identificar una cámara que merezca la pena
Si estás pensando comprarte un móvil con buena cámara para fotografía, lo mejor es que no cuentes solo los círculos en la parte trasera del smartphone; busca estas tres claves en las especificaciones:
- Tamaño del sensor (no solo los megapíxeles): un sensor de 200 MP puede ser peor que uno de 50 MP si el primero es minúsculo. Busca sensores grandes (por ejemplo, de 1/1.3" o cercanos a 1") y aperturas amplias (f/1.6, f/1.8). El tamaño físico del sensor es el factor principal que determina cuánta luz capta y la profundidad de campo, mientras que la apertura solo regula la cantidad de luz que entra por la lente.
- Estabilización óptica (OIS): si la cámara principal no tiene OIS, tus fotos nocturnas y vídeos sufrirán. Es preferible un móvil con solo dos cámaras y OIS, que uno con cinco cámaras y estabilización digital (EIS) mediocre.
- Principal + Gran Angular + Teleobjetivo: es la Santísima Trinidad en fotografía móvil. Si el teléfono tiene estas tres, estarás comprando un equipo versátil. El teleobjetivo es el marcador real de calidad, es caro de fabricar y requiere buen procesado. Si un móvil lo incluye, suele ser señal de que el sistema fotográfico ha sido tomado en serio en este terminal.
Algunos ejemplos puedes encontrar en la ficha de los móviles
A continuación, te exponemos una tabla con algunos ejemplos de configuraciones que puedes ver en las fichas técnicas de algunos smartphones.
| configuración típica | valor real | NUESTRA RECOMENDACIÓN | 
|---|---|---|
| Principal (108MP) + Macro (2MP) + Profundidad (2MP) | Gama media "de relleno" | Evítalo si buscas fotografía profesional | 
| Principal (50MP OIS) + Gran Angular (12MP) | Gama media-alta equilibrada | Es una configuración recomendad: calidad frente a cantidad de sensores | 
| Principal + Gran Angular + Teleobjetivo (Zoom Óptico) | Gama premium | Es el móvil ideal para fotografía. Ofrece versatilidad para todo tipo de situaciones | 
Analizando todo, la próxima vez que veas un módulo de cámaras que parece una placa de inducción, pregúntate cuántas de esas lentes usarás. A menudo, las marcas sacrifican la calidad del sensor principal para poder poner cuatro cámaras en la caja. Así que es preferible una sola cámara excelente que cuatro mediocres.
Teléfonos móviles a destacar en fotografía por gama
Gama de entrada-media
- Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro: con un sensor principal de 200 MP, es uno de los claros ejemplos de que el número vende en la caja. Sin embargo, para poder decir que este Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro tiene cuádruple cámara, añaden lentes secundarias mediocres.
Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro - Smartphone de 8+256GB
Gama media-alta equilibrada
- Google Pixel 10: el último smartphone de Google es uno de los reyes de esta categoría. Durante años, solo usaron una cámara y ahora que usan dos o tres, se aseguran de que cada una sea excelente. No verás sensores de 2 MP. Prefieren darte un gran angular de 12 MP o 48 MP que realmente sirvan para hacer fotos a paisajes o monumentos con nitidez, apoyado por un OIS que evita que las fotos en este Google Pixel 10 salgan movidas.
Google Pixel 10 - 128GB
Gama premium
En este apartado, y ya que estamos centrados en la fotografía móvil, hablaremos de tres modelos que destacan para hacer fotos con el teléfono. Estos son el Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, el iPhone 17 Pro y el Xiaomi 17 Ultra.
Estos tres smartphones destacan por incluir un teleobjetivo, que es un factor importante para distinguir entre un móvil normal y uno profesional; aunque no es el único, ya que el procesado, el sensor principal y el HDR también son críticos.
El sistema fotográfico de lente principal + gran angular + teleobjetivo (zoom óptico) es el único que te permite sacar una foto nítida de un detalle de una catedral, de un animal a lo lejos o de un retrato con desenfoque manual, no generado por una IA que a veces te corta algunas zonas del rostro.
Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra 12 + 256 GB
Apple iPhone 17 Pro, Azul oscuro, 512 GB, 5G, 6.3 " OLED Super Retina XDR
XIAOMI 17 Ultra - Smartphone de 16+512GB
Un truco para saber si estás ante un móvil con buena cámara: puedes hacerlo incluso en la tienda, cuando estés viendo móviles para comprar. Tapa con el dedo las lentes pequeñas y verás que la experiencia apenas cambia en la mayoría de situaciones. Tapa el teleobjetivo de un gama alta y verás cómo el zoom se vuelve borroso al instante. Ahí es donde está el valor real.

articles.title: Startup eyes AI search boom; VC slowdown tests startups
articles.text:
Startup eyes AI search boom; VC slowdown tests startups
DareAISearch is helping brands improve visibility across AI platforms as AI powered discovery reshapes online search. Meanwhile, Indian startup funding dropped to its second lowest weekly level this year.
Hello,
The effects of technological change are becoming inseparable from everyday life.
That shift is playing out at multiple levels. China’s rapid advances in artificial intelligence, chip manufacturing and robotics are raising the stakes in the global technology race. Powerful open source AI models developed by Chinese companies are challenging the dominance of established American players, prompting fresh debate in Washington and Silicon Valley over competitiveness, regulation and national security.
At the same time, separate disclosures from OpenAI and Anthropic that autonomous AI agents breached testing environments have intensified scrutiny of AI safety, reinforcing concerns that governance may not be keeping pace with increasingly capable systems.
The impact of these technological advances is also being felt well beyond governments, and research labs.
Across the UK, phone-free clubs, digital detox retreats and screen-free social events are attracting people looking to disconnect from constant notifications and reclaim uninterrupted time. As digital devices become more deeply woven into everyday life, moments away from screens are becoming a sought-after experience.
The same shift is reshaping consumer behaviour. Demand for bathroom mini fridges is growing, driven partly by the rise of GLP-1 weight-loss medicines, which require refrigeration before first use, and partly by a booming wellness industry centred on skincare, supplements and personalised health routines. What was once a niche appliance is finding a new place in modern homes, showing how advances in healthcare and consumer technology are influencing domestic spaces.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- Startup eyes AI search boom
- VC slowdown tests startups
Here’s your trivia for today: Which Nintendo game introduced the character who would later become Mario?
Startup
As AI reshapes online discovery, Gurugram startup DareAISearch is helping brands boost visibility across AI platforms. Founded in 2026, it combines analytics and AI to improve recommendations, aiming to become a global leader in AI search optimisation.
Key takeaways:
- DAIS analyses AI citations, search trends, brand content and competitor signals to explain why AI recommends certain brands and identify ways to improve visibility.
- The startup serves over 25 enterprise clients, including ASICS, Ambuja Cement and Earthful, and has generated about Rs 1.8 crore in revenue so far this year.
- Competing with firms in New York and Berlin, DAIS aims to reach $100 million in annual recurring revenue within 40 months as AI driven discovery expands.
Weekly funding
Indian startup funding slipped to its second lowest weekly level this year, with just $67 million raised across 14 deals. Weak AI investment, economic headwinds and cautious investors have slowed funding, though many believe capital inflows may now be nearing a turning point.
Key takeaways:
- Startup funding fell below $100 million for the sixth time this year, highlighting prolonged investor caution despite hopes that the market may have reached its lowest point.
- India’s AI startup sector has yet to attract the strong investor interest seen globally, limiting its ability to drive a broader recovery in venture capital funding.
- Arboreal Bioinnovations led the week’s fundraising with about $24 million, followed by Sid’s Farm, Fixxly, Omega Seiki Mobility and AI startup Revspot.
News & updates
- Earnings: Ahead of its first earnings call, SpaceX investors are asking about pink rockets, mascots and Moon missions, revealing excitement about vision over financials.
- Football: UEFA has welcomed FIFA’s decision to abandon plans to sell a stake in the World Cup and said it will work with other confederations to prevent a repeat.
- Currency: The US Treasury has reportedly bought yen alongside Japan for the first time in over a decade, signalling coordinated efforts to support the weakening Japanese currency.
Did you know?
Which Nintendo game introduced the character who would later become Mario?
Answer: Donkey Kong

articles.title: Adiós al spam en Gmail: método para eliminar miles de correos sin buscarlos manualmente
articles.text:
Mantener la bandeja de entrada de Gmail libre de correos promocionales puede parecer una tarea interminable cuando, con el paso del tiempo, se acumulan boletines informativos, ofertas comerciales y mensajes de servicios a los que el usuario se suscribió hace meses o incluso años.
Sin embargo, la plataforma incorpora una función que permite localizar todas esas suscripciones desde un único lugar y cancelar las que ya no resultan útiles, sin necesidad de buscar los correos uno por uno.
PUBLICIDAD
La herramienta está disponible desde la versión web de Gmail y reúne los remitentes que envían mensajes periódicos a la cuenta. Gracias a ello, los usuarios pueden revisar rápidamente qué servicios siguen enviando correos y decidir cuáles desean conservar y cuáles prefieren eliminar para mantener una bandeja de entrada más ordenada.
Esta función simplifica un proceso que normalmente implicaría abrir decenas de mensajes distintos, localizar el enlace para cancelar la suscripción y repetir la misma operación una y otra vez.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo acceder a la herramienta de suscripciones
El procedimiento es sencillo y puede realizarse directamente desde el navegador.
Después de iniciar sesión en Gmail, el usuario debe fijarse en la dirección que aparece en la barra de navegación. Allí, donde normalmente figura la palabra “inbox”, basta con sustituir ese término por “sub” y cargar nuevamente la página.
PUBLICIDAD
Al hacerlo, Gmail redirige automáticamente a un apartado específico donde aparecen organizadas todas las suscripciones asociadas a esa cuenta de correo.
En esa sección se muestran los boletines informativos, promociones comerciales y otros servicios que envían mensajes periódicos al usuario.
De este modo, ya no es necesario recorrer la bandeja de entrada para identificar cada remitente de forma manual.
Cancelar suscripciones con pocos clics
Cada servicio listado incorpora una opción para dejar de recibir sus correos.
Junto al nombre del remitente aparece un botón que permite iniciar el proceso de baja. Al seleccionarlo, Gmail muestra la opción “Anular suscripción”, que solo requiere confirmar la acción para que el usuario deje de recibir los mensajes promocionales de ese remitente.
PUBLICIDAD
Esta herramienta resulta especialmente útil para quienes, con el paso del tiempo, se registraron en numerosas páginas web, aceptaron promociones o autorizaron el envío de boletines sin recordar posteriormente esas suscripciones.
Al concentrar todas ellas en un único panel, Gmail facilita una limpieza rápida y mucho más eficiente del correo electrónico.
Por qué la bandeja de entrada termina llena de spam
La mayoría de los mensajes promocionales llegan después de crear una cuenta en una tienda en línea, descargar una aplicación, participar en una promoción o aceptar recibir novedades de una empresa.
PUBLICIDAD
En muchos casos, estas autorizaciones pasan desapercibidas porque forman parte del proceso de registro o aparecen incluidas entre las opciones de privacidad.
Con el paso del tiempo, la cantidad de correos puede crecer de forma considerable, dificultando la localización de mensajes realmente importantes relacionados con el trabajo, estudios, bancos o comunicaciones personales.
PUBLICIDAD
Aunque estos correos no siempre constituyen spam en el sentido estricto del término, sí representan contenido no deseado para muchos usuarios.
Ventajas de mantener el correo organizado
Reducir el número de mensajes promocionales ofrece beneficios que van más allá del aspecto visual de la bandeja de entrada.
Una cuenta con menos correos innecesarios permite encontrar información importante con mayor rapidez y disminuye el riesgo de pasar por alto comunicaciones relevantes entre cientos de promociones.
PUBLICIDAD
Además, una mejor organización facilita la gestión diaria del correo y reduce el tiempo que los usuarios dedican a eliminar mensajes de forma manual.
También puede contribuir a identificar con mayor facilidad intentos de phishing o correos fraudulentos, ya que una bandeja menos saturada hace más sencillo detectar mensajes sospechosos.
PUBLICIDAD
Una herramienta para recuperar el control del correo
La acumulación de promociones y boletines es una situación habitual para millones de usuarios de Gmail.
Con esta función integrada, Google ofrece una alternativa para administrar todas las suscripciones desde un único lugar, evitando tener que repetir el mismo proceso correo por correo.
Aunque seguirán llegando mensajes procedentes de servicios que el usuario decida conservar, cancelar las suscripciones innecesarias ayuda a reducir significativamente el volumen de correos diarios.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Hackers Poison Adform Script to Swap Crypto Wallet Addresses Across Customer Sites
articles.text:
Attackers modified a JavaScript file served by advertising technology company Adform, turning it into a browser-side tool that rewrites cryptocurrency wallet addresses.
Adform detected the incident on July 27, 2026, removed the malicious code, notified affected clients, and reported it to authorities.
Anyone who visited a site carrying the affected script on July 27 and copied a Bitcoin, Ethereum, or Tron address may have pasted a different address inserted by the malicious code instead.
Adform is telling people to clear their browser cache because the altered file may remain cached after the fix, and to check any wallet address before sending funds.
Adform says the code was not designed to install software or establish persistence and operated only while an affected page remained open. The captured sample also rewrites addresses entered directly into form fields, so clipboard copying was not the only path to replacement.
The public timeline is unresolved. Adform's notice identifies July 27 as the affected date; Kevin Beaumont says he saw malicious activity via Adform over the past week.
The compromised resource is trackpoint-async.js, served from s2.adform[.]net. Adform's implementation documentation says the tracking code can run on one page, several sections, or unconditionally across an entire website. Compromising that shared resource gave the attackers a route into unrelated downstream sites without having to breach each one separately. The shared deployment path makes this a supply-chain compromise.
While the affected page remained open, one altered address at the point of payment could redirect a transfer.
Beaumont, an independent security researcher, disclosed the compromise and wrote, "Even if you notice the address is wrong and recopy the wallet, it keeps replacing it." Beaumont reported that the file and its associated URLs, domains, and IP addresses returned no detections on VirusTotal at the time. Max Maass published a captured copy of the script on July 27.
The captured sample contains two malicious blocks appended to the legitimate library. Their replacement strings are obfuscated with a six-byte XOR key. The first watches for the copy event, tries to read the clipboard every four seconds, and to replace matching addresses.
It also attempts an HTTP request to 84.32.102[.]230:7744 on page load that includes the hostname and path of the page the visitor is on.
The second block walks the document's text nodes, rewrites values in input, textarea, and contenteditable elements, and restores the cursor position after a rewrite. It hooks the value setter on input and textarea elements, so programmatic writes are rewritten in transit.
It also intercepts copy, cut, paste, and input events. Both blocks contain hardcoded replacement strings for Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Tron address patterns, and Beaumont said the addresses appeared to vary.
Adform says it found no evidence that the code transmitted visitors' IP addresses or information about websites they visited. It added in its incident notice that "Technical analysis indicates that such transmission may have been possible." The first payload's request is built to send a page hostname and path to the outside server; whether it reached the operator is not established by the sample.
Most of the scope is still missing: how many websites carried the file, how many visitors were exposed, how the attackers reached Adform's deployment path, and whether any funds were diverted. The duration gap also prevents a defensible exposure estimate because Adform's July 27 affected-date statement and Beaumont's longer observation remain unreconciled. Adform's public incident notice lists no indicators of compromise.
Adform's 2025 annual report says the company had roughly 1,800 customers, enabled 1.5 billion ads to be displayed daily, and served or transacted ads in more than 180 countries during 2025.
Those figures describe the platform, not this incident. A more useful number is how many page loads actually received the altered resource, a count Adform has not published. Adform has not publicly identified the attacker.

articles.title: Securpost : ce capteur français vous prévient lorsque le facteur est passé
articles.text:
Securpost : ce capteur français vous prévient lorsque le facteur est passé
La boîte donne de ses nouvelles
Médaillé d'or au Concours Lépine 2026, le capteur français Securpost transforme une boîte aux lettres ordinaire en objet connecté. Il prévient sur smartphone de l'arrivée ou du retrait d'un courrier et d'un colis, sans Wi-Fi ni abonnement obligatoire.
Securpost Capteur connecté pour boîte aux lettres.
À l'heure où le smartphone peut signaler qu'une machine à lavera terminé son cycle ou qu'un aspirateur-robot s'est égaré sous le canapé, la boîte aux lettres demeurait étonnamment silencieuse. Securpost compte bien lui donner la parole avec un petit capteur capable d'envoyer une notification lorsqu'un courrier ou un colis est déposé.
Cette invention française, récompensée par une médaille d'or au Concours Lépine, s'adresse notamment à ceux qui multiplient les descentes inutiles pour découvrir une boîte vide. Elle peut aussi trouver son utilité pendant les vacances, dans une résidence secondaire ou auprès des personnes ayant des difficultés à se déplacer.
La boîte donne de ses nouvelles
Le principe ne nécessite pas de remplacer la boîte aux lettres. Le capteur Securpost se fixe simplement à l'intérieur à l'aide d'un adhésif. Le fabricant annonce une installation en moins d'une minute, sans outil. Le boîtier mesure 84 × 76 × 34 mm et pèse 300 g, piles comprises.
Contrairement à de nombreux objets connectés, il n'a pas besoin d'accéder au réseau Wi-Fi du logement. Il communique en 4G LTE-M et transmet ses informations à l'application Securpost, disponible sur iOS et Android. Cette particularité permet notamment de l'installer loin de la maison, dans le hall d'un immeuble ou sur une résidence secondaire.
Ses différents capteurs sont censés reconnaître l'arrivée d'un courrier, le dépôt ou le retrait d'un colis ainsi que les ouvertures de la boîte. Le fabricant affirme également que son système peut distinguer une lettre d'un paquet, y compris lorsque le courrier est glissé sans ouverture de la porte.
L'application conserve un historique des événements et permet de partager les alertes avec des proches. Plusieurs capteurs peuvent également être regroupés au sein d'un même compte.
Le boîtier fonctionne avec trois piles AA fournies. Le fabricant estime son autonomie à environ deux ans, selon la fréquence des ouvertures et des événements détectés. Il annonce également une résistance aux projections d'eau et un fonctionnement compris entre -20 et 70 °C.
Sans abonnement, mais avec une option Premium
Securpost est commercialisé au prix de 69,90 €, avec la connectivité 4G incluse et sans abonnement mensuel obligatoire. L'application gratuite permet de recevoir les alertes principales, de consulter l'historique et de les partager.
Une formule Premium facultative ajoute toutefois une photo à chaque réception, l'envoi des notifications par courrier électronique et la suppression des publicités dans l'application.
Le fabricant annonce une compatibilité avec la majorité des boîtes aux lettres standard, individuelles comme collectives. Une antenne externe est fournie lorsque la réception mobile à l'intérieur du compartiment métallique se montre insuffisante.
