articles.title: How a Nigerian tutor relocated to Thailand on a $500 visa
articles.text:
Ava Anthony arrived in Thailand expecting little more than a holiday. What she found instead unsettled the way she thought about music.
One evening, inside a jazz bar, she watched performers whose ease on stage felt almost rehearsed into instinct. Beyond the live performances, she discovered an industry built on years of deliberate preparation, in which aspiring artists could spend seven to nine years training before a record label would consider them ready to debut.
For Anthony, a Nigerian singer-songwriter who performs under the stage name ‘Denle,’ the experience raised an uncomfortable question.
If Afrobeats has become one of the world’s fastest-growing music genres with far less formal preparation, what could it become if artists developed within similarly structured systems?
“There’s a structure that Asia has been able to incorporate,” Anthony told TechCabal. “I’m also taking a look at the numbers and the statistics comparing that to Afrobeats, and the stat is alarming—how they’re doing like 30 to 100 billion streams in a year, and Afrobeats is just doing like 30 [billion streams].”
It was an unlikely realisation for someone who had travelled to Thailand on a modest budget, intending to teach English while experiencing life in a different country. Yet that journey would leave her thinking as much about Nigeria’s creative economy as her own career.
The irony is that Anthony’s relationship with music began in a far less structured setting.
Growing up, mornings in her family home often began with the voices of Nigerian gospel singer Panam Percy Paul or American country musician Jim Reeves drifting through the house.
Both of her parents sang in the church choir—her mother still does—and music was woven so naturally into family life that she scarcely noticed its influence.
She certainly didn’t imagine it would become the opening chapter of a life that would take her from studying electrical and electronics engineering to working as a digital strategist for major Nigerian brands, teaching English in Thailand and pursuing a career as a singer-songwriter. Nor did she expect that travelling halfway across the world would fundamentally reshape how she thought about the future of African music.
From church choirs to campus busking sessions
Long before Chiang Mai, there was a 13-year-old girl discovering that her voice could move people.
Anthony says she first realised she might actually be able to sing after performing a solo in her church’s children’s choir.
Afterwards, a woman approached her mother and remarked in Yoruba, “What a voice your daughter has.”
Anthony remembers that moment as a turning point. Encouraged by her mother, what began as a fascination with music gradually evolved into writing original songs while she was still in secondary school.
She sang Disney songs alone in her room, joined the school choir and continued writing. Her mother supported her ambitions but insisted that education came first.
“Once you get that certificate, then you can go into music,” they told her, according to Anthony.
At Landmark University in Kwara State in southwestern Nigeria, she studied Electrical, Electronics and Communications Engineering; she met a guitarist who shared her enthusiasm for performing.
Together, they began holding informal Saturday evening busking sessions behind one of the campus cafeterias.
What began as two students playing music gradually attracted regular audiences of between 15 and 20 people.
“It became an every-Saturday thing,” she said. “That was when I started thinking, ‘okay, I can actually do this in real life.’”
After graduating in 2015, the guitarist—Damilola Aalabi ‘Isama’—became her manager, and she began attending recording camps that helped launch her music career.
One of the clearest confirmations that she was on the right path came during a recording session for an unreleased song titled Magnificent, performed under her stage name, Denle.
She sent the song to her sister in the United Kingdom, who called back in tears.
Written for Black girls navigating questions of beauty, race and self-worth, the song resonated deeply with her sister’s experience of living as a Black minority in Britain.
That conversation reinforced Anthony’s sense of purpose.
“I feel like I was given this gift and this talent to be able not just for myself but for people.”
After university, Anthony was posted for the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), Nigeria’s compulsory one-year national service programme, to Brotherhood Secondary School in Ibesikpo Asutan, Akwa Ibom State, in southern Nigeria.
The public school bore little resemblance to the private schools she had attended.
She says she arrived on her first day convinced the students would mock her accent. Despite having no formal training as an English teacher, she found herself teaching the subject anyway.
Rather than retreat, she leaned into the challenge.
One lesson at a time, she built a rapport with her students. She asked what they hoped to become, shared stories of people who had overcome difficult circumstances and, every so often, ended lessons by singing.
“Before I leave the class, [the kids] would say, ‘Teacher, teacher, sing one more song,’” she said. “It felt like a beautiful merger: teaching and music.”
Teaching may have become her profession, but music never stopped being her ambition.
The strategist behind the songs
After completing national service, Anthony built a career in digital strategy.
Between 2016 and 2020, she said she worked in advertising and branding, developing campaigns for clients including Nigerian tier-one lenders Access Bank and Zenith Bank. She later served as a community manager on a Lagos State gubernatorial campaign that challenged incoming governor Jimi Agbaje in 2019, according to Anthony.
Those years gave her something many emerging musicians never acquire: a practical understanding of digital communities, audience development and brand positioning.
“I realised that it’s not just for corporate sectors,” she said. “You can actually put that into music and entertainment, into a person.”
By 2020, Anthony was ready for another chapter.
She had secured admission to the University of Ilorin Business School to pursue a master’s degree, but the COVID-19 pandemic derailed those plans before the programme could begin.
“In 2020, I secured admission into the University of Ilorin Business School in Nigeria. My plans to continue my studies were disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic,” Anthony said.
Instead, she pivoted into music management, working with artists while continuing to take on freelance branding and digital strategy projects. For the first time, the two sides of her career—advertising and music—began to converge.
“From 2020 to 2025, my career was shaped by a single theme: using technology to bridge creativity, business, and education across different industries and countries.
Moving to Thailand
By 2024, Anthony had accumulated experience as a teacher, digital strategist, and music manager. It was, however, her brief teaching experience during national service that unexpectedly shaped her next move.
Inspired by her time in the classroom, she developed an interest in English-language instruction and educational technology. Anthony decided to travel to Thailand in 2025, first on a tourist visa, combining what she expected would be a short holiday with a Teaching English as a Foreign Language (TEFL) certification.
“[The certification] required a structured TEFL training programme that combined coursework with practical teaching assessments,” Anthony said. “Rather than a single written exam, the certification required successfully completing teaching practicum sessions and demonstrating classroom competence over the course of about a month.”
Applying for a Thailand tourist visa, which has a 60-day validity period, requires applicants to hold about 20,000 THB ($600) per person, or 40,000 THB ($1,200) for a family.
“I had already been saving towards an international relocation because I had previously been preparing for [an] opportunity,” she said. “When my plans changed, I redirected those savings toward relocating to Thailand while ensuring I met the country’s official financial requirements.”
Thailand generally requires visitors to demonstrate they have sufficient funds to support themselves during their stay, a requirement Anthony had already prepared for while planning her move abroad.
She moved to Thailand in March 2025, just weeks before the country’s annual Songkran Water Festival.
“I remember just getting into Thailand, and it just felt so right,” she said. “It felt like I was supposed to be here.”
The TEFL programme introduced her to teachers from different parts of the world and exposed her to new approaches to technology in education across Asia.
What began as a one-month certification course soon became something more. Anthony stayed on, spending two months teaching English in Chiang Mai while immersing herself in Thailand’s education system, culture and creative industries.
Then came the conversation that would reshape how she thought about African music.
One evening, while out with a friend who had persuaded her to experience Chiang Mai’s nightlife, Anthony struck up a conversation with the owner of a local record label. He described the years of structured training that many Thai artists undergo before making their professional debut—an approach that contrasted sharply with how many artists emerge in Africa.
The conversation has stayed with her.
Today, Anthony says she hopes to help build a similar training-oriented ecosystem for African artists—one that combines vocal development, performance coaching, branding and strategic positioning before musicians are introduced to international audiences.
“Afrobeats goes beyond a genre,” Anthony said. “It’s our heritage. It’s our culture. It’s who we are.”
Inside Thailand’s digital nomad visa
Anthony returned to Nigeria after the Songkran festival with her mind already made up. But she wasn’t done with Thailand.
“I got back home, and I told my parents, I think I’m actually going to apply for the digital nomad visa because there’s so much I [still need to] learn in Thailand,” she said. “I was very anxious, obviously applying as a Nigerian with the Nigerian passport. But it was quite easy.”
She had travelled to Thailand as a visitor. She wanted to return with the freedom to build a life there: as an educator, a creative, and a remote worker.
In June 2025, after several weeks of applications, Anthony relocated to Thailand on a Destination Thailand Visa (DTV), the country’s long-stay visa designed for remote workers, freelancers, creatives and participants in approved cultural or soft-power activities, including teaching.
Introduced in July 2024, the visa allows eligible foreigners to live in Thailand while working remotely, although holders cannot legally work for Thai-registered companies without additional authorisation.
Anthony said the application required proof of remote income or employment, reference or employment letters, evidence of sufficient financial means, about 500,000 THB—between $14,000 and $20,000, according to her—and an online application followed by an interview at the Royal Thai Embassy in Abuja, the capital city of Nigeria.
She estimates the entire process cost between $450 and $500.
“The DTV is created for creatives and remote workers to thrive,” she said, pointing to Thailand’s abundance of cafés, creative spaces and reliable internet infrastructure, with Wi-Fi often included in residential rent.
Her application was processed electronically and approved within two to four weeks after a single interview.
With a 5-year validity period, the digital nomad visa allows her to stay in Thailand for up to 180 days at a time before leaving and re-entering the country, with the option to extend her stay by another 180 days.
“People call it a visa run,” she said. “But I don’t even see it as a visa run. You should explore other countries and come back in.”
She sees Thailand’s programme as part of a broader regional effort to attract global talent, pointing to similar digital nomad initiatives introduced by countries such as South Korea and Malaysia.
Building from Chiang Mai
More than a year after relocating, Anthony has lived in only two Thai cities: Bangkok and Chiang Mai.
Bangkok, she says, felt too familiar.
“I can’t leave Lagos [and] come to another version of Lagos,” she joked.
Chiang Mai offered something entirely different: a slower pace of life, quieter streets and a sense of calm that she says reshaped the way she thinks, works and creates.
She believes that mindset also influences how many Thai people relate to foreigners.
“They [Thai locals] don’t see colour here; they just see you as a person,” she said. “Buddha says don’t see people, don’t see colour, don’t see skin, don’t see gender, just see the human. That’s what they live by here.”
Whether or not that perception reflects the experience of every foreigner, Anthony says it has shaped her own experience of living in Thailand.
More profoundly, it has transformed her creative life.
“I learned how to breathe here,” she said. “I learned how to be calm here. I learned how to think here.”
She argues that the relentless pace of Lagos conditions many Nigerians to accept a level of stress they no longer recognise because it has become routine.
Thailand, she says, forced her to slow down—to unclench her shoulders, think more deliberately, and approach both work and music with greater intention.
The change has shown up most clearly in her songwriting.
“I remember telling my friend—the kind of songs I’ve written since I got here [Thailand],” she said. “I don’t think I could have written that when I was back home [Nigeria].”
Today, Chiang Mai serves as both her home and her studio. She works remotely as a brand consultant while continuing to build her music career, drawing inspiration from a country that has changed not only how she lives but also how she imagines the future of African artists.
“I’ve learned to structure my time so that neither career is neglected.” Anthony said, “For me, they’re not competing paths; one provides stability while the other allows me to express creativity and tell stories through music.”
She still hopes to explore Rayong, Koh Samui, Pai, and other parts of Thailand. But for now, Chiang Mai is where she has found the space to keep asking the question that first brought her back: what could African music become if talent had more time—and more room—to grow?
“My long-term goal,” Anthony revealed, “Is to contribute to building stronger ecosystems back home, where technology empowers education, where creative industries have better infrastructure, and compete globally through innovation.”
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: Kioxia CM10 Series Launched for the PCIe Gen6 Generation of SSDs
articles.text:
Ahead of FMS 2026, Kioxia launched its new CM10 series, marking the company’s entry into PCIe 6.0 enterprise storage with direct liquid cooling capability for AI infrastructure deployments. These new SSDs leverage Kioxia’s BiCS FLASH generation 10 memory technology and target high-performance KV cache workloads alongside NVIDIA CMX context memory solutions.
Kioxia CM10 Series Specifications and Features
This new CM10 series delivers substantial performance gains over the previous CM9 generation, with Kioxia claiming up to approximately 92 percent higher sequential read performance and up to approximately 85 percent higher random read performance. These improvements address the scaling demands of AI models approaching trillions of parameters and context windows expanding to millions of tokens.
KIOXIA offers the CM10 series across multiple form factors to accommodate different deployment requirements. Its E3.S and E1.S variants support direct-cold-plate liquid cooling for specific thickness profiles, while all forms remain compatible with traditional air-cooled environments. The EDSFF lineup includes E3.S at 7.5 mm thickness and E1.S in both 9.5 mm and 15 mm profiles. 9.5 mm variants of both form factors support direct liquid cooling environments. There is also a dual-port design in E3.S for high availability for traditional HA storage arrays.
A 2.5″ option extends the CM10 Series to conventional enterprise chassis that cannot accommodate EDSFF forms or require higher capacity per drive slot. The 2.5″ CM6 is 15mm in thickness and maintains a dual-port design like the E3.S variant for high availability applications. Something interesting from the slides is that the 2.5″ is listed as using BiCS FLASH generation 8 TLC flash memory with PCIe 5.0 compliance, rather than the Gen 10 memory and PCIe 6.0 interface found in EDSFF models. On STH, we have been warning that the traditional U.2/ U.3 drives were likely to start giving way to EDSFF connectors as the electrical requirements of PCIe Gen6 hit. This is a great example of that.
Final Words
We expect to see the Kioxia CM10 series drives in AI storage tier deployments where ephemeral KV cache benefits from flash latency between GPU HBM and networked storage. Still, the new announcement is important since we are seeing chips like the NVIDIA Vera CPU and the AMD EPYC Venice series hit the market. The new CM10 series represents Kioxia’s response to AI infrastructure storage demands that extend beyond traditional enterprise SSD requirements. Direct liquid-cooling capability addresses thermal constraints in dense GPU pods, where KV cache storage sits adjacent to accelerator racks. Its performance claims against the CM9 generation suggest meaningful headroom for context memory workloads that NVIDIA CMX solutions target.
Perhaps most notable is that we are finally seeing a split in NVMe SSDs away from around a decade and a half of 2.5″ U.2 form factors leading the way. Separating PCIe 6.0 EDSFF forms from PCIe 5.0 2.5″ variants allows Kioxia to serve both next-generation liquid-cooled deployments and existing air-cooled infrastructure with a single product family branding. The use of BiCS FLASH generation 10 in EDSFF form factors versus generation 8 in 2.5″ form factors reflects the thermal and density requirements. Perhaps we will see more of that with PCIe Gen5 drives using older NAND generations, while Gen6 drives use newer ones.

articles.title: Balance Theory Raises $19 Million to Help Enterprises Manage Cybersecurity Investments
articles.text:
Cybersecurity investment management startup Balance Theory has raised $19 million in Series A funding to expand its platform for helping CISOs evaluate and manage security spending.
Balance Theory’s platform is designed to bring cybersecurity investment planning, market intelligence and execution into a single system. It maintains contextual information about an organization’s security program, supplements it with proprietary market data, and employs AI agents and automated workflows to support purchasing and portfolio-management decisions.
As the company explains, “Balance theory manages security investment events end-to-end. Detect investment decision triggers, run each event for the best cost and coverage outcome, and continuously rationalize the program to maximize the impact of every dollar deployed.”
The platform also creates a record explaining why individual investments were made and monitors for changes that could affect their value, suitability or priority. According to the company, its technology currently manages more than $1 billion in cybersecurity spending.
The funding round was led by SYN Ventures, with participation from existing investors DataTribe and TEDCO. The company also announced that Dan Burns, founder of Accuvant and former CEO of Optiv, has joined as executive chairman.
Balance Theory said it will use the new funding to accelerate go-to-market efforts, build deeper enterprise integrations, expand its cybersecurity market intelligence, and continue developing the platform’s AI agents and skills.
The Columbia, Maryland-based company raised $3 million in Seed funding back in 2022.
“Security leaders lacked a consistent way to understand their own enterprise, navigate an increasingly complex market and connect those insights to action,” Balance Theory co-founder and CEO Greg Baker said.
The company did not disclose its valuation following the investment.

articles.title: Cloudflare Introduces Meerkat for Strongly Consistent Global Coordination
articles.text:
Cloudflare recently introduced Meerkat, an internal globally consistent control-plane service based on the QuePaxa consensus algorithm. Unlike Raft, it allows leaderless writes while preserving strong consistency, improving availability across Cloudflare's global network.
James Larisch, senior research engineer at Cloudflare, Bob Halley, principal research engineer at Cloudflare, and João Pedro Leite, research engineer at Cloudflare, write:
Unfortunately, commonly deployed consensus algorithms like Raft suffer in wide-area networks like Cloudflare’s because they rely on leaders and timeouts. The leader is the only replica allowed to make writes, and if it fails due to a crash or network degradation, the system becomes unavailable until some other replica times out and a new leader is elected.
To avoid further incidents caused by unavailable leaders in consensus-driven systems, the team has been developing a new distributed consensus service based on the QuePaxa consensus algorithm.
Unlike Raft, QuePaxa allows all replicas to accept writes without relying on leader timeouts, avoiding the availability loss that leader-based systems experience when a leader becomes unreachable across wide-area networks. Meerkat provides a consensus log that supports services such as a transactional key-value store and a leasing system, and Cloudflare says it is expected to be the first production deployment of QuePaxa at a global scale.
After outlining the consistency and fault-tolerance requirements, the article explains how Meerkat achieves strong consistency via a globally replicated consensus log that ensures all replicas agree on the order and values of committed operations, guaranteeing linearizable reads and writes. Larisch, Halley, and Leite add:
The Meerkat log is a sequence of slots. A slot is a box that can contain an event or not. A slot that contains an event is called a decided slot. All slots in the log are decided except the last slot, which is currently being decided. One of Meerkat’s invariants is that if any two replicas decide on the value for a slot, those values are the same. In other words, no two replicas will ever disagree on the value of a decided slot.
Source: Cloudflare blog
In a popular Hacker News thread, some practitioners found the article difficult to follow, while others questioned whether the additional round trips would be worth it in typical deployments. A user comments:
What's interesting here is that this would be the first production implementation of an asynchronous consensus algorithm (QuePaxa). Paxos, Raft, etc. are all partially synchronous, meaning they rely on timeouts and only make progress if message delay is sufficiently small compared to timeout durations. QuePaxa doesn't rely on timeouts and makes progress even under wild fluctuations in message delay. The question is whether performance is competitive enough in the normal case.
Assessing Meerkat’s performance, Larisch, Halley, and Leite warn:
Meerkat has limitations. It is not designed to create general-purpose data systems like databases. All consensus algorithms come with a cost: lots of round-trips. QuePaxa in particular takes one to three round trips (usually, although it can take more) between the initial proposer and a majority of replicas to decide on a proposal and add an event to the log.
While some developers ask Cloudflare to open source the specification they used to design and verify Meerkat, Aniket Ray, software engineer at KPIT, writes:
QuePaxa's approach to the latency-consistency trade-off is sharp. Research shows consensus overhead typically adds 40-60% latency in multi-region Paxos deployments, making Meerkat's optimization critical for strongly consistent systems.
Meerkat is not yet deployed to production, but Cloudflare says it has completed multiple proofs of concept with up to 50 replicas distributed worldwide.

articles.title: Suspected Chinese-Speaking Hackers Target Central Asian Governments With OctLurk and SilkLurk
articles.text:
A Chinese-speaking threat actor is suspected to be behind a fresh wave of cyber attacks targeting government organizations mainly located in Central Asia, including Afghanistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, and the Syrian Arab Republic, since January 2025.
These targeted organizations operate across several sectors, such as healthcare, research, government offices, ministries of foreign affairs, logistics, law-enforcement agencies, urban planning and facilities management, and public educational establishments, per Kaspersky. The activity has not been linked to any known adversary or group.
The attacks are characterized by the use of two new obfuscated backdoors the Russian cybersecurity company is tracking as OctLurk and SilkLurk, as well as a specialized utility codenamed LurkProxy to proxy network traffic.
"OctLurk and SilkLurk can download and inject additional plugins to perform further malicious actions, including launching command shells, performing file system activity, synthesizing keyboard and mouse events, network scanning, credential dumping, keylogging, password theft from browsers, email collection, and remote access," researchers Saurabh Sharma and Yaroslav Kikel said.
The initial access vector used in these attacks is currently unknown. However, Kaspersky's analysis has found that OctLurk is injected into memory and deployed by means of a loader, with the attackers also checking internet connectivity to the domain "dns.ssentialserv[.]xyz" before executing a batch script responsible for launching LurkProxy. The tool then establishes contact with a remote server ("154.196.162[.]76") for command-and-control (C2).
Once run, OctoLurk first collects system information, encrypts it, and sends it to a hard-coded C2 server ("dns.multitoconference[.]com") over a stream socket connection. It's equipped to load plugins received from the server directly into memory to enable command execution, file operations, clipboard content gathering and modification, screenshot capture, and mouse movements.
The threat actors have been found to leverage the backdoor's command shell plugin to perform the following series of actions -
- Fingerprint the host and harvest extensive data about the compromised system.
- Run commands to export successful logon events for remote interactive logons and to query those events for specific users.
- Harvest password hashes from domain controllers using Impacket's "secretsdump.py" tool.
- Drop and execute a keylogger that masquerades as AnyDesk to sidestep detection.
- Decrypt and extract passwords from Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox.
- Establish remote access to the victim machine using Pandora RC agent.
- Scan internal and public networks using Fscan to identify services running on specific ports, such as Secure Shell (SSH) on port 22 and MySQL on port 3306, and then attempt to access these services using credentials from a password file named "pp.txt."
- Connect to an email server, authenticate with a username and password, and issue commands to collect or manipulate emails.
LurkProxy, for its part, can function as a reverse proxy in two distinct modes, either as a SOCKS5 proxy or a transparent proxy. At any given time, the malware can operate in only one mode to route network traffic through a target address.
The third tool in the threat actor's arsenal is SilkLurk, which is launched by means of a DLL that, in turn, is executed using a DLL side-loading sequence. The backdoor then creates a TCP socket and connects to a C2 server specified in its configuration, followed by collecting victim information and transmitting it to the server.
In response, the server sends a command that's to be executed on the infected endpoint. This can involve getting the system's local time, setting a sleep interval that determines the frequency at which the backdoor polls the C2 server, sending or updating backdoor configuration, and receiving and injecting additional plugins into memory.
The post-compromise activity linked to SilkLurk is below -
- Invoke "cmd.exe" to launch PowerShell and run commands to connect to shared network resources with administrative credentials, search and stage confidential documents, disconnect from the network shares, and use legitimate archiving tools like WinRAR and 7-Zip to archive the stolen data.
- Run "cmd.exe" to initiate a DLL side-loading chain to drop PlugX, a known backdoor used by Chinese hacking groups.
Kaspersky said it found infrastructure overlaps between the campaign and a prior set of attacks involving a C++-based implant codenamed SilentRaid (aka MystRodX and TrustFall).
"This overlap points to shared infrastructure across multiple OS-targeting campaigns, though it remains unclear whether these activities ran concurrently or at different times," Kaspersky said. "The emergence of the OctLurk and SilkLurk multi-plugin malware framework highlights how threat actors continuously refine their tactics to evade detection and maintain control over compromised networks."
"Both families operate primarily in memory, leaving only a minimalistic loader on disk that relies on machine-specific data (OctLurk uses the drive serial number, and SilkLurk uses the computer name) to decode payload locations and contents. This victim-specific encoding makes reverse engineering and automated detection considerably harder."

articles.title: The Verge’s 2026 back-to-school shopping guide
articles.text:
Knowing exactly what your student needs for the school year ahead is next to impossible. Sure, you’ll probably nail the essentials, but there will likely be a few items you forgot to buy, or didn’t think they’d need to have. We’re pulling our weight during the back-to-school season with a new shopping guide that’s a mix of practical and aspirational products for students to use in and out of the classroom.
The Verge’s 2026 back-to-school shopping guide
From necessities to nice-to-haves, we’ve gathered 28 products that will make this year at school the best it can be.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
We’re covering items that make writing easier and more satisfying, alarm clocks that can rattle even the most sleep-deprived students from a deep slumber, bags that are just as great for the gym as they are for the weekend away, and more. We wish the students in your life (or you, if you’re the student in question) a prosperous year, and we hope that our curation makes things a little easier during your studies and your downtime a lot more fun.
The Shark TurboBlade Bladeless Tower Fan pivots, twists, and oscillates to keep the air in your room from feeling stale. It has 10 power levels, and its bladeless design can move air up to 80 feet away at full power. Its filter can be cleaned, so you don’t have to worry about buying replacement parts.
Apple MacBook Neo
When it comes to simple laptops for notetaking and essay writing, it’s hard to beat the value of the MacBook Neo. Its iPhone-grade CPU and 8GB of RAM mean this isn’t a powerhouse meant for engineering students. But it’s a better choice than a similarly priced Chromebook or Windows laptop.
Canon’s PowerShop ELPH 360 HS will make your memories really pop better than smartphone pictures. It has a 20.2-megapixel CMOS sensor that works well in low light, plus 12X optical zoom and optical image stabilization. It features a 3-inch LCD screen so your crew can review photos before posting them. I dig its hybrid auto mode that can take videos to go along with each photo, like behind-the-scenes footage for your antics.
Whether you’re trying to catch a quick game between classes, or you need a distraction on the bus ride home, the Anbernic RG Rotate gaming handheld is worth considering. Its aluminum design is slick and durable, and the 3.5-inch IPS LCD swivels away to cover up the buttons when it’s not in use. The device runs Android, which means you can install and play a compatible emulator of your choice.
Texas Instruments TI-84 Evo Graphing Calculator
As math classes start to ramp up in complexity, you’ll need a calculator that can hang. The Texas Instruments TI-84 Evo is the latest edition, with a lot of improvements to make it feel more modern than the old TI-83 you might’ve used. The color screen lets you see multi-equation graphs in a new light, and USB-C charging means no more hunting for batteries in the middle of an exam.
Blackwing Pencils Audition Pack
Blackwing pencils make a great gift for the stationery nerd or journaler in your life. They feel luxurious to write with, leaving rich strokes across the page. It’s obvious that a lot of thought went into the design, one example being its square eraser to keep them from rolling away (they’re easy to replace, too). They’re available in four different core hardness ratings, with frequent collaborations and special editions to collect.
Igloo Retro Square Lunch Bag
You’ll be the coolest kid in class if you show up with this 1990s-inspired cooler bag from Igloo, no matter how old you are. Its 108-ounce capacity is enough for your whole lunch or up to nine 12-oz cans, and the side pocket is great for holding an extra little treat, or some sunscreen. While it isn’t technically collapsible, I’ve found mine squishes down nice and flat for storage when it’s empty.
Looking for a low-stress way to get around campus? The Razor kick scooter is a convenient method of traveling to and from school or zipping around between classes. It folds up for storage in your locker or under your desk, and they’re available in a variety of colors and sizes. Some even include features like air-filled tires and suspension that would have made me jealous in middle school.
The 32-ounce Owala FreeSip does a good job of keeping your favorite beverage cold or hot for an entire day at school, with the option to drink through a straw or straight from its mouth. All the pieces come apart for easy cleaning, and there are a number of color combinations to choose from, as well as different sizes to accommodate different levels of thirst.
Loop Quiet 2 earplugs
The Loop Quiet 2 earplugs aren’t as isolating as simpler, cheaper foam options, which makes them a great choice for finding a bit of solace while studying in a crowded library. They have exterior loops that signal that you’re busy, and which make them easier to remove quickly. They come with a handy carrying case and a selection of different tip sizes to make sure you get a comfortable fit.
The waterproof Kindle Paperwhite lets you carry thousands of titles in a slim, lightweight device, so you won’t have to stuff your backpack with books or fill up precious shelf space in a tiny dorm room. It also can last for over a month on a single charge, making it one less thing to constantly charge during a busy semester.
The Fujifilm Instax Mini 13 is a fun gift for students starting a new chapter. It prints credit card-sized photos in seconds, and the new self-timer makes it easier to snap group photos with friends. The prints make great decorations for dorm walls and scrapbooks, giving them memories they’ll treasure during breaks and long after graduation.
If you or someone you know is the type of student who color-codes everything in journals, the Pusheen 10-in-1 Ballpoint Pen is a cute gift. With 10 colors, it’s easy to organize notes and planners without carrying around a handful of pens, and the adorable 3D Pusheen topper is just fun.
The Midori Paintable Stamp is a useful gift for students who like to use paper planners, bullet journals, or scrapbooks. The pre-inked stamp quickly adds a monthly calendar to any page, be it in a notebook or a sticky note, and its oil-based ink won’t bleed when colored in with water-based markers or highlighters.
Between textbooks, planners and notebooks, a student’s desk can get cluttered quickly. Aobopar’s adjustable steel bookends expand up to 18 inches, making it easy to stay organized as the semester goes on. They’re a practical gift that’s especially handy for small dorm rooms with limited storage.
Leuchtturm1917’s Bullet Journal Edition 2 is great for students who want to stay organized without relying on tech. Designed with bullet journal creator Ryder Carroll, the 204-page dot-grid notebook includes essentials like a key, index, future log, and page numbers, along with a sticker sheet, and a pocket guide that doubles as a ruler.
VidaBay NFC E-Paper Fridge Magnet
VidaBay’s NFC E-Paper Fridge Magnet is a fun way to personalize a dorm room fridge. Although it looks like an instant photo, its color E Ink display lets students update the image anytime using their phone. They can switch between photos of family back home, new friends, or favorite memories whenever they like, without buying packs of instant film.
The Boox Tappy Wireless Page Turner makes it easy to turn pages or scroll around without touching your e-reader, tablet, or phone. The Bluetooth remote works with Boox tablets, Kobo e-readers, as well as iPhone and Android devices, letting you flip pages forward and backward, scroll up and down websites, or skip tracks in music, audiobooks, and podcasts all without reaching for your screen.
Uni Kuru Toga Roulette mechanical pencil
Any pencil will do for completing homework and filling out the planner, but some are better than others. One of the most clever (yet still fairly affordable) is the Uni Kuru Toga Roulette. It’s a mechanical pencil with a mechanism that rotates the lead every time you lift it up between letters and words. Sounds silly, but it ensures that you always have a pointed tip to write with.
Computers are great note-taking devices, but if you’re like me, you might learn a little more by writing down notes. Remarkable’s Paper Pure has matte-textured glass that mimics the feeling of writing on paper, and the device lets you easily import or export notes, plus search for words within your notes. You could buy many paper notebooks for the cost of the Paper Pure, but this elegant gadget can do so much more.
The Duffel Pack 3 is a stellar bag for weekend getaways, trips back home, and adventures beyond high school, college, or post-grad life. Its suitable for schlepping school materials and a laptop, or packing in all of your gym attire, including bulky shoes. Aer’s bag has pockets on pockets, so to speak, with adjustable straps and a section that lets it easily (and securely) slide around luggage handles.
Using a planner is for more than just staying on top of homework, schedules, and extracurricular activities. It’s where you can journal how everything in your life is making you feel, jot down ideas you have for cool projects, and really anything you want to look back on. Hobonichi Techo’s planners come in various sizes and layouts, letting you look at things day-by-day or week-by-week. They’re great, and I really like that each page has a daily quote to make each day feel fresh.
A MIDI controller won’t be on everyone’s back-to-school shopping list. Something like the Arturia MiniLab 37 should get added, though, if you’re a student who wants to connect to their musical side with ease. The MiniLab 37 is reasonably priced, and small enough to fit into a backpack. And yet, our reviewer found that its size didn’t come at the cost of playability. It has access to the company’s top-notch synth effects, and it includes software so you can make music right out of the box.
Xgimi MoGo 4 laser projector
As much as you may be tempted to buy a TV for your dorm, consider a compact projector instead. You won’t save money going that route, but you’ll be able to use it just about anywhere, not just in your room. The Xgimi MoGo 4 Laser projector is slick, includes Google TV software built-in with robust app support, and works well with consoles thanks to its HDMI input. It runs off a built-in battery, though you can keep it charged with a USB-C power bank or with the included power adapter.
A noise machine is one of those unsung back-to-school essentials that might make various parts of your school year a lot easier. The LectroFan Classic’s digital re-creation of white noise is shockingly natural sounding, without obvious start/stops that can be jarring when you’re in the flow (or trying to sleep). It’s USB-powered, includes a power brick, and comes with numerous tones of sound to suit your preferences for sleep or concentration, from deep, ocean-like brown noise to shrill white noise.
Most people will agree that it’s tough to get out of bed. For others, it’s on another level. Standard alarms aren’t loud enough to pierce the veil of deep sleep. If I’m describing you or someone you know, the Sonic Bomb alarm clock is the nuclear option for being woken up. The alarm can blare loudly, and if that’s not enough, the egg-shaped vibrating pod that connects to it can buzz the bed until it’s turned off. It’s extremely effective, though keep in mind that roommates will likely hear it as well.
Govee Table Lamp Classic
The cordless Govee Table Lamp Classic is easy to move from a desk to a bedside table, so it can do the job of multiple lamps without taking up much space. With adjustable brightness, support for countless colors, and customizable lighting effects, it’s also just as useful for late-night study sessions as it is for relaxing after the big tests.
Buying an OLED... for school? I’m being serious. Alienware is among a few manufacturers making 27-inch 1440p QD-OLED monitors that are cheaper than you might expect. The AW2726DM is made for gaming (it has a 240Hz refresh rate), but it’s good for productivity and entertainment, too. Its QD-OLED panel is as good as $350 can get you, with rich contrast, deep blacks, solid text clarity, and a three-year warranty against panel burn-in.

articles.title: iPhone 17 Pro Max à 1 260 € : le prix le plus bas jamais vu sur ce modèle
articles.text:
L’iPhone 17 Pro Max occupe le sommet de la gamme Apple depuis septembre 2025. Avec son écran OLED de 6,9 pouces, sa puce A19 Pro et son système photo triple 48 mégapixels capable de zoomer jusqu’à 8x en optique, il n’a pas grand-chose à envier aux smartphones Android haut de gamme comme le Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra ou le Google Pixel 10 Pro. Le timing de cette offre n’est d’ailleurs pas anodin : les rumeurs autour des iPhone 18 évoquent une hausse de prix pouvant atteindre 200 à 300 euros sur la prochaine génération. Autant dire que le modèle actuel disponible pour 1 260 euros a de quoi faire réfléchir.
Les atouts de l’iPhone 17 Pro Max
- Son écran Super Retina XDR de 6,9 pouces, 120 Hz, 3 000 nits
- La puce A19 Pro avec chambre à vapeur et 12 Go de RAM
- Son autonomie record pour un iPhone : jusqu’à 37 heures de vidéo
L’iPhone 17 Pro Max 256 Go en Bleu Intense est actuellement proposé à 1 260 euros sur Joybuy mais aussi sur Amazon. On le trouve aussi à ce tarif sur Amazon dans le même coloris, ce qui reste dans les deux cas le tarif le plus bas relevé à ce jour sur ce modèle.

Un grand écran lumineux dans un châssis repensé
L’iPhone 17 Pro Max inaugure un design unibody en aluminium forgé qui tranche avec le titane des générations précédentes. La dalle Super Retina XDR OLED de 6,9 pouces conserve le ProMotion adaptatif à 120 Hz et grimpe jusqu’à 3 000 nits en extérieur, ce qui garantit une lisibilité correcte même en plein soleil. Le Ceramic Shield 2 protège l’avant et l’arrière, avec un traitement antireflet en prime.
Côté gabarit, le smartphone mesure 163,4 × 78 × 8,8 mm pour environ 231 grammes. Il est légèrement plus épais que son prédécesseur, un choix assumé par Apple pour loger la chambre à vapeur et une batterie plus généreuse. Le format reste imposant et la prise en main à une seule main demande de grandes paumes, ce qui peut freiner ceux qui préfèrent les écrans plus compacts.
A19 Pro, photo 8x et autonomie marathon
La puce A19 Pro, gravée en 3 nm, embarque un processeur 6 cœurs cadencé jusqu’à 4,26 GHz, un GPU 6 cœurs et un Neural Engine 16 cœurs dédié à Apple Intelligence. Les 12 Go de RAM LPDDR5 assurent un multitâche fluide. Côté photo, les trois capteurs de 48 mégapixels couvrent du grand-angle au téléobjectif périscopique 8x (200 mm), une première sur iPhone. La batterie de 5 088 mAh permet d’atteindre jusqu’à 37 heures de lecture vidéo selon Apple. La recharge filaire rapide grimpe jusqu’à 50 % en une vingtaine de minutes avec un adaptateur 40 W, et le MagSafe monte à 25 W. Seul regret : le poids et l’épaisseur restent élevés, et la charge filaire maximale reste en retrait face à certains concurrents Android qui dépassent les 100 W.

articles.title: AWS Introduces Free Sandbox Environments for Workshops
articles.text:
AWS Builder Center now offers free, time-limited sandbox environments for workshops, so developers no longer need to use their own AWS account and credit card or worry about unexpected charges. This has been a long-standing request from the community and removes one of the biggest friction points for practitioners learning new AWS technologies.
According to the announcement, each sandbox provides 8 hours of pre-provisioned access and is ready within 15 minutes, with automatic cleanup on expiry. Developers can initially create only one sandbox per week, and the option is currently available only for a subset of workshops.
The workshops accessible via the sandbox environment are step-by-step guided labs covering topics such as building serverless APIs, setting up VPCs, deploying containers, and working with AI services. Rick Suttles, senior manager at AWS, explains:
Sandbox environments are a new addition to AWS Builder Center that lets you request a free, time-limited AWS account and start building right away. Whether you want to try a workshop without creating a personal account or just want to experiment without worrying about unexpected charges, sandboxes give you a clean environment to work in.
The new option adds to a broader set of no-cost, no-account learning paths the cloud provider now offers, each suited to a different use case: Builder Center Sandbox is for trying AWS for a few hours without persisting anything, while the revamped Free Tier gives developers an actual account with USD 200 in credits and 6-month auto-closure for side projects. Sumit Tiwari, SRE & DevOps engineer at ADP, comments:
One thing that often stops people from learning AWS is not the technology itself. It's the fear of accidentally spending money, setting things up incorrectly, or forgetting to clean up resources.
Among the workshops currently supported, many are related to generative AI and agentic AI workflows, including "Claude Code on Amazon Bedrock", "AI-DLC Workshop," and "Storytelling based AI-powered insights and automation using Amazon Quick." Explaining "why this matters more than you think," Sarvar Nadaf, cloud architect at Deloitte, writes:
I've onboarded probably 40+ engineers to AWS across different client engagements. The pattern repeats every single time. Day one of training, someone raises their hand: "What happens if I accidentally leave something running?" That question comes from fear. And fear makes people skip hands-on practice entirely. They read docs. Watch videos. Never deploy a thing.
The long-awaited feature has received positive reactions from a community that hopes it will be extended further. Still, AWS is the last of the major hyperscalers to introduce it. Microsoft has offered no-signup Azure sandboxes via Microsoft Learn for years, and Google Cloud has similarly provided comparable temporary environments through Qwiklabs/Google Cloud Skills Boost. As reported on InfoQ, Cloudflare's recent "Temporary Accounts" instead addresses a different use case, with no signup required for AI coding agents and a 60-minute human claim window.
Sandboxes are currently limited to select workshops, with broader coverage planned as AWS rolls out support over time.

articles.title: Voiture électrique : ce que révèlent vraiment les chiffres du marché automobile français de juillet - Numerama
articles.text:
Après un mois de juin historique pour la voiture électrique, les données d’immatriculations de juillet publiées par AAA Data viennent de tomber le 1er août. Le moins que l’on puisse dire, c’est que la période estivale n’a pas refroidi le marché : avec 44 378 exemplaires écoulés (+127 % sur un an), le 100 % électrique franchit un cap symbolique en captant 35 % de part de marché. Il est un peu tôt pour y voir l’influence réelle de l’ouverture du leasing social du 16 juillet, mais cela annonce déjà une rentrée sur les chapeaux de roue.
Au-delà de ces chiffres globaux impressionnants, le mois de juillet ne manque pas d’intérêt et bouscule le paysage automobile à tous les niveaux. Entre le raz-de-marée tricolore mené par Renault, le contrecoup soudain de Tesla sur sa gamme, l’offensive discrète mais redoutable des constructeurs chinois et les envolées surprises comme celle de Skoda, la bataille des marques prend une tournure totalement inédite en cet été 2026.
L’électrique devant les autres motorisations
En additionnant toutes les formes d’hybridation, celles-ci représentent 48 % du marché (60 605 unités). Mais prises séparément, aucune ne rivalise désormais avec le 100 % électrique, qui devient la première motorisation du pays avec 35 % de part de marché.
- 100 % Électrique (BEV) : 35 % de part de marché – 44 378 unités
- Micro-hybrides (MHEV) : 21 % – 26 933 unités
- Hybrides simples (HEV) : 20 % – 25 163 unités
- Essence : 11 % – 13 903 unités
- Hybrides rechargeables (PHEV) : 6 % – 7 461 unités
- Essence-GPL : 4 % – 5 172 unités
- Diesel : 2 % – 2 750 unités
- Extended Range Electric Vehicles (EREV) : moins de 1 % – 1 048 unités
Ces résultats s’expliquent néanmoins par le durcissement fiscal au 1er janvier 2026 (malus CO2 dès 108 g/km et malus au poids abaissé à 1 500 kg) qui continue d’asphyxier le thermique pur : l’essence décroche de -44 % et le diesel s’effondre de -60 %. De leur côté, les hybrides rechargeables subissent l’abaissement de leur abattement au malus au poids et reculent de 11 %.
Ajouté à la crise au Moyen-Orient et à la flambée du carburant, tout ceci bénéficie donc à l’électrique qui passe en tête des achats des Français.
Renault vs Tesla : le duel des leaders de l’électrique
Sur le plan des constructeurs, le mois de juillet confirme la domination de Renault sur le marché français, qui accapare à lui seul plus de 25 % des immatriculations électriques grâce à un tir groupé impressionnant : R5, Scénic et Twingo occupent les trois premières places du podium.
En face, Tesla réplique avec sa stratégie habituelle et ses limites. Le constructeur américain se classe 3ᵉ du mois (2 429 immatriculations), repoussé derrière Peugeot (4 306 unités). Surtout, la marque américaine est désormais quasi-exclusivement portée par le Model Y (2 401 unités à lui seul), pendant que la Model 3 traverse un trou d’air spectaculaire avec seulement 28 livraisons sur le mois. Il faut croire que toutes les livraisons de la berline se sont concentrées sur le mois de juin.
Stellantis toujours en demi-teinte
La Peugeot e-208 maintient le cap à la 5ᵉ place. Avec 1 941 exemplaires rien que pour le mois de juillet, Peugeot renoue avec des volumes dignes de ses meilleurs mois : ceux poussés par le leasing social. La Citroën ë-C3 se maintient à la 7e place avec 1 320 unités livrées en juillet. Les Peugeot e-3008 et e-5008 s’accrochent à leur classement dans le top 20, respectivement 14e (791 exemplaires) et 16e (747 unités).
Le reste des modèles du groupe est disséminé hors de la tête du classement. Certains « anciens » best-sellers marquent le pas. La Peugeot e-2008 glisse en 25ᵉ position avec 541 unités et la Citroën ë-C4 chute en 69ᵉ place avec seulement 106 exemplaires, illustrant le renouvellement rapide des attentes des acheteurs. Alors que la Peugeot e-2008 devrait rebondir grâce au leasing social, la Citroën e-C4 ne fait pas partie des modèles éligibles.
Le Citroën ë-C3 Aircross, pourtant récent, peine aussi avec 426 exemplaires. Quant aux autres marques du groupe, c’est toujours compliqué. C’est à se demander si la demande est faible ou si Stellantis souffre toujours de problèmes d’approvisionnement.
Skoda Elroq devant les modèles allemands
Porté par le lancement très réussi de son SUV compact Elroq, Skoda signe une performance remarquable. Le modèle remonte à la 6e place du classement général (1 341 exemplaires), permettant à la marque tchèque de grimper au 7e rang des constructeurs avec 1 953 unités et une part de marché de 4,4 %, ce qui place la marque juste derrière Volkswagen (5e avec 2 365 VE) et Citroën (6e avec 2 226 VE).
Chez Mercedes, le renouveau de la gamme porte ses fruits. La marque allemande est en 9e place des marques avec 1 831 exemplaires. Le nouveau GLC 100 % électrique réussit un démarrage remarqué (à vérifier la part des véhicules de démonstration). Il devient le premier modèle de la marque avec 696 immatriculations (18e place), suivi de très près par la nouvelle génération de la CLA (686 unités), éclipsant désormais les anciens EQA et EQB.
Au coude-à-coude avec Tesla, BMW s’offre une solide 4ᵉ place des marques avec 2 402 voitures électriques. Le duo iX1 (967 unités) et iX3 (778 unités) pèse à lui seul plus de 70 % des ventes électriques du constructeur bavarois.
Volkswagen complète ce trio allemand de tête, toujours porté par un ID.4 très en forme qui intègre à nouveau le Top 10 des modèles (8ᵉ avec 1 291 véhicules) et supplante largement l’ID.3 (794 unités). On attend l’arrivée de l’ID. Polo à la rentrée pour voir si cela fait bouger un peu le classement.
Une poussée chinoise discrète, mais bien présente
À vrai dire, avant de commenter les résultats des constructeurs chinois, il convient de féliciter un constructeur coréen. Kia classe son EV2 en 10e place du classement des voitures électriques en juillet. Le modèle enregistre 1 037 exemplaires, et cela devrait être encore davantage dans les prochains mois : entre le leasing social sur l’entrée de gamme et la livraison des modèles à plus grande batterie, c’est un modèle à suivre. L’EV4 se classe aussi en 21e position, ce qui reste un bon résultat. Le reste de la gamme est par contre plus décevant : seulement 7 Kia EV6, ouille !
Loin de se limiter à des rôles de figurants, les marques chinoises confirment leur montée en puissance sur le marché français, même si le résultat est largement plus impressionnant sur les hybrides que sur l’électrique. MG pousse, XPeng et BYD confirment.
MG Motor reprend du poil de la bête sur l’électrique avec 997 immatriculations en juillet (2,25 % de part de marché). MG est ainsi le premier constructeur d’origine chinoise en France sur l’électrique. La marque s’appuie notamment sur les MG4 et MG4 Urban (432 ventes cumulées). Toutefois, la sous-marque IM Motors réalise 320 unités, qui correspondent principalement à la constitution de la flotte de véhicules de démonstration pour le réseau avant le vrai lancement commercial auprès des clients. Les résultats de la marque sont donc à prendre avec des pincettes.
XPeng (14ᵉ marque) réalise 963 immatriculations, grâce au succès de son SUV coupé G6 : 619 exemplaires et 22ᵉ du classement du mois. BYD (15e marque) engrange 921 ventes. Cumulées, les ventes de MG, XPeng et BYD représentent désormais près de 6,5 % du marché 100 % électrique français, dépassant des piliers historiques comme Dacia, Ford ou Audi. Leapmotor est par contre un peu plus en retrait avec seulement 622 immatriculations en juillet.

articles.title: KI-Infrastruktur Deutschland: AI Hosting für Agenturen
articles.text:
KI-Agenten: So umgehst du die DSGVO-Falle beim Hosting
Datenschutz, Souveränität, Nachhaltigkeit: KI geht auch in Deutschland
mittwald ist der Hosting-Partner für Agenturen, Freelancer und Entwicklerteams, die digitale Projekte professionell betreiben wollen. Fully managed, made in Germany — von Webhosting über Container bis zu DSGVO-konformem AI Hosting.
Die Entwicklung leistungsfähiger KI-Modelle bestimmt derzeit viele Diskussionen. Weniger Aufmerksamkeit erhält dagegen die Infrastruktur, auf der diese Anwendungen tatsächlich betrieben werden. Dabei entscheidet sie häufig darüber, wie gut sich Datenschutz, Compliance, Performance und langfristige Wartbarkeit miteinander vereinbaren lassen.
Gerade Agenturen und Entwickler, die KI-Lösungen für ihre Kunden umsetzen, stehen deshalb vor Fragen, die über die Wahl des passenden Modells hinausgehen. Wo werden sensible Daten verarbeitet? Welche rechtlichen Rahmenbedingungen gelten? Und wie lässt sich vermeiden, dass eine Lösung vollständig von einem einzelnen Anbieter abhängig wird?
Für viele Unternehmen rückt deshalb der Serverstandort stärker in den Fokus. Hosting in Deutschland bietet einen klar definierten rechtlichen Rahmen und kann insbesondere bei Projekten mit personenbezogenen oder sensiblen Unternehmensdaten ein wichtiges Entscheidungskriterium sein.
Deutschland wird dabei zunehmend als Standort für moderne Rechenzentrumsinfrastruktur wahrgenommen. Internationale Cloud-Anbieter investieren seit Jahren in den Ausbau ihrer Kapazitäten. Gleichzeitig profitieren Unternehmen von einer verlässlichen Regulierungsumgebung, hohen Datenschutzanforderungen und einer leistungsfähigen digitalen Infrastruktur.
Anbieter wie mittwald setzen genau hier an. Das Unternehmen betreibt seine Infrastruktur in Deutschland und richtet sein AI Hosting an Agenturen, Entwickler und Unternehmen, die Wert auf Datenschutz, digitale Souveränität und einen professionellen Betrieb ihrer KI-Anwendungen legen.
Auch Nachhaltigkeit spielt bei Infrastrukturentscheidungen eine immer größere Rolle. Energieeffizienz und ein verantwortungsvoller Umgang mit Ressourcen gehören für viele Unternehmen inzwischen zu den Kriterien bei der Auswahl eines Hosting-Partners. Nach eigenen Angaben verfolgt mittwald diesen Ansatz bereits seit Jahren und setzt auf einen nachhaltigen Betrieb seiner Infrastruktur.
Warum das für KI-Anwendungen besonders relevant ist
KI-Systeme verarbeiten Daten in einer Tiefe und einem Umfang, die klassische Webanwendungen oft übertreffen. Chatbots lernen aus Interaktionen, Analysewerkzeuge verarbeiten Unternehmensdaten und automatisierte Workflows, etwa mit n8n, greifen auf interne Geschäftsprozesse wie Rechnungsstellung oder Zahlungsabwicklung zu. Diese Anwendungen erzeugen erhebliche Rechenlast und verarbeiten häufig sensible Informationen.
Damit wird die Standortfrage zu mehr als einer Kostenentscheidung. Werden KI-Anwendungen in Deutschland betrieben, erfolgt die Datenverarbeitung innerhalb des deutschen Rechtsrahmens. Gerade für Unternehmen aus dem DACH-Raum sowie aus regulierten Branchen wie dem Gesundheitswesen, der Finanzwirtschaft oder dem öffentlichen Sektor kann das ein wichtiger Faktor bei der Auswahl der Infrastruktur sein.
Was das für deine Kunden bedeutet
Der Serverstandort ist für viele Kunden zunächst nicht das wichtigste Gesprächsthema. Spätestens wenn Datenschutz, Compliance oder Nachhaltigkeit zur Sprache kommen, gewinnt er jedoch an Bedeutung. Wer verarbeitet die Daten? Welchem Recht unterliegen sie? Wie transparent ist die Infrastruktur? Und wie flexibel bleibt eine KI-Lösung, wenn sich Modelle oder Anbieter verändern?
Eine Möglichkeit, langfristig flexibel zu bleiben, besteht in modellagnostischen Anwendungen. Sie lassen sich mit unterschiedlichen KI-Modellen betreiben und erleichtern es, den Anbieter bei Bedarf zu wechseln oder neue Modelle zu integrieren. Dadurch sinkt die Abhängigkeit von einzelnen Plattformen.
Für Agenturen kann das ein wichtiges Argument sein. Aussagen wie „Gehostet in Deutschland, verarbeitet nach deutschem Recht und betrieben auf einer professionellen Infrastruktur von mittwald“ schaffen Vertrauen. Insbesondere dann, wenn KI-Anwendungen mit Kundendaten oder personenbezogenen Informationen arbeiten oder Nachhaltigkeitsziele eine Rolle spielen.
Was das für deine Agentur bedeutet
Wer KI-Lösungen entwickelt, übernimmt Verantwortung, nicht nur für die Anwendung selbst, sondern auch für die Infrastruktur dahinter. Dazu gehören Fragen nach Datenschutz, langfristiger Wartbarkeit und der Unabhängigkeit von einzelnen Cloud-Anbietern oder KI-Modellen.
Eine zukunftsfähige Infrastruktur sollte deshalb mehr leisten als reine Rechenkapazität. Sie sollte den Betrieb unterschiedlicher Modelle ermöglichen, rechtliche Anforderungen erfüllen und langfristig zuverlässig verfügbar sein.
Mit seinem AI Hosting positioniert sich mittwald als Hosting-Partner für Agenturen und Entwickler, die KI-Anwendungen professionell betreiben möchten. Das Angebot verbindet Hosting in Deutschland mit DSGVO-konformen Betriebsmodellen, hoher Flexibilität und einer Infrastruktur, die auf langfristige Projekte ausgelegt ist.

articles.title: Cyberattaque sur Chrome et Edge : ce virus manipule votre navigateur pour piller vos données
articles.text:
Un nouveau logiciel malveillant s’attaque aux utilisateurs de Google Chrome et de Microsoft Edge. Débusqué par les chercheurs de Cisco Talos le 22 juillet 2026, le virus s’intitule « msaRAT ». Ce « nouveau cheval de Troie d’accès à distance » est massivement utilisé par Chaos, un gang de pirates spécialisés dans les attaques par ransomware, pour arriver à ses fins.
La cyberattaque commence par une opération de phishing. Les pirates vont entrer en contact avec la cible, que ce soit par message, par mail ou encore par le biais d’un appel téléphonique. En manipulant l’internaute, ils vont se frayer un chemin jusqu’à son ordinateur, par exemple à l’aide d’un fichier piégé, d’un site trompeur ou encore d’une pièce jointe infectée.
À lire aussi : Google corrige 7 failles dans Chrome, dont une vulnérabilité découverte par OpenAI
Un mode pour développeurs détourné
Une fois sur l’ordinateur, les attaquants déposent un fichier d’installation sur le système. Baptisé update_ms.msi, il ressemble à une mise à jour Windows légitime. Lorsqu’il s’exécute, le fichier d’installation charge en toute discrétion le code de « msaRAT ». Le malware fait tout pour rester invisible. Il ne s’affiche jamais à l’écran et ne se connecte pas à Internet.
Dans l’ombre, le logiciel malveillant va vérifier si Chrome ou Edge est installé sur l’ordinateur qu’il vient d’infecter. Si c’est le cas, il démarre discrètement le navigateur dans son collimateur en arrière-plan, sans qu’aucune fenêtre n’apparaisse à l’écran. Le virus active ensuite le mode débogage, qui est initialement destiné aux développeurs. Le mode permet d’inspecter le fonctionnement interne du navigateur, de tester du code, ou d’automatiser certaines actions. Le virus s’en sert pour envoyer des instructions au navigateur, exactement comme le ferait un développeur.
Le malware peut ouvrir des onglets, naviguer vers des adresses web, ou encore lire et modifier le contenu affiché. Il ne tarde pas à injecter directement du code JavaScript malveillant à l’intérieur du navigateur. Désormais sous la coupe du virus, le navigateur entre en contact avec un service Cloudflare Workers, une plateforme cloud parfaitement légitime, ce qui lui permet de se lier avec l’infrastructure des cybercriminels
Pillage de données
Une fois relié, le malware reçoit des instructions de la part des commanditaires de l’attaque. Le virus va alors explorer le réseau et identifier la présence de données sensibles. Sans surprise, msaRAT va siphonner toutes les informations qu’il peut. Enfin, le maliciel va télécharger et installer un ransomware. Celui-ci chiffre alors les fichiers de la victime. Comme toujours, le gang Chaos mise sur une stratégie de double extorsion. Ils vont à la fois voler des fichiers et en chiffrer d’autres. Cette stratégie, de plus en plus répandue chez les cybercriminels, permet de maximiser les chances qu’une victime verse une rançon sans tarder. Comme le soulignent les chercheurs, l’opération ne s’éternise pas, de manière à limiter les risques de détection.
Les chercheurs précisent que la cyberattaque ne repose sur aucune faille de sécurité dans le code de Google Chrome ou de Microsoft Edge. De facto, il n’y a pas de correctifs à installer pour se protéger. Il faut surtout se méfier des prises de contact un peu suspectes, que ce soit par mail, par message ou par téléphone. En restant vigilant, il est possible d’entraver l’intrusion avant qu’il ne soit trop tard. La menace de Chaos plane surtout sur les grandes organisations. Les internautes lambda ne sont pas les principales cibles du groupe criminel.

articles.title: Why India still imports apples; How Magic Bus is helping rural women
articles.text:
Why India still imports apples; How Magic Bus is helping rural women
If India is growing record quantities of apples, why is it importing more of them than ever? In other news, the Rural Livelihood Programme of Magic Bus India Foundation is helping women across seven states to become entrepreneurs through locally tailored livelihood programmes.
Hello,
There’s a lot of talk about sovereign AI.
IBM and Sarvam are walking the talk with a partnership to advance sovereign AI adoption. They will together help governments and regulated organisations in India deploy AI that keeps data, operations, and governance under their own control.
The partnership combines IBM’s Sovereign Core software platform with Sarvam’s India-built AI stack, which includes reasoning models and multilingual voice and language technologies trained from scratch in India.
Moving on, tech giant Apple has posted a record June quarter revenue of $109.4 billion, up 16% year on year. This is supported by double-digit growth in most emerging markets including India. But the company has also flagged business concerns in the next few quarters driven by rising memory chip prices and supply constraints.
In other news, edtech firm Imarticus Learning has acquired Singapore-based BELLS Institute of Higher Learning for Rs 800 crore. The acquisition marks Imarticus’s first international acquisition and provides its access to learners in Southeast Asia. It also establishes Singapore as the company’s hub for Southeast Asia.
Meanwhile, days after OpenAI’s rogue attack, Anthropic has revealed that some of its Claude AI models had hacked into three companies during cybersecurity tests. This incident yet again underscores the need for stronger controls and guardrails as developers struggle to contain their AI models.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- Why India still imports apples
- How Magic Bus is helping rural women
- Urban Company’s Q1 results
Here’s your trivia for today: What art word is derived from the French word meaning ‘pasting’?
Economy
Why India still imports apples
If India is growing record quantities of apples, why is it importing more of them than ever? Why does so much home-grown fruit still fail to earn what it should?
For decades, India asked how to grow more apples. The bigger opportunity is to own more of the year: keep fruit sellable longer, process lower grades, and cut the import bill.
Key takeaways
- A kilo of apples can cost Rs 80 in September and Rs 220 by January, even in a year when India produces a record crop. Jammu and Kashmir, which grows roughly three-quarters of India’s apples, harvested more than 21 lakh tonnes in 2024-25. Yet India imported close to 5.6 lakh tonnes of apples during the same period, for an import bill of $418 million. The import bill has risen almost fortyfold from under $10 million 20 years ago.
- The problem is not only how much India harvests. It is also the shape of the year. India produces a flood of fresh apples for roughly four months, from the August-to-November harvest, then spends the other eight months drawing down cold stores and topping up with foreign fruit.
- The waste and the import bill are deeply connected. Both reflect India’s inability to preserve, grade, process and market enough of its crop beyond the harvest season. Call it the eight-month gap. The way to close it is not to fight the seasons–which no one can–but to break the link between when an apple is harvested and when it earns its money.
Top Deals of the Week
Startup: Arboreal Bioinnovations
Amount: Rs 230 Cr
Round: Series A
Startup: Sid’s Farm
Amount: Rs 81 Cr
Round: pre-Series B
Startup: Fixxly
Amount: $5.5M
Round: Seed
Social impact
How Magic Bus is helping rural women
The Rural Livelihood Programme of Magic Bus India Foundation is helping women across seven states to become entrepreneurs through locally tailored livelihood programmes.
The programme teaches life skills to young people from underprivileged backgrounds. It has helped 1 million young people transition into jobs after skilling over the last 10 years.
How the programme works
- The organisation identifies economically vulnerable blocks within a district and works intensively within those communities. Each intake is screened through a selection tool that weighs social and economic marginalisation—the programme works only with BPL families—alongside a test of entrepreneurial aptitude.
- It partners with gram panchayats and local stakeholders, conducting door-to-door outreach and village meetings to enroll participants—primarily women—into its free livelihood programme.
- Each intervention is anchored by a Livelihood Resource Centre, where participants are introduced to livelihood opportunities based on local market demand. Magic Bus enables women to choose between wage employment, self-employment, and entrepreneurship.
Quarterly earnings
Urban Company slips into red
Urban Company, the digital home services platform, returned to losses in the first quarter of FY27 despite posting a 44% year-on-year increase in revenue. The company, however, described the quarter as one of its strongest performances to date.
The company reported a net loss of Rs 92.12 crore in the April-June quarter, compared with a net profit of Rs 6.94 crore in the corresponding period last year. On a sequential basis, the company narrowed its losses by 43% from Rs 161.64 crore reported in the January-March quarter of 2026.
News & updates
- Medical logistics: Air India has signed an initial pact with SkyDrive, a global eVTOL (electric vertical take-off and landing) aircraft developer and manufacturer, and Suzuki Motor Corporation of Japan to conduct a joint feasibility study on the use of eVTOL aircraft for medical air logistics in India.
- Police case: The Hyderabad Cyber Crime police has registered two cases against some social media users and the Head of Meta in India, following a complaint by BJP activists over alleged objectionable content targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
- Vehicle probe: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration in the US has opened a preliminary investigation into about 1.2 million Tesla vehicles over reports of suspension failures that could cause a loss of  vehicle steering control.

articles.title: Envie d'un iPhone Pro sans attendre les 18 ? Amazon casse le prix du 17 Pro
articles.text:
L’iPhone 17 Pro occupe une place particulière dans la gamme Apple. Lancé en septembre 2025, il reprend l’ensemble des caractéristiques du Pro Max – puce A19 Pro, triple capteur 48 mégapixels, zoom tétraprisme 8x, dans un format plus compact de 6,3 pouces. Face au Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra ou au Google Pixel 10 Pro, il reste l’une des références du marché pour qui cherche un smartphone taillé pour la photo et la vidéo. Bonne nouvelle : il profite en ce moment d’une réduction de 200 euros sur Amazon.
Les atouts de l’Apple iPhone 17 Pro
- Son écran OLED 6,3 pouces ProMotion 120 Hz, 3 000 nits
- La puce A19 Pro gravée en 3 nm avec 12 Go de RAM
- Son triple capteur 48 mégapixels avec zoom tétraprisme 8x
Habituellement vendu 1 329 euros en 256 Go, l’iPhone 17 Pro est affiché à 1 129 euros sur Amazon. Soit 200 euros de moins que le tarif officiel Apple, ce qui en fait l’un des meilleurs prix relevés sur ce modèle depuis sa sortie.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant Apple iPhone 17 Pro. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Un châssis repensé et un écran taillé pour l’extérieur
Apple a changé de direction avec l’iPhone 17 Pro. Le dos en titane des 15 Pro et 16 Pro laisse place à un châssis unibody en aluminium forgé, associé à un panneau arrière en verre Ceramic Shield 2. Le résultat : un smartphone de 206 grammes qui tient bien en main malgré ses 8,8 mm d’épaisseur. Un choix assumé qui a permis d’intégrer une batterie plus généreuse et une chambre à vapeur pour la dissipation thermique.
L’écran Super Retina XDR de 6,3 pouces grimpe à 3 000 nits en pic de luminosité extérieure, ce qui le rend parfaitement lisible en plein soleil. La technologie ProMotion adapte la fréquence de 1 à 120 Hz selon le contenu affiché. Petit bémol : le châssis en aluminium a tendance à accrocher les micro-rayures au fil des semaines, un défaut que le titane de la génération précédente encaissait mieux.
A19 Pro, photo et autonomie : ce qu’il a dans le ventre
La puce A19 Pro gravée en 3 nm, épaulée par 12 Go de RAM, gère sans broncher la navigation quotidienne comme le montage vidéo 4K ou les tâches Apple Intelligence exécutées localement. Côté photo, le triple module 48 mégapixels est identique à celui du Pro Max. Le téléobjectif périscopique monte jusqu’à un zoom optique 4x, prolongé par un recadrage capteur qui atteint un équivalent 8x avec des résultats convaincants. L’autonomie progresse aussi : Apple annonce jusqu’à 31 heures de lecture vidéo, et les tests montrent un gain d’environ 1 h 30 par rapport à l’iPhone 16 Pro en usage continu. La journée complète ne pose aucun problème, même si le Pro Max reste devant sur ce terrain. La recharge filaire 40 W permet de récupérer 50 % en 20 minutes.
Plus d’informations vous attendent dans notre test de l’iPhone 17 Pro, où nous détaillons chacun des critères techniques de ce smartphone Apple.
Si vous hésitez encore entre les différents modèles de la marque, nous vous invitons à consulter notre guide des meilleurs iPhone du moment pour faire votre choix.
